OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Bounda.summary: Defines readings as families of finite laws on a finite outcome type, the record-determined property, triangular discrimination at a pair, least repeat cost, and goal propositions for the record pole, boundary zero set, adaptive protocol pole, order-one residue, Godel, diagonal tower, recursion and two-point bounds. Proves record-determined readings have zero discrimination at merged pairs, that merged pairs are exactly the common zero set of such readings, and that adaptive record-determined protocols gain zero terminal and limit information. Proves quantitative order-one cost bounds, the least-cost residue interval and a two-point decoder error lower bound. Proves Godel and content orientation poles with zero repeated information, one-reading side-symbol separations, diagonal stage and limit absence with preservation, and the combined recursion clause.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Bounda.boundary: At a merged pair every record-determined reading and every adaptive record-determined protocol has zero discrimination and zero terminal and limit information, while a distinguishing side symbol or counted coordinate outside the record restores one bit in one reading. With positive discrimination the information-cost tradeoff lies in the order-one residue interval between c log 2 and 4 log(1/(2 eta)) plus discrimination.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Bounda.conclusion: The merged boundary is exactly the common zero set of all record-determined readings, at which every such reading and adaptive protocol acquires zero discrimination and zero information while side information outside the record restores acquisition.
assumptions: Fintype Y for finite outcome types
Fintype A for finite action types
Fintype S and DecidableEq S for Godel side-symbol types
Nonempty T for the decreasing-measure part of the recursion clause
universe-polymorphic content type T : Type u
noncomputable section
classical reasoning to form the Boolean indicator decide (q z = q x0) in boundaryZeroSetGoal
hypotheses IsMergedPair, RecordDetermined, PairMenu, HistoryBank, positive discrimination, fair prior and unit cost where stated

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.Reading
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: A reading with finite outcomes Y is a function X -> FiniteLaw Y, assuming Fintype Y.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.RecordDetermined
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Given q : X -> Q and K : Reading X Y, K is record-determined by q if for all x x' with q x = q x' one has K x = K x'.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.readingDiscrimination
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The discrimination of K at x and x' is the real number discrimination (K x).mass (K x').mass, assuming Fintype Y.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.RecordPoleGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all X Q Y with Fintype Y, all q : X -> Q, all K : Reading X Y and all x0 x1, if RecordDetermined q K and IsMergedPair q x0 x1 then readingDiscrimination K x0 x1 = 0.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.BoundaryZeroSetGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all X Q, q : X -> Q and x0 x1, IsMergedPair q x0 x1 holds iff x0 != x1 and for every Y with Fintype Y and every K : Reading X Y with RecordDetermined q K one has readingDiscrimination K x0 x1 = 0, with no Fintype or DecidableEq hypothesis on Q.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.RecordProtocolPoleGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all X Q A Y with Fintype A and Fintype Y, all q : X -> Q, x0 x1, all p : FiniteProtocol Bool A Y and all K : List (A x Y) -> A -> Reading X Y, if IsMergedPair q x0 x1 and every K h a is record-determined and p.observation h a b = K h a (pairState x0 x1 b) for all h a b, then for every n and bank with HistoryBank n bank one has terminalMI p n bank = 0 and informationLimit p = 0.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.recordPoleGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Proves RecordPoleGoal: every record-determined reading has zero discrimination at every merged pair.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.boundaryZeroSetGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Proves BoundaryZeroSetGoal: merged pairs are exactly distinct pairs with zero discrimination for all record-determined readings; the converse uses the record-determined Boolean indicator reading with discrimination 2 at a split pair.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.recordProtocolPoleGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Proves RecordProtocolPoleGoal: under the merged-pair, record-determinedness and observation-equality hypotheses, terminal mutual information is zero at every history bank and the information limit is zero, whatever the cost.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.leastRepeatCost
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For finite Y and laws P Q and target c, the least repeat cost is sInf {N | c <= terminalMI (repeatProtocol P Q N) N (historyBank Unit Y N)}.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.PoleOrderOneGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all finite Y and P Q : FiniteLaw Y with 0 < discrimination P.mass Q.mass, every pair-menu protocol with menu value discrimination satisfies c * log 2 <= discrimination * expectedCost whenever c <= terminalMI, and for every eta with 0 < eta and eta <= 1/2 there exists N with 1 - binEntropy eta / log 2 <= terminalMI of the N-repeat and discrimination * N <= 4 * log (1/(2*eta)) + discrimination.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.poleOrderOneGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Proves PoleOrderOneGoal assuming positive discrimination, giving the finite-horizon lower residue bound and the repeat-target upper residue bound.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.PoleResidueGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all finite Y, P Q and eta with 0 < discrimination P.mass Q.mass, 0 < eta and eta <= 1/2, the product of discrimination with leastRepeatCost for target 1 - binEntropy eta / log 2 lies between (1 - binEntropy eta / log 2) * log 2 and 4 * log (1/(2*eta)) + discrimination.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.poleResidueGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Proves PoleResidueGoal: the nonempty attainment set bounds its least qualifying repeat horizon on both sides via the pair-menu cost bound and minimality of sInf.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.GodelPoleGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every finite Y and K : Reading Formula Y, if K is record-determined by Provable then readingDiscrimination at arithGodelSentence versus its negation is zero and every N-repeat has zero terminal information.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.godelPoleGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Proves GodelPoleGoal: the unprovable merged pair of the Godel sentence and its negation yields zero discrimination and zero repeated information.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.GodelSideSymbolGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every finite S with DecidableEq and s : Formula -> S, if s distinguishes the Godel sentence and its negation then 1 <= terminalMI of the 1-repeat deterministic-row protocol on historyBank Unit S 1.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.godelSideSymbolGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Proves GodelSideSymbolGoal: distinct deterministic side-symbol rows acquire one bit in one reading.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.DiagonalWalkGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all C V, E : C -> C -> V, j : V -> V and v0 with forall v, j v != v, for every n the transformed diagonal is represented by no code at stage n, the added code of the next stage reads the old diagonal, and every old evaluation is kept.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.diagonalWalkGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Proves DiagonalWalkGoal: each finite diagonal is absent, its old version is represented, and old rows persist.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.DiagonalUnionGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all C V, E : C -> C -> V, j : V -> V and v0 with forall v, j v != v, there is no code c with limitEval c x = j (limitEval x x) for all x.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.diagonalUnionGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Proves DiagonalUnionGoal: the union diagonal remains absent by the limit-evaluator theorem.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.OrientationPoleGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every content type T : Type u, every finite Y and K : Reading (T x Nat) Y, if K is record-determined by RecursorDecidability.content then for all R j k the discrimination at (R,j) versus (R,k) is zero and every N-repeat has zero terminal information.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.orientationPoleGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Proves OrientationPoleGoal: content-determined readings have zero discrimination at any two passes of the same content with zero repeated information.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.CounterSideSymbolGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every T : Type u, R : T and j k : Nat with j != k, the 1-repeat Boolean test row for decide (p.2 = j) at (R,j) versus (R,k) satisfies 1 <= terminalMI on historyBank Unit Bool 1.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.counterSideSymbolGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Proves CounterSideSymbolGoal: a test of the counted place coordinate separates distinct passes of the same content by a deterministic one-reading protocol.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.RecursionClauseGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Conjunction of OrientationPoleGoal and CounterSideSymbolGoal with: for every nonempty T : Type u and M : T x Nat -> Nat strictly decreasing along Pass, M is not content-determined; and for every n the left entropy of Fin (n+1) trivial carriers equals log (n+1).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.recursionClauseGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Proves RecursionClauseGoal from orientationPoleGoal, counterSideSymbolGoal, orienting_measure_not_content_determined and content_leaves_log.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.TwoPointGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all finite A Y, p : FiniteProtocol Bool A Y, delta with PairMenu p delta and 0 <= delta, decoder g : List (A x Y) -> Bool and n, if the prior is fair with mass 1/2 then log 2 - delta * expectedCost <= binEntropy of the decoder error mass sum over stoppedMass for negated g.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPole.twoPointGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Proves TwoPointGoal: every decoder of a discrimination-at-most-delta protocol about the fair label errs with mass e satisfying binEntropy e >= log 2 - delta times expected cost.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Bounda.summary: The file defines ε-indistinguishable rows and the two M6.14 obligations for discrimination and adaptive cost. A pointwise likelihood-ratio argument gives |a-b| ≤ tanh(ε/2)(a+b) and hence a per-row discrimination bound. Summation yields the discrimination goal with quadratic ε bound, and the pair-menu cost theorem yields the expected-cost lower bound.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Bounda.boundary: Rows with likelihood ratio bounded by exp ε have triangular discrimination at most 2 tanh(ε/2)^2, hence at most ε^2/2, which forces every adaptive stopped protocol to pay proportionally more expected cost for each bit.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Bounda.conclusion: Privacy with parameter ε limits discrimination quadratically and lower-bounds the expected cost of any adaptive protocol extracting given mutual information.
assumptions: Fintype Y A
0 ≤ ε for discrimination, 0 < ε for cost
FiniteLaw masses nonnegative summing to 1
1 ≤ protocol cost per reading

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPrivacy.IndistinguishableRows
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For parameter ε and functions P Q, IndistinguishableRows means for every y both P y ≤ exp ε * Q y and Q y ≤ exp ε * P y hold.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPrivacy.PrivacyDiscriminationGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every Fintype Y, finite laws P Q and 0 ≤ ε, indistinguishable rows imply discrimination is at most 2*tanh(ε/2)^2 and that bound is at most ε^2/2.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPrivacy.PrivacyCostGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every finite protocols with 0 < ε, indistinguishable rows at each history and unit cost at least 1, any bank and c below terminal mutual information satisfy c*log 2/(2*tanh(ε/2)^2) ≤ expected cost.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPrivacy.privacyDiscriminationGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The PrivacyDiscriminationGoal holds for all finite laws, proved from a pointwise tanh bound and tanh x ≤ x for x ≥ 0.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundaryPrivacy.privacyCostGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The PrivacyCostGoal holds for 0 < ε under indistinguishable rows and unit cost, by applying the adaptive pair-menu cost theorem with delta = 2*tanh(ε/2)^2.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Bounda.summary: The file defines the ciphertext law of a message under a key law and three secrecy goals. It proves that pointwise equal ciphertext laws have zero triangular discrimination. It proves the fair one-bit pad gives uniform ciphertext 1/2. It proves a decryptable perfectly secret cipher needs at least as many positive-mass keys as messages.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Bounda.boundary: Equal ciphertext rows sit at the discrimination-zero pole and yield no distinction, while distinct rows leave the pole; decryptable secrecy holds only when positive key support is at least message count, failing below that bound.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Bounda.conclusion: A decryptable perfectly secret cipher needs at least as many positively weighted keys as messages, with equal rows giving zero discrimination and the fair bit pad giving uniformity.
assumptions: Fintype K M C
DecidableEq C
noncomputable section
classical reasoning with Classical.choose for key selection
no sorry, axiom or native_decide visible

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundarySecrecy.cipherLaw
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For finite key type K, message type M, ciphertext type C with DecidableEq, key law, encryption enc and message m, cipherLaw is the sum over k of key.mass k when enc k m equals c and 0 otherwise.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundarySecrecy.PerfectSecrecyPoleGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all finite K C, all key laws, enc and messages m0 m1, if cipherLaw rows for m0 and m1 are pointwise equal then their discrimination is 0.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundarySecrecy.OneTimePadGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every key law on Bool with mass 1/2 on each key, for all m c the xor-pad ciphertext law equals 1/2.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundarySecrecy.ShannonKeyGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all finite K M C, key, enc, dec with dec k (enc k m) = m for all k m and with equal ciphertext rows for all messages, the card of M is at most the card of keys with positive mass.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundarySecrecy.perfectSecrecyPoleGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Pointwise equal ciphertext laws have zero triangular discrimination, proving PerfectSecrecyPoleGoal.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundarySecrecy.oneTimePadGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If the Bool key is fair then for each message and ciphertext exactly one key gives the required xor, so the ciphertext law is 1/2.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.BoundarySecrecy.shannonKeyGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If decryption succeeds for all keys and messages and ciphertext rows are equal, then messages inject via positive-mass keys into positive support, so card M is bounded by positive key support, with empty M by simp.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Bounda.summary: This file defines triangular discrimination of two finite rows and proves its basic properties: nonnegativity, vanishing exactly on equal rows, value 2 on distinct deterministic rows and 8 delta-squared for the binary symmetric kernel. It proves a single binary reading carries at most discrimination over log 2 bits, via a two-point entropy bound. It packages readings of discrimination at most delta into pair menus and conditional pair menus, proving finite-horizon and limit cost lower bounds c log 2 / delta and zero information at delta zero, summarized in boundary_singularity.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Bounda.boundary: Positive discrimination delta > 0 forces expected cost at least c log 2 / delta for c bits. At discrimination zero no information is acquired at any finite horizon or in the limit.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Bounda.conclusion: Pair readings of discrimination at most delta need cost at least c log 2 / delta for c bits at every horizon and in the limit, acquire nothing when delta is zero, and discrimination vanishes exactly on merged deterministic pairs.
assumptions: Fintype Y, A; DecidableEq Y for deterministic rows

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Bounda.conclusion: The core Boundary Theorem conjunction holds with each clause given its accepted proof.

IsMergedPair hypothesis where stated
universe polymorphism and Fintype hypotheses for fiber clause

It proves the reading is record-determined and has discrimination two exactly on split pairs. It proves merged pairs are exactly distinct states with zero discrimination for all finite-output record-determined readings, in two descriptions and with a natural-number control.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Bounda.conclusion: Without any finiteness on records, being merged is exactly having zero discrimination for all record-determined finite readings.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Checke.summary: The file builds two validating interpretations for arithmetic checkers. A projection reading of addition and multiplication validates the base checker with induction but falsifies a true closed equation. A negation-asymmetric valuation validates the repaired equality checker with induction but falsifies a true negated equation. Each yields soundness plus a concrete unprovable true sentence.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Checke.boundary: Each checker is sound for its validating interpretation yet misses a true sentence, so truth outruns provability in both the base and the repaired equality checkers.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Checke.conclusion: The base checker misses a true closed equation and the repaired checker misses a true negated equation, each witnessed by a validating interpretation.
assumptions: classical logic via Classical.not_not.mp for double negation
closed terms for substitution lemmas
first-order arithmetic language with induction

It defines termination as accessibility in the reverse relation, plus immediate subterms and descent as reduct-or-subterm. It closes termination under every constructor, shows descent is well founded below terminating traces, handles the recursor by descent on its counter, and concludes every trace terminates with no weight or ordering parameter.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Demand.summary: The file develops finite-constraint completion with compact witnesses and closed acceptance sets, finite-agreement closure, and conservative diagonal self-extension. It proves compact closed models lift finite goodness to global goodness with finite minimal certificates for failure, and exhibits the threshold problem as finitely good but globally bad with no finite obstruction. It builds one-code, staged and directed-union extensions that preserve old tables while missing their own changed diagonals at every stage and in the limit. It derives the source-contract core goal with finite obstruction, licensed coloring, repair soundness, compact completion with budget transport and diagonal exclusion, and specializes it to readout sources with finite retained coloring and empty zero-color endpoint.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Demand.boundary: With compact witnesses and closed acceptance sets finite success lifts to global success and global failure has a finite certificate, while the threshold shows finite goodness without global goodness when compactness is absent. Every fixed-point-free diagonal extension misses its own diagonal at each finite stage and in the directed-union limit.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Demand.conclusion: From one source contract all finite, licensed, compact, cost and diagonal conclusions follow, while compact-closed hypotheses are sharp and every diagonal extension misses its own diagonal even in the limit.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Demand.summary: The file defines demand problems with witnesses, goodness, minimal bad obstructions, selectors, colorings, repair menus, combiners and least alphabets in extended naturals. It proves finite obstructions characterize failure and that selection coincides with obstruction coloring, finitely and with licenses, with sound repair assembly. It provides executable finite tables with replayable witness or minimal-obstruction certificates and licensed search with exhaustive replay. It proves the licensed selector criterion that least feasible and least coloring alphabets coincide with top for impossibility, illustrated by triple and denied-permission examples.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Demand.boundary: A demand set is good exactly when it contains no minimal bad obstruction, and licensed feasibility coincides with licensed coloring on finite retained sets. Without permission or candidates the least alphabet is top, while the permission-free chromatic number can be finite, as triple needs two and denied permission needs top versus one.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Demand.conclusion: For one menu and finite retained set the least feasible selector alphabet equals the least licensed coloring alphabet in extended naturals, with top for impossibility and finite values as least succeeding sizes.
assumptions: Finite and Fintype carriers where stated
DecidableEq for enumeration
Classical choice for minimal bad and selection
noncomputable leastFinite and leastAlphabet

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Demand.summary: The file builds native SourceContract instances for counted-recursion, evaluated-code, stochastic-support, common-law and affine adapters, plus bounded-halting sources encoding halting at input zero and variants testing omitted premises and selector licenses. It proves each instance satisfies its native problem equation, combiner law and the source-indexed core, and it isolates exact obstructions: content blindness, paired diagonal exclusion, same-support different laws and posteriors, triangle global obstruction with minimal badness, affine negation failure, threshold finite-versus-global split, and Shannon information not preserved by incidence isomorphism. It reduces halting to source feasibility to show no computable total boundary and obstruction detector exists and no fixed-budget evaluation record classifies all successes.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Demand.boundary: Computable detectors cannot separate feasible from obstructed represented sources, and fixed-budget evaluation records cannot separate success from failure at the same input. Finite demand families can be locally realizable while the global family is obstructed, and incidence isomorphism preserves feasibility but not Shannon information.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Demand.conclusion: No computable total detector decides global source obstruction across the explicit bounded-halting family, and no fixed-budget record, even noncomputably classified, determines semantic success.
assumptions: Fintype A for common-law sources; Fintype Y, Z for stochastic instruments
Field K, AddCommGroup V and Module K V for affine equation sources
Classical.choice via Classical.choose and classical tactic in separating-inputs proof; file header notes axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound
set_option autoImplicit false; no sorry, axiom or native_decide visible in code

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Demand.summary: The file defines demand isomorphisms pairing demand and witness bijections with a satisfaction equivalence, and conservative embeddings with one-way preservation. It proves isomorphisms transport witnesses, goodness, minimal bad sets, selectors, repair menus, budgets and whole licensed plans. It instantiates the framework for support, experiment, affine-equation, common-law and instrument problems, including a row-shear example where global solutions agree but singleton restrictions diverge.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Demand.boundary: Feasibility, selectors and licensed plans transport across two-sided demand isomorphisms, but equality of feasible demand sets does not supply a witness isomorphism and a one-way conservative embedding does not reimport new solutions without an explicit return map; globally equivalent equation vectors can still disagree on restricted rows.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Demand.conclusion: Demand isomorphisms preserve the whole feasibility, selector, licensed-plan and budget structure, while profile equality alone and one-way embeddings do not recover witnesses.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Determ.summary: Defines conflict adjacency for deterministic readings, fibers, fiber graphs and target classes, and the largest fiber. Proves two inputs conflict exactly when they share a record but differ in target, that distinct fibers never conflict, and that each fiber graph is complete multipartite and isomorphic to the multipartite graph on its target classes. Proves the whole conflict graph is the supremum of its fiber graphs. Proves the chromatic number and the least side-alphabet size for zero-error decoding equal the largest number of target values on a fiber, and for the identity target all equal the largest fiber, which is also the least place-coordinate size.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Determ.boundary: An n-symbol side record admits a zero-error decoder exactly when n is at least the largest number of target values on a fiber, so fewer symbols fail on some fiber while enough symbols succeed.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Determ.conclusion: On a finite input set the least side-alphabet size and the chromatic number and the least place-coordinate size all equal the largest fiber.
assumptions: Fintype X
Fintype Y
DecidableEq X
DecidableEq Y
DecidableEq V
Nonempty X for the decoder-place equivalence

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Given [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y], the conflict graph equals the supremum over y of the mapped fiber graphs.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Diagon.summary: The file defines representability of predicates by object codes and the diagonal predicate flipping self-application. It proves a fixed-point-free output change makes the diagonal unrepresented and the evaluator non-surjective, with Boolean negation as the concrete instance. It shows no internal self-evaluation code or complete same-carrier observer exists, while external function records read every predicate but cannot be quoted back.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Diagon.boundary: Predicates representable by internal codes stop at the diagonal: a fixed-point-free output change yields an unrepresented diagonal, while external function records read every predicate but cannot be quoted back internally.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Diagon.conclusion: No object-coded total evaluator enumerates all predicates when the output admits a fixed-point-free operation, and no internal exact self-evaluation code exists under negation closure.
assumptions: DecidableEq C for fixed-pair separation

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Discri.summary: The file bounds triangular discrimination by total variation above and below and computes pointwise limits to point masses. It proves merged limits give discrimination zero with divergent information cost while split limits give two. It defines the extended information price as infinite at zero discrimination for positive targets and proves finite-horizon and limit cost lower bounds, closing with discrimination two exactly for disjoint supports and zero-error decodability.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Discri.boundary: Merged deterministic limits have discrimination tending to zero with divergent positive information price, while split limits have discrimination tending to two; a positive target has infinite extended price exactly at zero discrimination.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Discri.conclusion: Discrimination is two exactly for disjointly supported laws, which is exactly when a zero-error decoder exists, with merged limits at zero and split limits at two driving infinite extended price at the boundary.
assumptions: Fintype and DecidableEq for pointwise limits
Filter.atTop and nhds topology for convergence
ENNReal arithmetic for extended prices
nonnegative and unit-sum hypotheses for laws

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Distin.summary: This file factors the dynamical distinction boundary functor as a licensed reduction morphism into a verdict carrier with equality steps. It proves the canonical five-factor composite equals the morphism and that the kernel identifies every two traces, merging void and delta void, with subsingleton quotient and singleton image. It proves the verdict map is not injective and exhibits the quotient-to-image isomorphism between one-class dynamics and one-verdict dynamics.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Distin.boundary: Any two distinct traces are identified by the kernel; separation fails everywhere, with void and delta void as an explicit merged pair witnessing nonfaithfulness.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Distin.conclusion: The distinction morphism collapses all traces to a single verdict, factoring through a one-class kernel quotient isomorphic to its one-point image.
assumptions: Quot.sound for quotient equality
Noncomputable verdict and morphism definitions
No sorry, admit, axiom, native_decide; kernel-only as stated

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Dynami.summary: The file defines the k-step return and the Bellman value for stopping now or stepping once with cost. It proves the value bounds every permitted stopping time, is attained, is horizon-monotone, and equals immediate payoff under step bounds or preserved payoff with nonnegative costs. A three-stage delayed-revelation example shows zero first-step gain with a strictly valuable two-step continuation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Dynami.boundary: Stopping now versus continuing is decided by comparing current payoff to the full remaining Bellman value; zero immediate record gain does not imply stopping, since a two-step continuation can still exceed the immediate payoff after costs.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Dynami.conclusion: The Bellman value bounds every permitted stopping time and is attained, with a three-stage example where waiting two steps beats stopping despite no first-step gain.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Equali.summary: Defines five equality schemes for arbitrary terms, the extended axiom predicate and checker T_E, and provability in T_E. Proves every T_0 proof is a T_E proof and that every T_E axiom is true on N, hence T_E is sound on N and consistent. Develops congruence and Robinson numeral lemmas to prove every closed term is T_E provably equal to the numeral of its value. Concludes closed equations are T_E provable exactly when true on N, with the true equation S(S 0 plus 0) equals S S 0 as a repaired example.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Equali.boundary: For closed terms T_E proves an equation exactly when it is true on N, while T_0 leaves the true equation S(S 0 plus 0) equals S S 0 unprovable. Soundness implies falsum is not provable, so consistency holds.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Equali.conclusion: For closed terms T_E proves an equation exactly when the two sides have equal values on N.
assumptions: isClosedTerm hypotheses for closed-term results
no sorry or axiom or native_decide visible in the code

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Equali.summary: Defines code templates for the five equality schemes, Boolean recognizers on codes, canonical recognizers for term, formula and proof codes that check pairings at every node, the numeric checker for T_E, and the Boolean proof relation. Proves the code recognizers agree with the symbolic predicates on canonical codes and that canonical recognizers accept exactly the canonical codes. Proves each recognizer and the numeric checker primitive recursive by course-of-values steps. Proves the proof relation is primitive recursive and that existence of a code related to the code of phi holds exactly when T_E proves phi.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Equali.boundary: A number is accepted by the canonical recognizers exactly when it pairs correctly at every node and is the code of a term, formula or proof. Remaining numbers are rejected, so provability is defined by canonical proof codes.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Equali.conclusion: The Boolean relation proofRelE is primitive recursive and holds for some code of a formula exactly when T_E proves that formula.
assumptions: Primcodable instances for codes
pairing function cpair is not onto so non-canonical numbers exist
course-of-values recursion for recognizers and checker
no sorry or axiom visible in the code

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Equali.summary: Applies the incompleteness theorem for sound primitive recursive proof predicates to the proof relation of T_E to obtain a sentence gamma_E true on N exactly when unprovable, with neither it nor its negation provable. Packages extension, primitive recursiveness, definability, soundness, closed-equation completeness and incompleteness into a single conjunction. Defines the provability record, proves its collision with truth at gamma_E and its negation, the side-symbol criterion, representability of provability, and a second consistency collision under the formalized first theorem. Proves a corollary collecting collisions, maximal licensed singletons with no greatest licensed set, the swap stabilizer, and the one-bit fair label.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Equali.boundary: The provability record agrees with standard truth except at gamma_E versus its negation and at the consistency sentence versus its negation, which are true but unprovable collisions. No licensed set can contain both sides of a collision, giving two maximal licensed singletons and no greatest licensed set.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Equali.conclusion: The repaired checker has a true sentence that is unprovable with unprovable negation giving collisions of its provability record with truth.
assumptions: Classical.choose for the Goedel sentence gammaE
Primrec2 proofRelE and soundness of T_E on N
formalized first-theorem hypothesis ProvableE (not (Bew falsum) implies gammaE) for the consistency collision

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Erasur.summary: The file proves zero-error finite-cost recovery under every positive binary prior is equivalent to both strict exclusive-output supports. It computes geometric survival, normalization, entropy and exact weighted cost for first-exclusive stopping. It cuts any adaptive protocol at its first decisive output to prove a universal reciprocal lower bound with first-exclusive optimality, and shows shared outputs force a common undecided history so no finite horizon suffices.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Erasur.boundary: Zero-error finite-cost recovery under every positive prior holds exactly when both exclusive-output supports exist; with a shared output no finite horizon suffices and every adaptive protocol must continue on a common undecided history.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Erasur.conclusion: Stopping at the first exclusive output is exactly optimal: it attains the universal weighted-reciprocal minimum whenever both exclusive supports exist.
assumptions: Fintype Y A for protocols and laws
arbitrary normalized strictly positive binary prior for the exact equivalence
unit cost per reading for optimality and lower bounds
fixed conditional rows PairResolution.row P Q

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Erasur.summary: Defines the binary erasure row with keep mass p and erasure mass 1-p and the finite-horizon repeated-reading laws and the first-definite stopping protocol that halts at the first non-erased symbol with unit cost. Shows every fixed horizon leaves a common all-erasure transcript with positive mass under both labels, so every decoder errs on some label. Shows the first-definite protocol stops with probability one, has zero decoding error, attains one bit of information, and has extended cost 1/p. Generalizes to arbitrary finite-alphabet rows via exclusive mass and first-exclusive stopping, and proves zero-error finite-cost recovery with fair prior and unit costs holds precisely when each row charges an output the other excludes, with no such protocol under nested supports.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Erasur.boundary: At any fixed finite horizon the all-erasure transcript is shared with positive mass, so zero error is impossible. With stopping at the first definite output zero error is achieved at finite expected cost 1/p, and in general zero-error finite cost holds when each row has exclusive mass and fails when one support contains the other.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Erasur.conclusion: For erasure rows with 0 < p < 1 the first-definite protocol recovers the label with zero error at extended cost 1/p, and for general rows zero-error finite-cost recovery with fair prior and unit costs holds if and only if each row has positive exclusive mass.
assumptions: finite observation alphabet
fair binary prior
unit cost per reading
classical tactic for finite sums

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ErasureReading.erasure_fixed_horizon_ambiguous

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ErasureReading.firstDefinite
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For 0 < p < 1, the unit-cost protocol with fair prior, unit actions, erasure observations, stopping when a definite true or false report appears, and cost one.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ErasureReading.firstDefinite_stops

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ErasureReading.firstDefinite_zero_error

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ErasureReading.firstDefinite_information

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ErasureReading.firstDefinite_expected_cost

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ErasureReading.erasure_fixed_horizon_positive_error
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For 0 < p < 1 and n, each label has likelihood (1-p)^n on the all-erasure history which is positive, and every decoder errs on some label with positive stopped mass.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ErasureReading.erasure_stop_zero_error

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ErasureReading.erasure_expected_cost_eq_inv

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ErasureReading.atLabel

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ErasureReading.labelCost

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/FairRe.summary: The file proves a fair binary label carries at most half the triangular discrimination in bits, with distinct deterministic outputs attaining one bit at discrimination two. It develops a binary Pinsker inequality via a monotone gap to give lower bounds through discrimination and total variation. It combines them into a four-part chain for one fair reading. It concludes one fair reading is informative when discrimination is positive, which holds when the two rows differ.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/FairRe.boundary: Fair information lies between discrimination lower bounds and half discrimination above; it is positive when rows differ and zero when rows agree.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/FairRe.conclusion: One fair reading is informative when its two rows differ, with two-sided Pinsker bounds recorded in fair_reading_pinsker.
assumptions: Fintype Y
nonnegative kernel rows 0 ≤ K b y
normalized rows sum to 1
0 < Real.log 2

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FairReadingBound.fair_information_le_half_discrimination
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If rows are nonnegative and sum to 1 then jointMI of the fair prior with K is at most discrimination (K true) (K false) / 2.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FairReadingBound.fair_bound_attained_split
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If y0 differs from y1 then the split point-mass kernel has jointMI 1 and discrimination 2.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If 0 ≤ t and t < 1 then 2 * t ≤ log (1 + t) - log (1 - t).

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: pinskerGap t is -(negMulLog (1 + t) + negMulLog (1 - t)) / 2 - t^2 / 2.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: pinskerGap is monotone on Icc 0 1.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FairReadingBound.log_two_sub_binEntropy_eq
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all s, log 2 - binEntropy ((1 + s) / 2) equals -(negMulLog (1 + s) + negMulLog (1 - s)) / 2.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FairReadingBound.sq_div_two_le_log_two_sub_binEntropy
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If |t| ≤ 1 then t^2 / 2 ≤ log 2 - binEntropy ((1 + t) / 2).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FairReadingBound.fair_information_ge_quarter_discrimination
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If rows are nonnegative and sum to 1 then discrimination / (4 * log 2) ≤ jointMI of the fair label.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FairReadingBound.totalVariation
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: totalVariation P Q is (sum |P y - Q y|) / 2.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FairReadingBound.half_discrimination_le_totalVariation
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If P and Q are nonnegative then discrimination P Q / 2 ≤ totalVariation P Q.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FairReadingBound.totalVariation_sq_le_half_discrimination
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If P Q are nonnegative with sums 1 then totalVariation P Q ^ 2 ≤ discrimination P Q / 2.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FairReadingBound.fair_information_ge_totalVariation_sq
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If rows are nonnegative and sum to 1 then totalVariation^2 / (2 * log 2) ≤ jointMI of the fair label.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FairReadingBound.discrimination_sq_le_totalVariation_sq
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If P Q nonnegative then discrimination^2 / (8 * log 2) ≤ totalVariation^2 / (2 * log 2).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FairReadingBound.fair_reading_pinsker
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Under nonnegative normalized rows, discrimination^2/(8 log 2) ≤ TV^2/(2 log 2) ≤ I, discrimination/(4 log 2) ≤ I, and I ≤ discrimination/2.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Under nonnegative normalized rows, 0 < jointMI of the fair label holds if and only if 0 < discrimination holds.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/FiberR.summary: The file declares exact M6.5 goals for n-ary fiber resolution and defines repeated fiber readings, likelihoods, error mass, sparse rows and per-state errors. It proves a one-reading pairwise discrimination bound, the resulting local capacity bound, maximum-likelihood attainment with Bhattacharyya exponent, sparse control with bounded discrimination but unbounded information, Fano's inequality on the stopped law, and exponential per-state and uniform resolution horizons.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/FiberR.boundary: Zero-error finite-cost n-ary reading exists exactly when each pair of rows has mutually exclusive outputs. Under nested supports every zero-error protocol has infinite extended cost, while positive minimum discrimination yields exponential error decay and an explicit finite resolution horizon.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/FiberR.conclusion: An n-ary fiber admits zero-error finite-cost reading exactly under mutual exclusive outputs, with one-reading capacity, attainment, Fano and exponential resolution bounds proved.
assumptions: Fintype instances for Fin n, A and Y
uniform prior p0.mass b = 1/n where assumed
maximum-likelihood decoder hypothesis fiberLikelihood K b h <= fiberLikelihood K (g h) h where assumed
pairwise Bhattacharyya or discrimination bounds where assumed
unit or bounded reading cost where assumed
classical reasoning
no sorry, axiom or native_decide in code

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Every n-ary one-reading joint information is bounded by the prior-weighted pairwise discrimination sum divided by 2*Real.log 2.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FiberResolution.FiberFanoGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Under uniform prior with 2 <= n and bounded error, logb 2 n minus the Fano term of the error is at most the terminal information of the repeated reading.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FiberResolution.fiberAttainment
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Proves the FiberAttainmentGoal: under uniform prior, pairwise Bhattacharyya bound beta and maximum-likelihood decoder, the stopped error is at most (n-1)*beta^N.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FiberResolution.fiberStateError_le_exp

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FiberResolution.fiberMaxError_le_exp

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/FiberS.summary: Defines when a measure orients a relation into a strict order and the record image of a relation under an observer. Proves a measure determined by the observer falls at no fiber step, orients only outside fibers, and orients into a well-founded order with well-founded record image, with the converse via the record itself. Shows the record image is well founded holds precisely when some determined measure into a well-founded order orients the relation. Instantiates the lemma to counted passes, which stay in content fibers, and to the payload-lowering step, which stays in counter fibers, blocking determined orienting measures while the other projection orients.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/FiberS.boundary: A determined measure can fall at a step that leaves its fiber, and never at a step inside a fiber. Orientation by a determined measure into a well-founded order holds when the record image is well founded and fails otherwise.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/FiberS.conclusion: A determined measure orients a relation into a well-founded order if and only if the record image is well founded, so content-determined measures cannot orient counted passes and counter-determined measures cannot orient the payload step.
assumptions: irreflexive order
Determines q M
WellFounded lt
Nonempty T for pass instance
no sorry, axiom or native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Fisher.summary: Defines Fisher information for finite parametric families and pointwise twice differentiability, with C^2 implying the pointwise notion but not conversely. Proves second-order Taylor with Peano remainder and triangular-discrimination expansions with cubic big-O error under twice differentiability and little-o error under once differentiability. Exhibits the Bernoulli Fisher value 4 and a quadratic law with zero Fisher but quadratic support-boundary discrimination. Derives local quadratic bands and conditional information, cost, budget and reciprocal bounds for protocols limited by discrimination.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Fisher.boundary: When all masses at θ are positive and coordinates are differentiable at θ, discrimination equals half the Fisher information times (t-θ)^2 up to o((t-θ)^2). When a mass vanishes at θ, Fisher information can be zero while discrimination retains at least the new-support mass, so the interior quadratic law fails at the support boundary.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Fisher.conclusion: Under positive support and pointwise differentiability, triangular discrimination is locally half the Fisher information times squared displacement with matching two-sided band and conditional information and cost bounds, while vanishing support mass breaks Fisher control as the quadratic law shows.
assumptions: Fintype Y for finite families
positive masses 0 < P θ y at base parameter
DifferentiableAt / TwiceDifferentiableAt / ContDiff ℝ 2 per coordinate
0 < ε for local bands
No sorry, axiom, native_decide or classical choice in file

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Forced.summary: Defines the forced-output emission episode on a certificate tower, with definite verdicts or refusal as records and direct whole-term certificates as the distinction. Proves licensed soundness and object-witnessedness, that a licensed definite verdict requires a direct certificate, and that channel echo states coincide with orientation-boundary states. Proves at boundary states every licensed record is refusal and every raw definite verdict has false formal legitimacy, and that every output falls into one of three forced cases.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Forced.boundary: A definite verdict is licensed where a direct whole-term certificate exists, and at orientation-boundary states without such a certificate licensed output collapses to refusal while raw definite verdicts lack formal legitimacy.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Forced.conclusion: Echo states of the forced-output channel are the orientation-boundary states, where licensed output collapses to refusal.
assumptions: step-duplicating schema
certificate tower
two-point object coordinate
no sorry, axiom or native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/FourTe.summary: This file defines tables of disagreement rates, cycle inequalities, observers via shared records and vectors via unit vectors with prescribed inner products. It proves observer tables satisfy eight cycle inequalities and score at most 2, with score expressed via refused weights and a one-symbol-two-bits count. It proves observers yield vectors, vectors are equivalent to angle cycle inequalities and to PSD completions with unit diagonal, with quadratic bound, score at most 2 sqrt 2 and bits at most 1, witnessed by the extreme table and refuted by the corner table.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/FourTe.boundary: Tables with an observer satisfy score at most 2 while the extreme table attains 2 sqrt 2 with vectors but no observer. Tables with vectors satisfy score at most 2 sqrt 2 while the corner table attains 4 with neither vectors nor observer.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/FourTe.conclusion: Observer tables satisfy cycle inequalities with score at most 2, vector tables are characterized by angle cycles and PSD completions with score at most 2 sqrt 2 and at most one bit, both bounds sharp and the score-4 table admits neither.
assumptions: Rates in [0,1] for the vectors-iff-angle-cycle direction
Finite shared records with weights summing to 1 for observers
Euclidean-space unit vectors for HasVectors
No sorry, admit, axiom, native_decide; kernel-only as stated

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Gaussi.summary: Builds joint laws by convolving independent standard normals along finitely many vectors, covering Dirac and singular cases. Computes projections, means, variances and covariances from the construction and shows covariance on one finite measure is positive semidefinite. Proves PSD matrices are exactly centered Gaussian covariances and that vector tables are exactly those with a common Gaussian law and with prescribed Gaussian pair marginals.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Gaussi.boundary: A rate table admits a common centered Gaussian law and prescribed Gaussian pair marginals exactly when it has vectors, hence a PSD completion. Without vectors no common law with the required second moments exists, Gaussian or otherwise, while singular covariances need no exception.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Gaussi.conclusion: Vector tables are exactly those admitting a common centered Gaussian law and prescribed Gaussian pair marginals, with covariance uniquely determining the Gaussian measure.
assumptions: Second-countable Borel Euclidean codomain for Gaussian sums
IsGaussian and IsFiniteMeasure with MemLp 2 for moments
Correlation bound |r| at most 1 and rates in [0,1] for equivalences
No sorry, axiom or native_decide; singular and zero covariance allowed

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/GodelP.summary: Defines the checker-undecided pair of the Gödel sentence and its negation. Proves the augmented provability observer licenses standard-model truth on that pair exactly when the side map distinguishes the two sentences. Packages this criterion with the provability collision, maximal refusals without a greatest licensed set, and a provability-preserving transposition.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/GodelP.boundary: The augmented provability observer licenses standard-model truth on the two Gödel sentences exactly when the side coordinate takes distinct values on them. With equal side values the provability collision forces refusal, so licensing holds on the distinguishing side and fails on the identifying side.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/GodelP.conclusion: Side-distinguishing is exactly the extra observation needed to license truth on the Gödel pair, packaged with its collision, maximal refusals and stabilizing transposition.
assumptions: Provability observer and truth target from imported collision theory

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/GroupO.summary: Defines uniform keys on finite nonempty types with left-additive encryption and left-subtraction decryption. Proves decryption inverts encryption, ciphertext mass is uniform and message-independent, and two message laws have zero triangular discrimination. Shows positive-key count equals cardinality and the pad attains the key bound, with the two-element group as half-mass instance.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/GroupO.boundary: With a uniform key covering the whole group, ciphertext laws are message-independent with zero triangular discrimination. The uniform pad decrypts correctly and attains the positive-key cardinality bound, marking the limit where secrecy and correctness meet key size.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/GroupO.conclusion: Left-additive uniform group pads decrypt correctly, conceal messages perfectly with zero discrimination, and attain the Shannon positive-key bound.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Haltin.summary: The file studies protocols that observe halting codes only through a bounded-record entry at fixed budget. It shows the shared empty entry gives zero discrimination, the fair prior carries one bit, and therefore at every budget there is a halt-loop pair with zero acquired information at every horizon and in the limit, leaving a one-bit terminal gap.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Haltin.boundary: Protocols confined to bounded records cannot distinguish a halting code from a diverging code sharing the same empty entry, so the one-bit terminal gap persists; a resolving channel outside the bounded records can close it.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Haltin.conclusion: At every budget there are halting and diverging codes whose bounded-record protocols acquire zero information and leave a one-bit terminal gap at every horizon and in the limit.
assumptions: Finite types A and Y for actions and observations

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instan.summary: The file defines occurrences as pairs of a Trace term and a Fin 2 argument place for eqW, with projections to content and place and the two canonical occurrences of eqW a a. It proves the two occurrences share content but differ in place, forming a merged pair for the content observer, while a Boolean place test separates them. It then proves the full root Step rules: the reflexive rule yields void exactly when contents are equal, and the difference rule fires unconditionally, so both reducts are available on eqW a a. It closes with a bundled statement and preserves two historical merged-pair theorems for void and unit occurrences.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instan.boundary: The content projection merges the two argument occurrences with identical content, while the finite place reading separates them. The reflexive root rule holds exactly on content equality, whereas the difference root rule has no side condition and fires even on equal contents.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instan.conclusion: Every term yields a merged pair of occurrences with identical content but distinct places on which both full root equality rules fire.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instan.summary: The file studies the kernel rewriting relations Step, the guarded EqGuardedStep and contextual StepCtxFull on Trace. It characterizes the reflexive and difference rules for eqW, counts nodes to isolate void as the unique one-node term, and enumerates the four contextual reducts and two normal forms of eqW void void. It develops numerals, spines, descents and frame copies to unroll the recursor, and models the observation O with its zero, successor and unrolling laws. It ends with blindness of the content observer to the zero test, separation behavior of that test, and merged step copies.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instan.boundary: The content observer cannot determine the counter-zero test though the counter observer can, and the guarded difference rule applies only to distinct arguments while the unguarded rule applies to all. Of the four contextual reducts of eqW void void, only void and the empty frame are normal forms.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instan.conclusion: The contextual reducts of eqW void void are exactly four terms with two normal forms, and the recursor observation unrolls to a spine while its content observer cannot determine the zero test.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instan.summary: The file isolates the root-step recursor theory: the generic pass accompanies the root step, the positive-counter reduct is unique, and the recursor returns its content in one root step exactly at counter zero with a decidable test. It also isolates a Trace-specific deterministic counter protocol that separates distinct counters, and a demand-transport adapter where content readout and content orientation have no good solution while the counter zero test does and eventual termination holds with content blindness. It closes by restating the one-step return and a finite pigeonhole equivalence for coordinate maps.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instan.boundary: Content-only readout cannot decide the zero test or orient passes by content, though the counter zero test is realizable and every pass sequence terminates at zero. The one-step return holds exactly at counter zero, so termination does not imply content observability.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instan.conclusion: The recursor returns in one root step exactly at counter zero, yet no content-only readout or orientation is good though termination holds and the counter test is good.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instru.summary: Defines joint channels and adaptive sequential composition retaining both outcomes while summing the intermediate state, plus deterministic embeddings. Proves support characterization of recoverability, composition and decomposition of restoration, associativity, and preservation of first-outcome laws and equalities. Shows conflicts and side-information budgets persist forward and are exactly preserved under recoverable continuations, with keep-then-erase strictly adding a conflict.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instru.boundary: Joint support separated across initial states is exactly restorable, while overlapping support is not. Recoverable continuations preserve conflict graphs and chromatic side-information cost, whereas the keep-then-erase composite strictly adds a conflict, so the recovery hypothesis cannot be dropped.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instru.conclusion: Adaptive composition preserves restoration and target-relative side information exactly under recoverable continuations and otherwise can strictly increase conflicts as erasure shows.
assumptions: Finite outcome and post-state types with Fintype
Nonempty initial or target types where restoration or decoding is stated
Normalized stochastic kernels summing to 1

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instru.summary: The file defines a fair binary label over two input states and its joint, record-marginal, uncertainty, read, erased and retained quantities for finite stochastic instruments. It proves the three parts sum to one bit, each lies in [0,1], and adaptive continuation cannot reduce erasure. It corrects erasure by initial ambiguity to intrinsic loss and characterizes zero intrinsic loss as pair and global recoverability.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instru.boundary: One fair bit separates readable, retained and erased amounts; deterministic joint collision gives one erased bit while separation gives zero, and adaptive continuation can increase but never decrease erased information.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instru.conclusion: Read, retained and erased parts plus initial ambiguity partition one fair bit in [0,1], erasure is monotone under continuation, and zero intrinsic loss characterizes pair recoverability.
assumptions: Fintype R, Fintype T
normalized stochastic weights with total 1
classical reasoning in finite case splits

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instru.summary: This file defines deterministic instruments with read and post maps, joint output and recoverability, characterizing recovery by joint injectivity and its behavior under composition with collision persistence. It exhibits silent-keep versus silent-erase and read-and-erase showing equal records can differ on recovery and retained records can reverse reset. It defines stochastic instruments with outcome and state laws and positive-support recovery, exhibiting random reads where keeping recovers and erasing does not despite identical outcome laws.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instru.boundary: Recoverable instruments are exactly those with injective joint output. Equal outcome records can still differ on recoverability, and equal outcome laws can hide different state changes.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Instru.conclusion: Recovery needs the full joint outcome; outcome records or laws alone do not determine recoverability or state change.
assumptions: Nonempty X for recoverable-iff-injective
Fintype Y Z for stochastic instruments
Classical.choose and Classical.choice used to build restore map
No sorry, axiom, native_decide visible

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Kalman.summary: The file defines the unobservable subspace as the intersection of kernels of all iterates, its behavioral record, finite stacked map, and quotient action and record. It proves the unobservable is the largest invariant subspace in the record kernel and equals the first finrank-many kernels. It identifies future equality with unobservable difference and gives swap and identity examples.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Kalman.boundary: Vanishing versus nonvanishing unobservable subspace separates injective behavioral records from confounded ones; full rank of the finite stacked map is the finite test.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Kalman.conclusion: The infinite-horizon unobservable subspace equals the first finrank-many kernels, is the largest invariant subspace in the record kernel, and its quotient is the universal minimal stable observer.
assumptions: Field K
modules over K
FiniteDimensional K V for finite criteria
Cayley-Hamilton via charpoly

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Kalman.summary: The file rewrites Kalman behavioral equality, merged pairs and record-preserving translations as unobservable or stacked-kernel differences. It proves no merges exactly when the stacked map has full rank. It shows every projection onto the unobservable or stacked kernel resolves all merged pairs and such a projection exists, with an explicit two-point merged example.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Kalman.boundary: Empty versus nonempty merged-pair boundary separates full-rank stacked maps from rank-deficient ones; a projection onto the kernel resolves exactly the merged states.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Kalman.conclusion: Record equality, merged pairs and record-preserving translations are exactly unobservable or stacked-kernel differences, absence of merges is full rank, and kernel projections resolve all merges.
assumptions: Field K
modules over K
FiniteDimensional K V for stacked criteria
existence of linear complements for projection

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Kernel.summary: The file keeps the exact Goedel sentence, its negation and the provability observer with unconditional incompleteness assumptions. OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Kernel.boundary: Provable versus unprovable separates the two sentences merged under provability; a side symbol resolves them iff it takes two values on the pair.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Kernel.conclusion: The Goedel sentence and its negation are distinct yet provability-equal, resolvable by a side symbol iff it distinguishes them and by restriction iff it omits one.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Merged.summary: The file defines when an observer determines a target, what a merged pair is, and the boundary as the set of merged pairs. It proves Lemma 2.3 on determination via collisions, invariance and orbits, and Proposition 2.4 on transitive closures and apartness. It then proves the clauses of Theorem 4.1 on tests, invariant relations, side symbols, restrictions and comparison decoders, with Corollary 4.2 and Propositions 4.7 and 4.8.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Merged.boundary: The boundary of an observer is its set of merged pairs; it is empty exactly when the observer is injective. A test determined by the observer is constant on every merged pair, while undetermined tests can separate the pair.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Merged.conclusion: Every observer and merged pair satisfies the six clauses of Theorem 4.1, with empty boundary exactly for injective observers.
assumptions: DecidableEq X for separating-test and comparison clauses
Subsingleton X for constant test
classical tactic used in two invariance proofs

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/NoRetu.summary: The file studies when an observer can be inverted and what observing twice does, proving that a left inverse exists iff the observer is injective and characterizing inverting side maps by fibre sizes. It defines the record-choice composite, shows it is idempotent and injective exactly when the observer is, and that the non-disturbing instrument merges nothing. It proves that no infinite sequence implies no return with a successor counterexample and finite-type equivalence, then applies this to show the calculus has no infinite steps and no step is undone.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/NoRetu.boundary: An observer has a left inverse exactly when it is injective, with inverting record size bounded by the largest fibre. A relation has no return when it has no infinite sequence, with the converse failing in general but holding on finite types.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/NoRetu.conclusion: No infinite-step relation has a return, the calculus terminates and no step is ever undone, and observers invert exactly when injective.
assumptions: Classical.choice for record sections and infinite sequences
Finite T for return iff infinite sequence
kernel-only checking with no sorry or native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/NoisyR.summary: The file fixes the joint law of N noisy reports of a uniform hidden bit and defines the error of a deterministic decoder. It proves every transcript has positive mass and a uniform positive lower bound for any decoder, so no finite decoder has zero error at positive noise. It defines the majority decoder, proves its exponential error bound and that every positive tolerance is achieved at some odd horizon, concluding exact finite recovery fails while reliable recovery succeeds.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/NoisyR.boundary: No deterministic decoder of finitely many noisy reports has zero error when noise is positive, but majority vote makes error arbitrarily small with growing horizon. Exact finite recovery is impossible while arbitrarily reliable approximate recovery is possible.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/NoisyR.conclusion: Exact finite decoding is impossible at positive noise while majority vote attains every positive error tolerance.
assumptions: 0 <= epsilon <= 1/2 for lower bounds
0 < epsilon < 1/2 for positivity and no exact decoder
kernel-only checking with no sorry or classical choice

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Normal.summary: This file places the chosen normal-form map in observer vocabulary under unique normal forms. It characterizes merged pairs as distinct convertible states, determination by the normal form as step-invariance, and determination of the normal form via convertibility and kernels. It shows the ambient conversion class determines the normal form exactly under unique conversion of normals, which fails on the five-point example that has a merged pair.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Normal.boundary: An observer determines the normal form exactly when it separates nonconvertible states; the five-point relation lies on the failing side with a merged pair and nondetermining ambient class.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Normal.conclusion: Under unique normal forms, merged pairs, determination and collisions are exactly convertibility phenomena, with the five-point relation showing ambient convertibility need not determine the normal form.
assumptions: UNR R for merged-pair, determination and kernel characterizations
Five-point relation fiveRel with five_unr and five_not_unc for instances
No sorry, admit, axiom, native_decide; kernel-only as stated

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Nullst.summary: The file defines a polynomial observer that records the evaluations of a finite family of multivariate polynomials. It proves the zero fiber of the observer equals the zero locus of the ideal generated by the tests. It proves a target polynomial is constant on the variety exactly when a constant shift lies in the radical, including the empty variety. Failure of all such radical certificates yields two variety points with equal observer records and different target values.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Nullst.boundary: A polynomial target is constant on the variety exactly when some constant shift lies in the radical ideal. When no shift lies in the radical, two variety points share the same observer record but give different target values.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Nullst.conclusion: A polynomial target is constant on a variety exactly under a radical certificate, otherwise a merged pair witnesses non-constancy.

Field k
IsAlgClosed k
Finite σ
classical tactic in variety_collision proof

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.summary: The file records four statements not stated elsewhere: the readout family of a downward-closed family is nonempty iff it contains the empty set, and finite retained sets give equality and least-value characterizations of selector and coloring alphabets. It proves relabeling an annotated derivation commutes with taking its payload. It proves no function of only morphism and event trace returns the fixed-length certificate floor on a two-state system, witnessed by two transactions with same morphism and trace but floors 0 and 1.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.boundary: No function of only the morphism and event trace returns the fixed-length certificate floor of every operation. Feasible selector and coloring alphabets coincide on finite retained sets, infinite exactly when no finite alphabet succeeds.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.conclusion: Certificate floors are not functions of morphism and trace alone, while demand alphabets and annotated payloads transport as stated.
assumptions: kernel-only checking with no sorry, axiom or native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.summary: The file develops the Fisher remark: discrimination as the f-divergence of (u-1)^2/(u+1) with second derivative one at one, its closed form on the boundary law and failure of little-o, and the two forms of the reciprocal cost bound. It proves cost exceeds every multiple of (t-theta)^-2 at zero Fisher information and that repetition attains the inverse-square cost near parameters with positive information. It closes with the quadratic term of a twice-differentiable f-divergence as f''(1)/2 times the Fisher form.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.boundary: At positive Fisher information cost obeys reciprocal bounds in (t-theta)^-2, while at zero Fisher information it exceeds every multiple of (t-theta)^-2. On the support boundary discrimination is 2t^2/(2-t^2), not o(t^2), so the interior quadratic bound fails.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.conclusion: Fisher information controls local discrimination quadratically inside the support but not at the support boundary, with reciprocal cost bounds accordingly.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.summary: The file gathers language, computability and rewriting sentences: the Beth property without inhabitance and its licensed equivalence, maximal licensed subsets of the Goedel pair, and zero discrimination with failure of uniform evaluation. It records fair-coin, uncounted-run and fork facts with recursor unrolling, bounded-record and budget reports. It proves exact outgoing transport for injective encodings with machine conjugation, and decidability of bounded halting sets.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.boundary: Provability determines truth on each singleton of the Goedel pair but on no larger subset, and no total computable uniform evaluation exists. OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.conclusion: Maximal licensed subsets of the Goedel pair are the two singletons, bounded halting is decidable, and exact outgoing transport preserves paths, accessibility and confluence.

It extends the singularity to arbitrary costs and conditional initial records, gives Fisher loss as mean conditional variance for every channel via attained support including deterministic fibers, and adds kernel-pair readout impossibility, universal stable range, side-stabilizer equality, licensed-plan budget transport, depth-ratio bounds and persistent-state values.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.summary: Defines exact comparisons of observation systems by state, action and record equivalences with commuting observation and transition laws. Proves they preserve finite words, adaptive experiments, executed traces, costs, separating budgets, solvability, first distinctions and minimal observers, including the surjective-projection case. Introduces the countdown with exact finite separation costs and hidden payloads whose minimal observers coincide without a raw isomorphism. Defines resolution singularity and uniform budget obstruction and proves the countdown admits no uniform bounded solver, with transport across all such isomorphisms.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.boundary: A word of length at most n separates countdown states n and m with n smaller exactly when n is within budget, so each pair is finitely separable but no fixed budget separates all pairs. Solvability of the identity target within any uniform finite budget holds nowhere because resolution singularity transports across every observation isomorphism.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.conclusion: Every explicitly supplied observation isomorphism preserves exact solvability and singularity, and the countdown has no uniform finite-budget adaptive solver with that boundary surviving all such isomorphisms.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.summary: Extends recursor decidability to empty content carriers and to resolving coordinates of general observers. Proves content determines observations, counters and orienting measures exactly when the content type is empty, with a joint termination and determination statement for all carriers and an empty control. Classifies when a resolving or place coordinate is determined by or invariant under the license stabilizer as exactly injectivity of the observer, with merged-pair movement and identity controls.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.boundary: Content determines observations, counters and orienting measures on one side exactly when the content carrier is empty, and fails on every inhabited carrier. A resolving coordinate is stabilizer-invariant on one side exactly when the observer is injective, and every merged pair moves some resolving coordinate on the other side.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.conclusion: Content determines observations and admits a content-determined orienting measure exactly in the empty-content case, and a resolving coordinate is stabilizer-invariant exactly when the observer is injective.
assumptions: IsEmpty and Nonempty type-class hypotheses as stated in each theorem
No sorry, axiom or native_decide visible
Uses Pass, content, counter, Determines and Pass well-foundedness from RecursorDecidability
Uses licenseStabilizer and PlaceCoord from imported theories

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.summary: This file proves foundational observer sentences: least separating sets, constancy of continuous discrete maps, kernel characterizations via transitivity and determined tests, apartness, closed test families, and unique record bijections for surjective observers. It classifies swap-invariant relations, self-test orbits and invariant tests with indicator laws and entropies, least resolving sizes and fiberwise coordinates, and unequal-fiber orbits with mutual-information maxima.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.boundary: A reflexive symmetric table is a kernel exactly when transitive; continuous maps to a discrete space cannot separate states on a preconnected space, and resolving coordinates need at least the largest fiber size.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.conclusion: Two surjective observers share a kernel exactly when a unique record bijection commutes with them, and unequal fibers yield two nonempty resolving orbits.
assumptions: PreconnectedSpace and DiscreteTopology for constancy
DecidableEq where transpositions and filters are used
Fintype and Nonempty for uniform laws
IsEmpty for empty-state resolving size
Finite fibers with bound m where stated
