OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.summary: This file proves finite observer realization: gluing lemmas, binary rows with a common rate from cycle conditions, and the converse that cycle inequalities imply a hidden observer, hence a full rate-table characterization. It proves a general convex-hull characterization of common laws, score preservation, separating certificates and repair bounds, with context and hidden-record forms. It records the triangle incompatibility as unrealizable with optimal repair cost 1.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.boundary: A rate table has an observer exactly when cycle inequalities hold; a report family is realizable exactly when no linear score separates it, with the triangle (1,1,1) recorded as unrealizable and every repair costing at least 1.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.conclusion: Rate tables are realizable exactly under cycle inequalities and otherwise a separating score certifies a quantitative repair cost, with triangle optimum 1.
assumptions: Fintype record and assignment types
DecidableEq for coordinate comparison
Nonnegative normalized weights
Cycle inequalities with bound 1
Closed convex hull of finite range for Hahn-Banach separation
Classical decidability for finite sums

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.summary: Defines maximal repairs retaining no strictly larger stable repair and greatest repairs dominating every stable repair. Proves maximal means saturated in both relation and predicate coordinates, that both endpoint repairs are maximal and incomparable on a crossing fixture, with separate deletion costs monotone in the order. Proves a greatest repair exists exactly when the raw pair already preserves the predicate, so a boundary edge forbids it while the universal system has one.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.boundary: A greatest repair retaining the raw transition relation and predicate exists exactly when the raw pair already preserves the predicate; a single boundary-crossing edge places the system on the side with maximal but incomparable repairs and no greatest repair.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Observ.conclusion: Maximal repairs are exactly doubly saturated pairs with incomparable examples, while a greatest repair exists iff no repair was needed.
assumptions: Fintype for deletion counts
No sorry, axiom or native_decide visible
Trailing #check and #print axioms lines are checks only

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Occurr.summary: This file defines the occurrence law from content weights and place conditionals and proves its content marginal and entropy chain rule H(occurrence)=H(content)+H(place|content). It defines the uniform place law, proves its normalization and log(i+1) entropy, identifies the uniform conditional term with the recursor content-leaves-log, and proves the copy entropy with a log-2 non-vacuity check.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Occurr.conclusion: The copy occurrence law has entropy H(b)+log(i+1) nats and H(b)/log2+log2(i+1) bits.
assumptions: Fintype content and place types
Normalized place conditionals summing to one
Normalized content law where stated

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Orient.summary: This file studies orientation obstruction for recursor passes on Trace x Nat with the original content map. It defines goals quantifying over well-founded relations, strict orders and all universes with an exact irreflexivity criterion. It proves irreflexive relations already obstruct content determination via the adjacent pass, with well-founded and strict-order consequences, and exhibits counter and reflexive controls showing non-vacuity and load-bearing irreflexivity.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Orient.boundary: Content-determined decreasing maps exist exactly when the codomain relation has a reflexive point; irreflexive, well-founded and strict-order relations lie on the impossible side.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Orient.conclusion: No pass-decreasing measure into an irreflexive, in particular well-founded or strict-order, relation can be determined by content, and this holds exactly for irreflexive relations.
assumptions: Pass relation on Trace x Nat and content map from RecursorDecidability
Well-founded, strict-order or irreflexive codomain relations in any universe
No sorry, admit, axiom, native_decide beyond stated trust

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PairIn.summary: This module proves that record-preserving pair orbits are indexed by two records and one equality bit, and that invariant two-state functions depend only on that data. It constructs record-preserving matchings for finite sets with equal class counts and proves the full orbit equivalence without assuming finite classes. It proves point stabilizers are transitive off the fixed point with indicator-function invariants.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PairIn.boundary: Two pairs lie in one record-preserving orbit exactly when records match and equality bits match; two finite sets do exactly when per-class counts match, otherwise no such permutation exists.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PairIn.conclusion: Pair and finite-set orbits under record-preserving permutations are classified by records with equality and by per-class counts.
assumptions: DecidableEq on state and record types
Finiteness only of the two compared finsets, not of record classes

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PairQu.summary: This file builds the real vector spaces of quaternionic Hermitian matrices and their description by real diagonal and strictly-upper quaternion coordinates. It proves a real-linear coordinate equivalence and computes real dimensions 6 for size 2 and 28 for size 4, plus the general formula N + 4*N*(N-1)/2. It shows the 36-dimensional tensor product of two local spaces admits no linear equivalence or injective linear map into the 28-dimensional composite, while the Hermitian Kronecker products span the composite. It also records a raw Kronecker product of Hermitian matrices that is not Hermitian.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PairQu.boundary: The 36-dimensional real tensor product of the local Hermitian spaces lies across a dimension boundary from the 28-dimensional composite Hermitian space, so no linear equivalence or injective linear map bridges them. Within Kronecker products, Hermiticity is the boundary: a raw product of Hermitian matrices can fail to be Hermitian, while the subset of products that are Hermitian spans the composite.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PairQu.conclusion: The file proves the general quaternionic Hermitian dimension formula together with spanning of the size-4 Hermitian space by Hermitian Kronecker products and nonexistence of an injective linear map from the local tensor product.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PairRe.summary: This file repeats one two-row reading and decodes by likelihood ratio. It defines likelihood, Bhattacharyya coefficient, and the decoder, proves error at most half BC to the N with discrimination and exponential forms, and cost exactly N. It proves information at least one minus binary entropy over log two, a ceiling N attaining any target below one bit, a two-sided order inverse discrimination cost, and the split versus merged deterministic ends with zero versus one coefficient.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PairRe.boundary: At a split deterministic pair the Bhattacharyya coefficient is zero and one reading resolves the bit, while at a merged pair it is one with zero discrimination and no protocol gains information. Both sides of resolution cost are order inverse discrimination.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PairRe.conclusion: Every finite reading satisfies a two-sided resolution cost of order inverse discrimination with split pairs resolved in one reading and merged pairs yielding nothing.
assumptions: Fintype Y for rows and Fintype A for protocols
DecidableEq Y for deterministic rows
noncomputable definitions; no sorry axiom or native_decide visible

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Partia.summary: This file completes self-evaluation with an unresolved value none for Option Bool. It defines extended negation and proves none is its only fixed point, so exact self-evaluation forces none on the diagonal. It gives a two-code witness retaining definite values, proves no total Boolean readout preserves negation via a fixed-point obstruction, recovers definite records by restriction, and proves no self-evaluator exists in a cycle-closed language.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Partia.boundary: Exact self-evaluation in a negation-closed language forces the diagonal value to unresolved none. No total Boolean readout can preserve negation and no cycle-closed language has a self-evaluator.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Partia.conclusion: No total Boolean readout preserves negation and no cycle-closed language admits an internal self-evaluator.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Persis.summary: This file prices persistent decaying binary evidence with actual stopped laws and costs. It proves a geometric price identity, a finite lower bound four c times four to the n with positivity, and no uniform finite budget across states. It gives a concrete one-reading protocol with positive information at unit cost, defines frozen readings experiments costs and optimal infimum, and proves matching lower and ceiling repetition upper bounds yielding two-sided four to the n growth.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Persis.boundary: Any protocol attaining fixed positive information pays at least four c times four to the n, so no common finite budget works across decaying states. The optimal frozen cost lies between a times four to the n and b times four to the n plus one.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Persis.conclusion: The optimal frozen cost grows two-sided as four to the n for every positive target below one bit.
assumptions: Fintype A for action alphabets
noncomputable section with Filter and Topology limits
no sorry axiom or native_decide visible

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Persis.summary: The file builds a decaying bias family epsilon with limit zero and the actual binary-kernel output rows answer. It defines the successor relation step from n to n plus 1, proves every state is reachable from zero and every state is exogenous hence persistent, and computes triangular discrimination as 8 times epsilon squared tending to zero. It defines the fair-target joint law with positive mutual information and combines persistence, informativeness andreachable no-floor into one family.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Persis.boundary: Persistence with positive information holds on one side, but no positive uniform discrimination floor holds on the other. Discrimination is always positive yet tends to zero, so no d greater than zero bounds all reachable states.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Persis.conclusion: There is a persistent, always informative binary family whose discrimination is always positive but has no positive uniform lower bound over reachable states.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Persis.summary: This module defines the persistent difference license as disequality of all guarded reducts with its operand interior, proving interior characterization, preservation under reduction, failure on joinable pairs, and the (void, delta void) instance. It defines the licensed seven-rule contextual relation, proves inclusion, termination, local joinability and confluence via Newman lemma with recorded non-confluence of the plain relation. It proves the witness term is unlicensed yet reaches void uniquely.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Persis.boundary: The plain guarded contextual relation is recorded as not confluent, while the licensed repaired relation terminates and is confluent; a pair is licensed exactly when no common reduct exists.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Persis.conclusion: The licensed repaired relation terminates and is confluent, and the witness term reaches void as its unique normal form.
assumptions: WellFounded repaired relation via polynomial interpretation
Contextual guarded reduction and StepCtxFull inclusion
No infinite reduction of PStepCtx

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Pitows.summary: The file defines deterministic and table correlations and proves a table has a finite common observer exactly when its correlation vector lies in the convex hull of deterministic vectors. It rewrites box bounds and eight cycle inequalities as sixteen sign-pattern inequalities, constructs explicit convex weights to prove the half-space description, and deduces Fine theorem and the observer-cycle equivalence. It shows the hull has eight vertices, sixteen facets and full dimension four, and exhibits a control table satisfying the cycle inequalities but lying outside the hull.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Pitows.boundary: A rate table in [0,1] has a finite observer exactly when its correlations satisfy the box bounds and the eight cycle inequalities. The cycle inequalities alone do not suffice, since the control table satisfies them yet has no observer.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Pitows.conclusion: A four-test table with rates in [0,1] has a common finite observer exactly when its correlations lie in the eight-vertex full-dimensional polytope with sixteen facets.
assumptions: Rates in [0,1] and CycleIneq with bound 1 for Fine direction
No sorry, admit, axiom or native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PlaceC.summary: This module proves content-place complementarity: joint injectivity, one-step joins, total transitive closure, unique class intersections, and occurrence trichotomy. It proves existence of n-valued place coordinates exactly under finite at-most-n fibers using choice, and that full labellings biject states with record-place pairs in one free transitive orbit. It proves pair labellings biject with members equivariantly.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PlaceC.boundary: A place coordinate with n values exists exactly when every record class is finite with at most n elements; fewer values than some class size never suffice.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PlaceC.conclusion: Labellings with full class size form one free orbit under record-preserving permutations, bijecting states with record-place pairs.
assumptions: Classical.choice for per-class injections
No finiteness or inhabitedness for content-place complementarity
Finite fibers with bound n where stated

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PlaceE.summary: The file states the exact existence goal for PlaceCoord on the original observer and proves a coordinate forces each attained class to be finite of size n. It constructs a coordinate from finite equal-size attained classes through the bounded-coordinate theorem and finite surjectivity, yielding the goal equivalence, its nonempty-fiber form, and the empty-source and zero-value edge cases.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PlaceE.boundary: A place coordinate with n values is nonempty exactly when every attained fiber is finite of size n, and with zero values exactly when the source is empty.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PlaceE.conclusion: Under finite attained classes, a place coordinate with n values exists exactly when every attained class has exactly n elements, with empty and zero cases classified.
assumptions: classical reasoning via PlaceCoordinates.exists_place_coordinate_iff
Fintype Fin n and Set ncard lemmas from Mathlib

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceExistence.PlaceExistenceGoal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: PlaceExistenceGoal q n says finite attained fibers imply Nonempty PlaceCoord q n is equivalent to every attained fiber having ncard n.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceExistence.placeCoord_fiber_cardinality
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If p is in PlaceCoord q n and y is attained then the fiber is finite with ncard n, under those hypotheses.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceExistence.placeCoord_nonempty_fiber_cardinality
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If p is in PlaceCoord q n and the fiber over y is nonempty then it is finite with ncard n, under those hypotheses.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceExistence.placeCoord_const_nonempty
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: PlaceCoord of the constant observer on Fin n with n values is nonempty for every n including 0.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceExistence.placeCoord_nonempty_of_fiber_cardinality

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceExistence.placeExistenceGoal

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceExistence.placeCoord_nonempty_iff_finite_fiber_cardinality
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: PlaceCoord q n is nonempty if and only if every nonempty fiber is finite with ncard n.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceExistence.placeCoord_nonempty_of_isEmpty
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If X is empty then PlaceCoord q n is nonempty for every n, under that IsEmpty hypothesis.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceExistence.placeCoord_zero_nonempty_iff

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PlaceO.summary: Defines fiber restrictions of invisible permutations and place families with per-fiber alphabets and their group action. Proves the action is free and transitive, hence one free orbit with a unique transporter, and every family resolves states with its record via a joint bijection. Relates the common alphabet Fin n to place coordinates by an equivariant equivalence and deduces coordinate freeness and transitivity. Gives a three-state control where a common alphabet yields four resolving maps in two orbits.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PlaceO.boundary: With a per-fiber alphabet every observer has one free orbit of place families. With a common alphabet Fin n the one-orbit statement holds for fibers of one size n but fails for fibers of unequal size, where the Fin 3 control splits into two orbits.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/PlaceO.conclusion: For every observer and alphabet family the place families form one free orbit with a unique transporting invisible permutation and resolve every state, while a common alphabet splits into two orbits when fiber sizes differ.
assumptions: arbitrary types X, Q and alphabet family A with no finiteness assumed
Classical.choice used for one bijection per fiber in nonempty characterization and common-alphabet existence

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.stabilizer_symm_apply
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For an invisible permutation sigma and every x, q applied to sigma-symm x equals q x.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.fiberPerm
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition: restriction of sigma to the fiber over y, sending a fiber point to sigma applied to its state with record preservation.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.fiberPerm_eq_fiberMulEquiv
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The restriction fiberPerm q sigma y equals the y-component of sigma under licenseStabilizerFiberMulEquiv.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.PlaceFamily
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition: PlaceFamily for alphabet family A is for each record y an equivalence from the observer fiber over y to A y.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.instMulAction
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Instance: the invisible group acts on place families by sigma dot f at y equals (fiberPerm sigma y).symm trans (f y).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.placeFamily_free
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every observer and alphabet family, an invisible permutation fixing one place family is the identity.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.placeFamilyTransport
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition: the invisible permutation carrying f to g, assembled fiberwise as (f y).trans (g y).symm through the stabilizer product isomorphism.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.placeFamily_transitive
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every observer and alphabet family, any two place families differ by some invisible permutation, with no finiteness assumed.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.instIsPretransitive
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Instance: the action of the invisible group on place families with one alphabet family is pretransitive.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.placeFamily_exists_unique
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For any two place families f and g with the same alphabet family, there is a unique invisible permutation sigma with sigma dot f = g.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.placeFamilyEquiv
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition: joint map sending x to its record together with f at its record, as an equivalence to Sigma y, A y.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.placeFamily_joint_bijective
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every observer, alphabet family and place family f, the map x to record plus f at record into Sigma y, A y is bijective.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.placeFamilyId
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition: identity place family using each fiber as its own alphabet.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.placeFamily_self
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: There is a place family with fibers as alphabets that resolves every state together with the record.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.placeFamily_nonempty_iff
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: There is a place family for A if and only if every fiber is in bijection with its alphabet, using Classical.choice for one bijection per fiber.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.toPlaceCoord
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition: labelling of a common-alphabet place family sending x to f at its record applied to x.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.toPlaceCoord_mem
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The labelling of a common-alphabet place family belongs to PlaceCoord q n.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.ofPlaceCoord
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition: noncomputable common-alphabet place family from a place coordinate by restriction to each fiber, using bijectivity on fibers.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.placeCoordEquiv
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition: noncomputable equivalence between common-alphabet place families and PlaceCoord q n.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.toPlaceCoord_smul
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The labelling of sigma dot f equals the labelling of f composed with sigma-symm.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.placeFamily_common_alphabet
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If every fiber is in bijection with Fin n, then PlaceCoord q n is nonempty and there is an equivalence from common-alphabet families to coordinates carrying sigma dot f to composition with sigma-symm, using Classical.choice.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.placeCoord_free_of_placeFamily
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If p in PlaceCoord q n is fixed by sigma in the stabilizer in the sense p compose sigma-symm = p, then sigma = 1.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.placeCoord_transitive_of_placeFamily
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For p and p' in PlaceCoord q n there are sigma in the stabilizer with p' = p compose sigma-symm.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.common_alphabet_two_orbits
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For q on Fin 3 with q 0=false, q 1=false, q 2=true, the maps (0,1,0) and (0,1,1) into Fin 2 are both injective together with q and no invisible sigma gives p' = p compose sigma-symm.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PlaceOrbitGeneral.common_alphabet_four_coordinates_two_orbits
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For the same q, the type of resolving maps into Fin 2 has cardinality 4, the two displayed maps are resolving and unrelated, and every resolving map lies in the orbit of one of them.

relations.explanation: Common-alphabet transitivity is the per-fiber transitivity applied through the coordinate-family equivalence.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Popesc.summary: Defines the PR table with disagreement only at true-true and proves its algebraic score is four. Proves it admits no single joint observer and violates the final-setting cycle inequality. Defines explicit half-weight parity joint laws and proves they are nonnegative, normalized, realize the table, and give uniform one-party marginals. Restates score, no-observer, and uniform-marginals facts in the FourTestTables namespace.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Popesc.boundary: Every table with a joint observer has algebraic score at most two, while the PR table attains score four and admits no observer. Its final-setting cycle inequality fails at the true-true pair.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Popesc.conclusion: The PR table has score four with no joint observer and is realized by half-weight parity joints giving uniform report marginals.
assumptions: Bool settings and reports with Fintype sums
FourTestTables score, corr, HasObserver, CycleIneq, disagree, boolSign as imported
proofs by norm_num, decide and case analysis with no extra hypotheses

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PopescuRohrlichBox.prBox
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition: table sending (x,y) to if x && y then 1 else 0, so disagreement is zero except at true-true.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PopescuRohrlichBox.prBox_score
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The score of prBox equals 4.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PopescuRohrlichBox.prBox_no_observer
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: There is no HasObserver for prBox, using that any observer table has absolute score at most two while prBox has score four.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PopescuRohrlichBox.prBox_cycle_fails
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: CycleIneq for prBox at 1 does not hold, with failure at the true-true component.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PopescuRohrlichBox.prJoint
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition: noncomputable joint assigning 1/2 when boolSign products equal (-1)^(x*y) and 0 otherwise.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PopescuRohrlichBox.prJoint_nonneg
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all x y a b, prJoint x y a b is nonnegative.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PopescuRohrlichBox.prJoint_normalized
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all x y, the double sum over reports of prJoint equals 1.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PopescuRohrlichBox.prJoint_realizes
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all x y, the disagree-weighted double sum of prJoint equals prBox x y.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PopescuRohrlichBox.prJoint_marginals_uniform
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all x y and reports, each single-party marginal sum of prJoint equals 1/2.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FourTestTables.pr_box_score_eq_four
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Recorded: the score of PopescuRohrlichBox.prBox equals 4, by the PR score theorem.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FourTestTables.pr_box_no_observer
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Recorded: PopescuRohrlichBox.prBox has no HasObserver, by the PR no-observer theorem.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.FourTestTables.pr_box_uniform_marginals
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Recorded conjunction: prJoint is nonnegative, normalized, realizes prBox, and has 1/2 marginals for each party.

relations.explanation: Score four exceeds the observer bound of two, blocking a joint observer.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Primre.summary: This file defines arithmetic definability with fresh variables above 53 and environment updates, with pairing and beta evaluation lemmas. It defines the precoding sequence and recursion formula and proves the formula correct via beta-coded finite sequences. It proves Godel Proposition VII that every Nat.Primrec function is definable by induction on its generation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Primre.boundary: An arithmetic definition is guaranteed only with input and output variables at least 53; smaller variables may clash with bound variables of order and remainder formulas.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Primre.conclusion: Every primitive recursive function has an arithmetic definition at all variable pairs at least 53.
assumptions: Input and output variables at least 53 to avoid bound variables 50-52
Godel beta-sequence existence beta_exists
Induction over Nat.Primrec constructors

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PrimrecDefinability.DefinesAt
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition: formula phi defines f at a,b when evalForm env phi iff f(env a)=env b for all env.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PrimrecDefinability.Definable
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition: f has a defining formula at every pair a,b at least 53.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PrimrecDefinability.vr
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition of fresh variables a+b+53+j above inputs and bound variables.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PrimrecDefinability.upd
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition of environment update at x with n.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PrimrecDefinability.PairF
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition of the Cantor pairing equation n=pair x y on variables.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PrimrecDefinability.precSeq
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition of the sequence computed by Primrec.prec at parameter z.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PrimrecDefinability.precForm
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition of the primitive-recursion defining formula from base and step formulas with fresh variables.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PrimrecDefinability.eval_PairF
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If x,y avoid 51 then PairF holds iff env n = Nat.pair (env x) (env y).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PrimrecDefinability.eval_betaT
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Under avoidance of 51 and 52 and variable-freeness hypotheses, betaF holds iff env w = beta (env c) (env d) (evalTerm env i).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.PrimrecDefinability.rec_eq_precSeq
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Nat.rec with f,g equals precSeq f g at every n.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If phiF and phiG define f,g at the stated fresh variables and a,b≥53, then precForm defines precSeq at unpair of env a versus env b.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If f is Nat.Primrec then f is Definable, by induction with zero/successor equations, pairing projections, fresh-variable pairing/composition, and beta-coded recursion.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Protoc.summary: Defines summed active mass below a horizon. Proves the drift identity expressing stopped mass of a potential with one-step mean drift d via prior mass plus d times summed active mass. Proves growth by one-horizon active mass, summation over horizons, unit-cost expected cost as summed active mass, nonnegativity, and vanishing of active mass under a uniform bound.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Protoc.boundary: When the summed active mass below n is bounded by C for all n, the active mass tends to zero so the protocol stops with probability one for that target; without such a bound the file gives no vanishing guarantee.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Protoc.conclusion: The stopped mass satisfies the drift identity with summed active mass, unit-cost expected cost equals that sum, and a bounded sum forces active mass to zero.
assumptions: Fintype Z, A, Y for finite protocols
one-step mean drift hypothesis hdrift at every unstopped history
unit costs with HistoryBank for expected-cost identity
bound C on summed active mass for vanishing

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ProtocolDynkin.activeBelow
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Definition: activeBelow p z n is the sum over historySet n of activeValue of prefixMass at horizon n.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ProtocolDynkin.protocol_dynkin
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Given a finite protocol, target z, function V and drift d such that at every unstopped h the one-step mean of V over policy and observation equals V h + d, the stopped-mass weighted sum of V at horizon n equals prior mass times V at empty plus d times activeBelow.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ProtocolDynkin.activeBelow_zero
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: activeBelow p z 0 equals 0, by definition of activeValue.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ProtocolDynkin.activeBelow_succ
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: activeBelow at n+1 equals activeBelow at n plus activeMass at n.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ProtocolDynkin.activeBelow_eq_sum
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: activeBelow p z n equals the sum over t in range n of activeMass p t z.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ProtocolDynkin.expectedCost_unit
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If every cost equals 1 and bank is a HistoryBank at n, then expectedCost at n equals sum over z of activeBelow p z n.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ProtocolDynkin.activeBelow_nonneg
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every p z n, 0 <= activeBelow p z n from nonnegativity of activeMass.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ProtocolDynkin.activeMass_tendsto_zero_of_bounded
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If for some C every n satisfies activeBelow p z n <= C, then activeMass p n z tends to 0.

relations.explanation: The summation form turns the bounded summed mass into summability and vanishing of active mass.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Protoc.summary: The file defines finite-horizon and limit family frontiers as infima of costs of qualifying protocols, with infinity for empty qualifying families. It proves every qualifying binary-menu family pays at least c over 4 epsilon squared in both horizons, including infinite extended cost. It lifts finite protocols to one-record conditional protocols preserving information and cost, and shows families containing majority protocols achieve the target within log of 1 over 2 eta over 2 epsilon squared plus 3 in both horizons.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Protoc.boundary: Information c is attainable only at cost at least c divided by 4 epsilon squared, while majority protocols attain it at cost at most log of 1 over 2 eta divided by 2 epsilon squared plus 3.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Protoc.conclusion: Binary-menu families need at least c over 4 epsilon squared to reach information c, and majority-containing families reach it within the stated logarithmic upper bound in both horizons.
assumptions: Fintype H0, Z, A and Y
BinaryMenu bias bounds 0 less than epsilon and epsilon at most 1/2
Information target hypotheses c at most stated majority information

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ProtocolFamilyCost.familyMinCost
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: familyMinCost S c is the infimum of extended costs of qualifying protocol-horizon pairs with information at least c, and infinity if none qualify.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ProtocolFamilyCost.familyLimitMinCost
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: familyLimitMinCost S c is the infimum of extended costs of protocols whose limit information is at least c, and infinity if none qualify.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ProtocolFamilyCost.familyMinCost_lower
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For a binary-menu family with 0 less than epsilon and epsilon at most 1/2, ofReal of c over 4 epsilon squared is at most familyMinCost S c, under those bias and menu hypotheses.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ProtocolFamilyCost.familyLimitMinCost_lower
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For a binary-menu family with 0 less than epsilon and epsilon at most 1/2, ofReal of c over 4 epsilon squared is at most familyLimitMinCost S c including infinite cost, under those hypotheses.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ProtocolFamilyCost.onePointLift
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: onePointLift p is the conditional protocol with one initial record whose joint law is the prior of p.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ProtocolFamilyCost.onePointLift_jointInfo
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every complete history bank, conditional joint info of the lift equals terminalMI of p, under that completeness hypothesis.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ProtocolFamilyCost.onePointLift_expectedCost
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every horizon and bank, conditional expected cost of the lift equals expectedCost of p.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.ProtocolFamilyCost.familyMinCost_upper_majority

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Protoc.summary: The file defines finite probability laws, entropy and mutual information in bits, and a signed-bias binary channel with its joint law and capacity envelopes. It builds finite adaptive protocols with history-dependent policy, observation, stopping, and cost, with stopped masses, terminal mutual information, and expected cost, plus conditional versions carrying initial side information. It proves per-step entropy telescopes, local capacity bounds, and finite-horizon and limiting information-cost inequalities, specialized to binary menus with quadratic and exact binary-symmetric capacities. It adds relabeling isomorphisms for protocols and tasks, a feasible-frontier framework with least costs, and concrete binary-task controls separating feasible from infeasible, probability from support, license from law, and cost from law.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Protoc.boundary: An adaptive binary reading of absolute bias at most epsilon yields at most 4*epsilon^2 bits, exactly binaryCapacity epsilon, per unit expected cost. Hence c bits need at least c/(4*epsilon^2) expected cost, and zero bias or zero capacity yields zero information while noiseless endpoints return full prior entropy.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Protoc.conclusion: Every admissible adaptive binary experiment obeys an inverse-square information-cost frontier, exactly binaryCapacity in the limit, preserved under relabeling but not by equal support, license loss, or cost change alone.
assumptions: Fintype instances for all finite carriers
FiniteLaw mass nonnegativity and total mass one
cost_nonnegative for every history and action
LocalCapacityBound required only on reachable active positive-mass branches
envelope hypothesis |delta| <= epsilon with epsilon <= 1/2
classical reasoning used for historySet; no sorry, axiom or native_decide shown

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Readin.summary: Proves an explicit positive signal radius from finite budget and information target. Shows every reading count within budget falls below the target inside that radius, including zero counts. Packages the quadratic ceiling, inverse-square minimum reading count, and bounded failure into a single resolution-cost statement.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Record.summary: This file proves record-choice sentences: the idempotent composite merges exactly as q does and distinct choices give distinct composites. It defines the fiberwise exchange of two choices as an invisible involution conjugating the composites. It proves conjugation closure gives one orbit, characterizes the stabilizer as fixing chosen states, and proves freeness exactly when no fiber has three states.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Record.boundary: The record-choice orbit is free exactly when no fiber has three or more states; with two extra states the exchange is a nontrivial stabilizer.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Record.conclusion: Record choices form one invisible-group orbit with stabilizer fixing chosen states, free exactly without three-point fibers.
assumptions: Classical.choice for decidability of equality in fiberExchange
Section hypotheses that u and u' are record sections
licenseStabilizer membership q circ sigma = q

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Record.summary: The file studies an observer q : X → Q with a record choice u picking one state per record, and the idempotent state transition e = u ∘ q. It characterizes the greatest compatible relation M_e and proves a relation realizes e iff its steps stay inside one q-fiber from an unchosen state and every state reaches its chosen state, with conversion equal to the kernel of q. It proves e has a least realization iff the conjugation action fixing chosen states is free, iff no q-fiber contains three distinct states, with the least realization then sending each unchosen state directly to its chosen state. It illustrates the bound with a two-state Bool example that has a least realization and a three-state Fin 3 example that has none.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Record.boundary: A record-choice transition has a least realization if every observer fiber has at most two states. If some fiber has three distinct states, in particular two distinct unchosen states sharing one record, no least realization exists.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Record.conclusion: Under the section hypothesis, a record-choice transition has a least realization, necessarily the direct-to-chosen relation RootStar, iff no observer fiber contains three distinct states.
assumptions: section hypothesis ∀ y, Set.rangeFactorization q (uc y) = y (q ∘ u = id) for the main characterizations
Classical.choice via classical tactic and imported decidability of equality
set_option autoImplicit false

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Recurs.summary: Defines the uncounted self-loop relation and its constant run, and the counted pass relation on T x Nat with content, counter and observed-test observers. Proves the self-loop returns and has an infinite run whose state determines only constant targets, so the zero-test on passes is not state-determined. Proves the counted passes have no infinite sequence or return, are well-founded, have run length exactly the starting counter, keep content constant while the counter orients, and that orienting measures and the observed test are counter-determined but not content-determined. Defines left-entropy and the zero-test on passes and proves the content leaves log (n+1) with one bit for one pass, the counter leaves zero, and the entropy split for the zero-test.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Recurs.boundary: Content-only measures orient no pass while the counter orients every pass; the uncounted state determines only constants, whereas the observed zero-test is determined by the counter and by no content observer.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Recurs.conclusion: The counted pass relation is well-founded and oriented by the counter, which alone determines the observed test and whose entropy cost separates content from counter.
assumptions: Nonempty T for orientation and non-determination theorems
Fintype with DecidableEq and Nonempty for entropy lemmas
autoImplicit false
No sorry, axiom, native_decide; kernel-only per header

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Resolu.summary: The file builds the majority protocol that reads a fair bit through N independent binary-symmetric readings of bias ε at unit cost and stops at N. It computes its paid cost, the likelihood structure of histories, and the error of majority decoding over 2n+1 readings. It proves a binary Fano bound by concavity of binary entropy and turns the error bound into an information lower bound. Together these give a two-sided resolution-cost bound whose exponent in ε is two on both sides.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Resolu.boundary: Every binary-menu protocol pays at least c/(4*ε^2) for c bits. The majority protocol pays at most log(1/(2*η))/(2*ε^2)+3 for 1-h₂(η)/log 2 bits, so the ε⁻² scaling cannot be improved.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Resolu.conclusion: The ε⁻² resolution-cost lower bound is sharp, attained up to constants by majority voting over 2n+1 readings.
assumptions: Fintype instances for E, Z, A, Y
set_option autoImplicit false

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Resour.summary: The file defines the resolution task family, its finite-horizon, limit, and confidence minimum costs, and a reading strategy that stops at N. It embeds the majority protocol into the task by a protocol isomorphism and computes its information and cost. It proves explicit two-sided bounds for all three minima and abstracts them into inverse-square scaling plus exact capacity lower bounds. It also shows budget feasibility is preserved under demand isomorphisms.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Resour.boundary: At bias ε in (0,1/2] at least c/(4*ε^2) readings are necessary for c bits while log(1/(2*η))/(2*ε^2)+3 readings suffice by majority. The same Θ(ε⁻²) frontier holds for unbounded experiments and confidence-constrained minima.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Resour.conclusion: Every fixed information target below one bit has least finite-horizon, extended, and confidence-constrained cost of order ε⁻² from both sides.
assumptions: c ≤ 1 - Real.binEntropy η / Real.log 2
Fintype instances
ENNReal infima with ToReal projection

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/RiceBo.summary: The file formalises bounded evaluation records, padding codes that hide computation budget, and the halting test. It proves Rice's theorem that a computable extensional Boolean test is constant and exhibits opposite-labelled codes sharing any bounded record. It derives zero-discrimination and zero-information poles for record-determined readings and shows halting is the union of bounded tests, semidecidable with non-semidecidable complement. Bounded records determine evaluation but are strictly finer.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/RiceBo.boundary: An extensional Boolean test is computable only if constant, so no nontrivial semantic property is decidable. Halting is enumerable through bounded records but its complement is not, and bounded records are strictly finer than evaluation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/RiceBo.conclusion: No nonconstant extensional Boolean test is computable, and bounded records determine but strictly refine program semantics.

ComputablePred and REPred
Fintype instances for readings

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/RuinWa.summary: Defines the counter, ruin stopping predicate, unit and fair-coin laws, and the symmetric ruin walk protocol that moves the counter by plus or minus one with equal chance, unit cost, and stops at 0 or N, with one step law under both values of a fair label. Proves the pair is merged at every reading so terminal mutual information is zero at every horizon and zero in the limit. Defines the potential c(N-c) and proves it drops by one at every unstopped history, giving the drift identity. Deduces the summed active mass and expected cost are at most k(N-k), the walk stops with probability one, expected cost tends to k(N-k), and this bound grows without bound as barriers recede.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/RuinWa.boundary: The label is indistinguishable at every horizon yet the walk still stops with probability one with expected cost at most k(N-k), a bound that becomes arbitrarily large as the barriers recede.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/RuinWa.conclusion: The symmetric ruin walk acquires zero information at every horizon yet stops with probability one with expected cost exactly k(N-k) in the limit.
assumptions: 0 less than k less than N for stopping and cost bounds
Fair label with prior 1/2 and fair step law with unit cost
autoImplicit false
No sorry, axiom, native_decide in the file

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Secrec.summary: The file defines discrete priors with possibly infinite support and the ciphertext marginal, law, and joint message-ciphertext law for finite ciphertexts. It proves the Shannon information identity without subtracting infinite entropies and that finite-support priors embed with matching information. It proves equal rows give zero information for every discrete prior and conversely, yielding the every-prior secrecy equivalence. A geometric prior and fair-coin example show the result beyond finite support.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Secrec.boundary: If all ciphertext rows coincide, information is zero under every discrete prior including infinite-support ones. If some rows differ, some prior gives positive information, so perfect secrecy is exactly row equality.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Secrec.conclusion: Equal ciphertext rows are equivalent to zero information under every discrete prior, including infinite-support priors.
assumptions: Fintype C
HasSum mass 1 for DiscretePrior
Summable joint columns
noncomputable section

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Secrec.summary: Defines finite-support priors and their support information as joint mutual information on the support subtype. Proves zero discrimination at every pair iff rows are equal, and rows are equal iff support information vanishes for every finite-support prior, with the uniform pair prior giving the converse. Transfers the finite-type case as support univ, shows protocols with equal rows acquire zero information at every horizon and in the limit, and illustrates both sides with the constant fair-coin reading and the informative parity reading on naturals.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Secrec.boundary: Equal ciphertext rows give zero information under every finite-support prior while any differing rows admit a two-point prior with nonzero information.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Secrec.conclusion: Equal rows hold exactly when support information vanishes for every finite-support prior, and any such reading gives protocols zero information at every horizon.
assumptions: Fintype C for ciphertexts and Fintype for finite-type lemmas
Classical for pairPrior construction
autoImplicit false
No sorry, axiom, native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Secrec.summary: The file proves the finite-message secrecy-privacy clauses: zero-ratio privacy forces zero discrimination and zero information at all horizons and in the limit, positive privacy forces a quadratic cost lower bound, and identical rows equal zero information for all priors. It computes the biased one-time pad discrimination 8δ², secret iff the key is fair, and lifts zero and positive privacy to conditional protocols with tanh and quadratic bounds. A reused-pad joint row with fair marginals decodes the label, showing marginal secrecy does not imply joint secrecy.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Secrec.boundary: At privacy parameter zero, readings and conditional experiments reveal nothing regardless of cost, while at ε>0 acquiring c bits costs at least 2c log 2/ε^2. For the biased pad secrecy holds exactly when δ=0, and fair marginals can coexist with perfect joint decoding under shared randomness.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Secrec.conclusion: Zero privacy gives zero information, positive privacy exacts a quadratic cost, and shared reuse breaks joint secrecy despite fair marginals.
assumptions: Fintype instances
IndistinguishableRows ε hypotheses
1 ≤ cost hypotheses
0 < ε and 0 ≤ ε as stated
classical tactic in biased-pad proofs

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/SeedFr.summary: The file bounds binary-output readings and constructs a seeded protocol attaining the bound. It shows a two-point mass has entropy at most one bit, local gain at a retained history is at most one bit, and any protocol with unit-cost binary readings acquires at most its expected cost in bits, conditionally and unconditionally. It defines the perfect reading, fair label and a seed-dependent branch that reads once when the seed is true and stops when false, with joint seed-label law and conditional protocol. It proves the true branch carries one bit at cost one, the false branch carries zero at cost zero, and the mixture carries exactly c bits at cost c, yielding the frontier that least cost of c bits is c.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/SeedFr.boundary: Binary-output readings costing at least one carry at most one bit per unit cost, so conditional information is bounded by conditional expected cost. The seeded protocol attains exactly c bits at expected cost c for 0 <= c <= 1, so c is the least cost of c bits.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/SeedFr.conclusion: For 0 <= c <= 1 some fair-label independent-seed conditional protocol with perfect unit-cost readings acquires exactly c bits at expected cost c, and no binary-output unit-cost protocol can do better, so the least cost of c bits is c.
assumptions: Fintype Z and Fintype A for binary-output section
1 <= cost at every history and action for upper bounds
0 <= c <= 1 for seeded protocol
No sorry, axiom, native_decide or classical choice visible

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/SelfEv.summary: The file formalizes one observation contract and two obstructions sharing it: collisions block every readout family and missing readouts block the full observer, separated by the xor evaluator whose code observer has empty boundary but whose diagonal is represented by no code. It classifies negation-preserving readouts of the three-valued completion over rationals and over real probabilities in [0,1] as normalized Boolean kernels, showing no total Boolean readout preserves negation while the fair coin does and is unique under accurate definite readings. It gives an approximate self-evaluation bound delta <= epsd + epsr with an attaining example, a collision-error half bound, and a fixed-point-free shift map with no uniform displacement showing the displacement hypothesis is needed. It separates test accuracy from coverage with threshold and paired families: finite input sets are passed, geometric mean error tends to zero and bounded-block minima are classified, yet no code represents the complemented diagonal and every code errs somewhere.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/SelfEv.boundary: A collision or a missing readout blocks exact observation, and no deterministic Boolean readout can preserve negation while a stochastic fair coin can. Finite test blocks can have zero error and arbitrarily small mean error, but globally every code misses its diagonal target.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/SelfEv.conclusion: Every finite input set is passed by some threshold code with geometric mean error tending to zero, yet no code represents the complemented diagonal and bounded paired blocks have minimum mean error 1/(2n).
assumptions: Nonempty V for univ characterization
PseudoMetricSpace V for approximate and collision-error bounds

No sorry, axiom, native_decide per file header

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Sequen.summary: Defines one-step and transcript log-likelihood ratios, the SPRT stopping rule and protocol, and KL divergence. Proves Wald identities at every horizon through the drift identity. Proves expected-count caps, stopping with probability one, the likelihood-ratio change of measure, and exp(-A) conditional error bounds. Proves divergence lower bounds via log concavity and specializes to binary symmetric rows as a biased ruin walk with explicit error and count bounds.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Sequen.boundary: Inside (-A,A) the test continues and outside it stops, with conditional error at most exp(-A) on one side and conditional expected count at most (A+ell)/divergence on the other.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Sequen.conclusion: The SPRT stops with probability one, errs with conditional chance at most exp(-A), and has expected count at most (A+ell)/divergence, instantiated as error exp(-4ek) and count (k+1)/(2e) for the biased walk.
assumptions: Full support 0 less than P and Q masses
Bound |llr| <= ell and threshold A >= 0
Distinct rows for positivity and Nonempty Y for count bounds
Positive prior masses for error bounds

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/SoundE.summary: Defines provability through a Boolean proof relation, its paired indicator and its primitive-recursive preservation, and a provability formula with a specification that it holds exactly when a proof code exists. Proves from definability and the diagonal sentence of negated provability that any sound primitive-recursive proof predicate has a true sentence that it does not prove and whose negation it also does not prove.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/SoundE.boundary: Soundness holds on one side while completeness fails on the other: the diagonal sentence is true exactly when unprovable, so neither it nor its negation is provable.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/SoundE.conclusion: Every sound primitive-recursive proof predicate is incomplete, with an explicit true sentence neither it nor its negation proves.
assumptions: Primrec2 prf
Soundness: ProvBy prf implies true in env0
autoImplicit false
No sorry, axiom, native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Stocha.summary: This file defines finite stochastic channels, their support-conflict graphs, and zero-error decoders with side records. It proves a decoder exists exactly when the side record separates conflicting inputs, equivalently colorings and chromatic number bound the side alphabet, repetition leaves the conflict graph and decodability unchanged, the five-cycle needs three side symbols and two do not suffice, and N-reading mutual information grows at most quadratically so any finite budget fails sufficiently weak signals.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Stocha.boundary: Zero-error decoding succeeds exactly when the side record assigns different values to inputs sharing a possible output with different targets, and repetition of a nonnegative reading does not change this requirement. Two side symbols cannot decode the five-cycle while three can, and any fixed reading budget is beaten by sufficiently weak signals.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Stocha.conclusion: Side-record chromatic number characterizes zero-error decodability, repetition never helps, and the five-cycle separates two from three symbols while finite budgets fail weak signals.
assumptions: Fintype Y for channels and DecidableEq Y for deterministic construction
Nonempty V for default value in decoder construction and Nonempty Y for full-support arguments
explicit classical choice via Classical.choose and Classical.choice with classical tactic
no sorry, axiom, or native_decide in code

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Stoppe.summary: Defines the miss indicator, active-history term, full until-stopping error, horizon error with an active rule, all-active horizon error, and continued-transcript active error. Proves summability and active-mass identities. Proves horizon error with any active rule exceeds full error by at most the active mass, with exact decomposition when actives are scored as errors, and that scoring actives as errors never lowers full error.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Stoppe.boundary: Deciding at horizon n versus running until stopping differ by at most the active mass at n, with equality minus the continued-transcript error when actives are scored as errors.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Stoppe.conclusion: Stopping at horizon n raises full decoder error by at most the active mass, with exact accounting when active histories are scored as errors.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Termin.summary: This file defines the terminal envelope, prior entropy and slack, terminal gap, and residual entropy for conditional protocols with retained histories, plus their information-limit versions. It proves the gap equals prior slack plus residual entropy at finite horizons and in the limit, characterizes zero slack by uniform conditional priors, and derives monotone cost bounds: gap thresholds and continuations charge reading cost via local capacity, with zero capacity preserving the envelope.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Termin.boundary: The terminal gap can never fall below prior slack, even with unbounded retained observation, and zero local capacity preserves the full envelope. Reducing the gap past a threshold forces proportional actual reading cost globally, incrementally, and in the information limit.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Termin.conclusion: Terminal gap equals prior slack plus residual entropy and any gap reduction below a threshold demands proportional reading cost, persisting in the information limit.
assumptions: Fintype H0 Z A Y
Nonempty Z for envelope bounds and uniformity characterizations
noncomputable section
no sorry, axiom, or native_decide in code

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Termin.summary: This file gives an explicit log-sum form for uniform relative entropy and identifies it with the envelope-minus-entropy deficit, splitting prior slack and terminal gap into weighted divergences plus residual. It builds concrete conditional protocols such as unit-record, binary reading, zero-signal, perfect-reading, biased-prior, no-reading, and silent-reset laws with exact information, cost, and gap values. It proves telescoping deficit-drop budgets imply only finitely many paid drops above any positive floor, expresses gap drops as retained-continuation information, caps binary local gain by discrimination to price gap reduction, and bounds the optimal fair-menu cost two-sidedly with inverse scaling via repeated protocols.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Termin.boundary: Zero terminal gap requires both uniform conditional priors and zero stopped residual entropy, while the zero-signal control pays unit cost yet keeps gap one and the perfect-reading control pays unit cost to reach gap zero. Any positive payment floor allows only finitely many gap drops, and fair binary gap reduction costs at least order one over discrimination.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Termin.conclusion: The optimal fair binary gap cost scales inversely with discrimination, witnessed by explicit repeat protocols, with only finitely many positively paid drops and a silent reset that erases state entropy without gaining joint information.
assumptions: Fintype H0 Z A Y and paired types W E where used
Nonempty Z for divergence identities and uniformity characterizations
noncomputable section with open Classical
no sorry, axiom, or native_decide in code
#check and #print axioms blocks report dependencies without adding axioms

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Thresh.summary: Defines fiber, class and top weights with a chosen heaviest class, the threshold acceptance predicate, accepted sets, masses and error mass. Proves fiberwise decompositions and error at most (1-tau) times accepted mass with antitone accepted sets. Proves at tau=1 the accepted set equals observerAccepted with refused mass R1-obs, and one-try vulnerability equals summed top weights. Proves at the least top fraction all records are accepted with error equal to the repair frontier R1, illustrated by a fair-pair example.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Thresh.boundary: Larger thresholds accept fewer records with conditional error at most 1-tau; the ends tau=1 with only single-class fibers and least top fraction with all accepted and forced-decision error R1 bound the error-reject curve.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Thresh.conclusion: The threshold rule has conditional error at most 1-tau, equals the observer-measurable refusal at tau=1 and the forced-decision frontier R1 at the least top fraction.
assumptions: Fintype X Q V with DecidableEq Q V and Nonempty V, plus Nonempty X for least fraction
Nonnegative or positive weights where stated
Classical.choice for topClass and decidability of real inequalities
autoImplicit false
No sorry, axiom, native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Transc.summary: This file defines transcript mass at stopped histories, its total, active mass still running, and transcript, active and tail uncertainties. It proves summability, the stopped-mass split, convergence of active mass to escaping mass, and that finite-horizon information equals prior entropy minus transcript and active parts, hence the information-limit formula. Under almost-sure stopping the tail vanishes and the limit equals the mutual information of a normalized countable transcript law, with no-stop and immediately-stopping fair-bit controls showing the stopping boundary.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Transc.boundary: Under almost-sure stopping the tail vanishes and the information limit equals the mutual information of the stopped transcript law. The never-stopping fair-bit protocol has transcript information one, observed information zero and tail one, so stopping separates countable mutual information from a missing bit.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/Transc.conclusion: Under almost-sure stopping the information limit equals the Shannon mutual information of the countable stopped-transcript law, and without stopping the never-stop fair-bit control separates transcript information from observed information.
assumptions: Fintype Z, A, Y with Nonempty Z where stated
summability and uniform-tail premises where stated
almost-sure stopping as vanishing active mass for limit equalities

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/TupleI.summary: This file studies finite tuples under permutations preserving observation classes. It proves a finite partial matching extends to such a permutation, hence a tuple orbit is exactly its pointwise records plus full equality pattern, and invariant functions depend exactly on those data. It contrasts this with independent per-position relabellings, which preserve only pointwise records, showing a shared reference is necessary to preserve equality, with the empty tuple as a trivial case.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/TupleI.boundary: A common invisible relabelling preserves both pointwise records and the equality pattern, while independent per-position relabellings preserve only pointwise records. Preserving equality therefore requires a shared reference.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryObserver/TupleI.conclusion: Finite tuples are classified up to common invisible relabelling by pointwise records plus equality pattern, while independent relabellings see only pointwise records.
assumptions: Fintype I where stated with no finiteness on state space
classical reasoning for DecidableEq inference

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For finite index type I, two tuples are related by a record-preserving permutation exactly when they have equal pointwise records and the same equality pattern.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.BoundaryObserver.TupleInvariants.tuple_invariant_iff
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For finite I, a function is invariant under common invisible relabelling exactly when it depends only on pointwise records and equality pattern.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator.lean.summary: The file defines a boundary-operator record carrying a partial domain, an apply function, gauge data, a channel, payload extraction and cost data together with six proof fields. Its projection theorems restate the six stored laws for any record. It also builds a finite example on Option Bool to Bool with two live inputs collapsing to false and true left without preimage, showing the irreversibility and payload non-recovery laws hold non-vacuously.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator.lean.boundary: A boundary operator is defined on a proper subdomain, has no output with a unique preimage, admits no global payload-recovery map, and charges at least cost_unit * cost_scale * log 2 on live inputs; total domains, uniquely invertible outputs, globally recoverable payloads and sub-floor costs lie on the failing side.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator.lean.conclusion: The file records a six-law boundary-operator structure and exhibits a finite two-input instance satisfying all six laws non-vacuously.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/AxisIn.summary: This file defines two morphism defects for licensed reduction morphisms: state collapse, where distinct source states map to one target state, and edge rejection, where a raw source edge is not admitted. It proves the Bool orientation fixture collapses states but rejects no edge, while the KO7 distinction fixture rejects the diagonal eqW branch but has no state collapse because its map is identity. The conjunction of the four fixture facts gives axis independence of orientation and distinction at the defect level.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/AxisIn.boundary: State collapse holds for orientation but fails for distinction. Edge rejection holds for distinction but fails for orientation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/AxisIn.conclusion: Orientation and distinction are independent morphism defects with opposite collapse and rejection behavior.
assumptions: set_option autoImplicit false

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/Engine.summary: Defines a typed-refusal runtime status pairing a classifier with its support proof, and an engine contract pairing a boundary operator with an optional status. Provides constructors for an empty contract, for adding a generic classifier with its support proof, and for the canonical TypedOutput package. Proves that an advertised status classifies every output inside the refusal support and that both constructors project to such a status.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/Engine.conclusion: Any contract exposing a typed-refusal status advertises a classifier whose values lie in the refusal support for every input.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/LCELP4.summary: This file defines an explicit hypothesis package pairing a runtime engine contract with source and target LCEL instances and a residual package, plus a consequence record with unrestricted-witness admission and witness-free structural identity. It proves the advertised typed-refusal surface remains in refusal support under that package. It proves the LCEL admission and universal-license conclusions follow once the residual obligation is supplied, which the contract does not synthesize alone.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/LCELP4.conclusion: Paired with an explicit residual package, the engine contract yields LCEL unrestricted admission and structural identity without synthesizing the residual itself.

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/Licens.summary: This file defines licensed quotient data with gauge action and projection plus a factorization certificate requiring B apply to factor through projection. It proves the codomain is nonempty and builds a default Option encoding with identity gauge and True license that yields an unconditional factorization certificate for any operator. A finite toy quotient with Z2 action factors the toy boundary operator through a constant false observation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/Licens.boundary: The default encoding separates domain points sent to some from outside-domain points sent to none with distinct observables. Every operator factors through such a quotient, so there is no obstruction to factorization.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/Licens.conclusion: Every boundary operator factors through a licensed quotient via an unconditional default encoding, as illustrated by the toy factorization.
assumptions: classical choice with Classical dot choice and classical tactic for Option encoding
noncomputable definitions
Group typeclass for gauge group

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/Licens.summary: This file defines pointwise agreement of two observation maps on the boundary-operator image and proves any two factorizations agree there because both equal B apply. OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/TRSIns.summary: Lifts a usable-rules concrete route candidate into a confession-core witness and route evidence with projection equalities for core, generic route and forgetting rank. Defines a three-point TRS plug with blocked, direct and shadow inputs, a constant TypedOutput verdict, a Z2 gauge swapping the live points, a runtime channel, payload tags and log-cost, assembled as TRS_BoundaryOperator with proofs of partiality, irreversibility, gauge covariance, channel preservation, payload non-recovery and cost bound. Proves the plug is inhabited, satisfies typed-refusal completeness from the generic TypedOutput completeness theorem, and factors through a one-point licensed quotient.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/TRSIns.boundary: The domain is False on blocked and True on direct and shadow, so blocked lies outside while the live points are inside. The two live inputs map to the same verdict with payload tags that cannot be recovered, so observation factors through a one-point quotient.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/TRSIns.conclusion: The TRS plug is an inhabited boundary operator with typed-refusal completeness and licensed-quotient factorization collapsing two live inputs to one verdict with unrecoverable payload.
assumptions: noncomputable TRS_BoundaryOperator construction

OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/TypedR.summary: This module enumerates four refusal constructors Y N U H and defines support as the universal set, so every value is trivially supported. It packages arbitrary maps into the carrier as classifiers and defines the canonical TypedOutput to refusal map. It proves constructor coverage and classifier codomain typing with completeness for arbitrary and TypedOutput operators and engine-grade exhaustive versions, noting that semantic correctness and disjointness need further predicates.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/TypedR.boundary: Constructor coverage and classifier codomain typing hold universally because support is univ, while semantic classification correctness and disjointness fail without additional predicates.
OperatorKO7/Meta/BoundaryOperator/TypedR.conclusion: Every classifier lands in universal refusal support and every refusal value is one of four constructors, giving completeness for arbitrary and TypedOutput operators.

OperatorKO7/Meta/CoRewritePairBoundary.l.summary: This file does not prove a new barrier theorem; it closes the co-rewrite and co-WPO note using already-landed scope facts. It defines the packed certificate structure CoRewritePairBoundary recording the notes-table status, the out-of-scope co-order fact, and the generalized-WPO compatibility. It proves the residual row coRewritePairCoWPO is classified as nonconservative_escape and that the co-order scope is not in the direct scope. Its final theorem assembles these into co_rewrite_pair_boundary_closed, with a stable string anchor for auditing.
OperatorKO7/Meta/CoRewritePairBoundary.l.boundary: Co-rewrite pairs and co-WPO belong outside the direct orientation lane: they appear only as nonconservative scope escapes requiring the out-of-scope co-order, so they are not direct-lane counterexamples.
OperatorKO7/Meta/CoRewritePairBoundary.l.conclusion: Co-rewrite pairs and co-WPO are closed as mere scope escapes, not loopholes in the direct orientation barrier.

OperatorKO7/Meta/ComparatorNecessity.lea.summary: The file defines an exact total Boolean comparator as a total cmp with soundness and completeness for equality. It proves such a comparator yields DecidableEq by case on cmp, and conversely DecidableEq yields such a comparator via decide. A round-trip lemma shows the construction computes as decide, and a witness gives an ExactComparator on the kernel Trace.
OperatorKO7/Meta/ComparatorNecessity.lea.boundary: A type admits a sound-and-complete total Bool comparator exactly when it has DecidableEq; without DecidableEq no such comparator exists.
OperatorKO7/Meta/ComparatorNecessity.lea.conclusion: An exact total Boolean comparator on W exists exactly when W has decidable equality.

OperatorKO7/Meta/ComparatorNecessityPart.summary: The file defines a sound partial comparator with an abstain value none and decisiveness as never abstaining, plus a Y/N/U verdict and classify map. It proves a decisive sound partial comparator induces an exact total comparator and hence DecidableEq, while DecidableEq yields a decisive sound partial comparator. It shows Y forces equality and N forces disequality, exhibits a decisive witness on Trace, and exhibits always-abstain as sound but not decisive.
OperatorKO7/Meta/ComparatorNecessityPart.boundary: Decisiveness, never abstaining, is the boundary: a decisive sound three-valued comparator gives DecidableEq, while a merely sound comparator need not, witnessed by always-abstain.
OperatorKO7/Meta/ComparatorNecessityPart.conclusion: A sound three-valued comparator yields decidable equality exactly when it is decisive; soundness alone does not suffice.
assumptions: Decisive P required for the forward bridge to ExactComparator and DecidableEq
DecidableEq W required for the reverse construction
OperatorKO7.Trace has DecidableEq from the kernel
No sorry, axiom, native_decide or redefinition; ExactComparator and DecidableEq are reused

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Predicate on P : SoundPartialComparator W stating forall a b, (P.pcmp a b).isSome, i.e. P never abstains.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Given P : SoundPartialComparator W and hP : Decisive P, there is an ExactComparator W with cmp := getD false; soundness uses sound_pos and completeness uses decisiveness plus sound_neg.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.ComparatorNecessityPartial.decisive_decidableEq
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Given P and hP : Decisive P, W has DecidableEq by reusing exactComparator_decidableEq on decisive_exactComparator P hP.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Given W with DecidableEq W, there is a SoundPartialComparator W with pcmp a b := some (decide (a = b)), positive soundness by of_decide_eq_true and negative soundness by of_decide_eq_false.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.ComparatorNecessityPartial.classify
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Function Option Bool -> Verdict sending some true to Y, some false to N, and none to U.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.ComparatorNecessityPartial.classify_exhaustive
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every o : Option Bool, either classify o = Y and o = some true, or classify o = N and o = some false, or classify o = U and o = none.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.ComparatorNecessityPartial.classify_no_ne
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Given sound P : SoundPartialComparator W and a b : W, if classify (P.pcmp a b) = N then a != b by sound_neg.
