OperatorKO7/Meta/LinearRec_Ablation.lean.summary: This file defines a non-duplicating linear recursor step and the additive node-count measure simpleSize. It proves simpleSize strictly orients both linear rules and hence well-foundedness of the linear step relation. It proves by explicit witness that the same measure does not orient the duplicating successor rule, establishing only this contrast.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LinearRec_Ablation.lean.boundary: Additive node count succeeds on the linear recursor side but fails on the duplicating side, witnessed by void and app void void where the right-hand side is larger. Duplication is shown as a contrast, not as the sole cause of every barrier.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LinearRec_Ablation.lean.conclusion: Simple node count terminates the linear recursor but cannot orient the duplicating recursor.

OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Dynami.summary: The file defines independent pair reductions, a modal Box for persistence, separated and kernel predicates, the off-diagonal observer boundary, reachability and coalescence. It proves that persistent separation is separation of all independent reducts and that its complement is reachability of the kernel, split into diagonal coalescence and boundary collisions. Two counterexamples show a diagonal outside Box without separation or boundary reachability, and a coalescing separated pair without boundary reachability.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Dynami.boundary: Separation persists on one side when all independent reducts keep distinct observations. It fails on the other side when reducts can be driven to equal observations, either by coalescing to a common reduct or by reaching distinct points with equal observations.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Dynami.conclusion: Persistent separation holds for all independent reducts together, and its failure is joint reachability of equal observations split into coalescence or boundary reachability.
assumptions: arbitrary types alpha beta
arbitrary rewrite relation r and observation q
ReflTransGen from Relation, Join for coalescence
classical tactic used locally for set complements
no sorry, axiom or native_decide in code

OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Estima.summary: The file defines finite differentiable experiments passed through a stochastic channel, input and record scores and Fisher informations, variances, residuals and conditional variances, and split scores. It proves Fisher loss equals state minus record information, monotonicity, a record Cramer-Rao product bound under a derivative-one hypothesis, and strictness of the reciprocal floor at shared outputs with different scores, with a deterministic fiber specialization.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Estima.boundary: Lossless transmission holds when no shared output carries different scores, while a shared output with different scores forces recordInfo < stateInfo and a positive reciprocal gap. The deterministic specialization replaces split scores by fiber collisions with different scores.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Estima.conclusion: Record information never exceeds state information with gap equal to expected conditional variance, gives the Cramer-Rao product bound, and is strict in the reciprocal bound if and only if split scores occur.
assumptions: open neighborhood of theta
forall x, 0 < law theta x
output alphabet restricted to attained support with positive q
HasDerivAt (expectation M a) 1 theta for Cramer-Rao lemmas
derivative-one hypothesis suffices without unbiasedness
noncomputable section, autoImplicit false, no sorry or axiom

OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Finite.summary: The file builds finite Hermitian linear algebra in coordinates, conjugated diagonals, spectral projections and weights, and the scalar resolvent with its Stieltjes sum form. It proves holomorphicity on the upper half-plane, nonnegative imaginary part, and reciprocal-height lower bounds at spectral atoms. It concludes that a nonzero vector and positive scalar preclude any vertically bounded representation on unit segments.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Finite.boundary: Holomorphic Stieltjes behavior with nonnegative imaginary part holds on the upper half-plane, while boundedness on every vertical unit segment fails at any spectral atom carrying positive weight for a nonzero vector.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Finite.conclusion: A finite Hermitian resolvent is holomorphic with nonnegative imaginary part and reciprocal-height atom bounds, so no positive multiple admits a vertically bounded representation for nonzero vectors.
assumptions: H.IsHermitian
v != 0 for atom and no-go parts
0 < c and 0 < epsilon and 0 < z.im
local DecidableEq Real via Classical.decEq
noncomputable section, no sorry or axiom

OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/GcdKer.summary: The file defines the square grid, Jordan totient counts, normalized gcd kernel, finitely supported coefficient vectors in complex square-summable sequences, and the based kernel and vectors with quadratic forms. OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/GcdKer.conclusion: The normalized squared-gcd kernel has a finitely supported Jordan-totient Gram realization with nonnegative quadratic forms, and subtracting the feature at one gives the based kernel vanishing at one.

OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Hetero.summary: The file defines finite rows, binary entropy, cell and gap informations, discrimination, biases with kappa bounds, BSC rows, Bayes and decoder errors, Bhattacharyya coefficients, finite tree experiments and protocols with acquired information and total cost, product rows and bias means. It proves acquired-cost bounds, adaptive squared-bias bounds, product error and eta-threshold information bounds for eta <= 1/2 with an eta = 1 counterexample, and a variance identity with constant-equality characterization.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Hetero.boundary: Acquired information stays below expected discrimination cost on one side, while eta = 1 violates the independent-reading threshold on the other side. Squared-bias sums meet the mean lower bound with equality if and only if biases are constant.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Hetero.conclusion: Acquired information is bounded by expected discrimination and adaptive squared-bias sums, independent readings have product-BC error and information thresholds, and squared-bias means are tight with equality for constant biases.
assumptions: finite real mass functions with Fintype
finite decision trees retaining all random choices and outcomes
arbitrary conditional priors in protocols
0 < eta <= 1/2 for Fano and independent-reading bounds
fair label with conditional independence for independent information
positive number of readings for mean bounds
classical used for product square-roots

OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/MagicS.summary: The file defines 3 by 3 integer tables, six row and column demands, and when a table satisfies a demand. It proves no integer table satisfies all six demands because row products force 1 while column targets force -1. It gives explicit plus-or-minus-one witness tables that satisfy all but any one omitted demand, showing every five-demand subset is realizable and the full set is a minimal obstruction. It also defines finite common laws and proves no finite family of tables admits a distribution giving each demand probability one.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/MagicS.boundary: The full six-demand set is not realizable while every proper subset is realizable; the threshold is five versus six. No finite family of tables admits a common probability law giving all six demands probability one.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/MagicS.conclusion: The six demands form a minimal obstruction with no finite common law giving them all probability one.
assumptions: Integer tables for the impossibility part
Signed tables with values 1 or -1 for witnesses and realizability
Finite type Omega with Fintype for the common-law part

OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Matchi.summary: The file defines a two-place copy model with left and right places, a place-to-role equivalence, and a copy isomorphism identifying pairs with content-role occurrences. It proves the isomorphism is bijective, unique for preserving content and place kernels, and transports separating side-records. It exhibits literal copied subtrees in equality and recursion traces with injective paths, and identifies the positional dependency-pair flag with a callee-subtree test. It proves the flag cannot be factored through content alone and the content-disequality guard is false on both copy pairs.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Matchi.boundary: Content alone cannot separate the two copies: no Boolean function of content alone equals the positional flag on both roles, so role and place information is necessary. The content-disequality guard is constantly false on each fixed-content fiber.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Matchi.conclusion: The role bijection uniquely identifies matching and duplication occurrences, preserves separation and literal subtrees, and the positional flag separates independently of content.

OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/PickKe.summary: The file defines quadratic forms, positive kernels, Schur complements, the Pick kernel on the upper half-plane, finite Stieltjes transforms, feature vectors and Stieltjes approximability. It proves Gram positivity, preservation of positivity under pointwise limits, Schur positivity with zero base rows, Pick diagonal and sign facts, and the finite Stieltjes Gram and rational-sum formulas. The main theorems give holomorphicity and Pick positivity for finite Stieltjes transforms and the sign, diagonal and Schur conclusions for their pointwise limits.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/PickKe.boundary: The analytic forward direction is proved only for finite Stieltjes transforms and their pointwise limits, because no reusable Nevanlinna-Pick theorem was located; the full holomorphic forward implication is not asserted. The diagonal, kernel-limit and Schur statements hold without that restriction.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/PickKe.conclusion: Every Stieltjes-approximable function has nonnegative imaginary part, positive Pick kernel, explicit diagonal and Schur complements with zero base rows.
assumptions: Upper half-plane domain
Nonnegative Stieltjes weights
NeBot filters with Tendsto for limits
Stieltjes approximability for the main equivalence
Noncomputable definitions

OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/TypedR.summary: The file defines priors, transcript rows, kernels, pointwise and summed error masses, and conditional pair error for definite decision rules. It proves that distinct answers with identical conditional rows force pair error at least the smaller prior, with positivity and conditional bounds, and that pair mass and total error are bounded by one. It proves a constant report of the more probable answer attains the bound and the bound is least.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/TypedR.boundary: If two hidden values have distinct answers but identical transcript rows, every definite report incurs pair error at least the smaller prior. Without distinct answers or identical rows the forced error need not hold.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/TypedR.conclusion: Identical transcript laws for distinct answers force pair error at least the smaller prior, attained by constantly reporting the more probable answer.
assumptions: Finite hidden carrier with Fintype
DecidableEq answers
Nonnegative summable transcript masses
Definite answers with no refusal symbol
Positive pair mass for the conditional bound
Prior already conditioned on retained history

OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Uncont.summary: The file defines subrelations, invariance, the box of states with reachable states in the permitted set, safe and controllable edges, and stable and maximal repairs. It proves the box is the greatest invariant subpredicate and maximal repairs are exactly pairs in normal form with all safe edges over the box domain. It proves every uncontrollable subrelation yields such a maximal partition with edge and path comparisons, including fully and never uncontrollable cases.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Uncont.boundary: Maximality holds exactly in normal form retaining all safe edges over the box domain; merely stable repairs need not be maximal and arbitrary edge sets fail invariance.
OperatorKO7/Meta/LiteratureReview/Uncont.conclusion: Maximal stable repairs are exactly safe restrictions to box domains of uncontrollable subrelations.
assumptions: Arbitrary state type
Predicates as sets
Reflexive transitive closure reachability
Full state observation and edge control in the supervisory interpretation

OperatorKO7/Meta/MPO_FullStep.lean.summary: Defines a KO7-specific multiset path order over Trace with fixed symbol precedence and subterm, precedence and same-head recΔ counter clauses. Proves each of the eight root Step rules MPO-oriented, with a master theorem that every Step is oriented. Defines a Veblen-based ordinal ranking and shows MPO steps strictly decrease it, yielding well-foundedness of reverse MPO and of reverse root Step.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MPO_FullStep.lean.boundary: With the fixed rank order void < delta < merge < integrate < app < eqW < recΔ, every root Step is MPO-oriented and strictly decreases the Veblen rank, yielding termination; the file proves only this positive side, with failure under altered precedence shown elsewhere.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MPO_FullStep.lean.conclusion: Every root Step is MPO-oriented and ordinal-decreasing, so reverse Step is well-founded.

OperatorKO7/Meta/MPO_Precedence_Barrier..summary: Keeps the same KO7 MPO shape but swaps precedence so app is above recΔ. Defines the smallest concrete rec_succ source and target. Proves by case analysis that no bad-MPO derivation exists for the void and delta-void prefixes and hence for that rec_succ instance, so no global root-step orientation exists under this precedence.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MPO_Precedence_Barrier..boundary: When app is placed above recΔ, the duplicating rec_succ rule already fails on the smallest concrete instance, so no MPO with that precedence can orient all root steps.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MPO_Precedence_Barrier..conclusion: Under app above recΔ, the KO7 MPO cannot orient all root steps.

OperatorKO7/Meta/MPO_ProofTheoreticBound.summary: Introduces the explicit ordinal envelope veblen 7 0 for the fixed-signature MPO ranking and proves every mpoOrd lies below it. Witnesses root-step termination by a ranking into that initial segment. Defines gamma0 as the least fixed point of a => veblen a 0, identifies it with Mathlib gamma 0, and shows veblen 7 0 < gamma0, so the MPO proof stays below the Feferman-Schütte ordinal.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MPO_ProofTheoreticBound.boundary: The MPO ranking is confined below φ₇(0) and hence below the Feferman-Schütte ordinal Γ₀, giving an explicit upper bound on the proof strength of this fixed-signature termination argument.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MPO_ProofTheoreticBound.conclusion: All MPO ranks lie below φ₇(0) < Γ₀ with strict decrease along every root step.

OperatorKO7/Meta/ManySortedBarrierSurviv.summary: Repackages the typed recursor barrier as a many-sorted first-order presentation without formalizing a general Aoto-Yamada translation. Defines sorts, terms, iterator and additive and affine measures as abbreviations of the typed versions. Proves the additive barrier and the affine barrier under a step-pump survive unchanged in the many-sorted reading.
OperatorKO7/Meta/ManySortedBarrierSurviv.boundary: Additive measures, and affine measures when the step sort admits an unbounded pump, cannot make the wrap of the recursor smaller than the recursor at the successor; this impossibility survives the many-sorted reading.
OperatorKO7/Meta/ManySortedBarrierSurviv.conclusion: Both additive and pump-backed affine barriers survive as many-sorted barriers.
assumptions: step-pump hypothesis HasManySortedStepPump for the affine case; no axioms, sorry or choice

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrier2.lean.summary: Specializes the tracked first-component dimension-2 barrier to KO7. Gives three theorems for unbounded first-component range, successor pump and wrap pump. Each reduces global Step orientation to the duplicating rec_succ step and applies the generic schema barrier.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrier2.lean.boundary: If the tracked first component is unbounded or satisfies succ/wrap positivity, no dimension-2 componentwise measure can orient all KO7 steps; the duplicating rec_succ step is the obstruction.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrier2.lean.conclusion: No tracked 2D componentwise measure orients all KO7 steps under the stated pumps.
assumptions: HasUnboundedRange1 M for componentwise version
1 ≤ succ_bias1 and 1 ≤ succ_scale1 for succ-pump version
1 ≤ wrap_const1 + wrap_right1 * c_base1 for wrap-pump version

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Given M with 1 ≤ succ_bias1 and 1 ≤ succ_scale1, it is false that all Steps strictly decrease in PairLt.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.MatrixBarrier2.no_global_step_orientation_matrix2_of_wrap_pump
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Given M with 1 ≤ wrap_const1 + wrap_right1 * c_base1, it is false that all Steps strictly decrease in PairLt.

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrier2_Schema.l.summary: Defines dimension-2 componentwise affine measures where each coordinate is scalar affine, with projections and unbounded-range predicates. Proves first- and second-component affine failures each rule out componentwise pair orientation of the duplicating step. Gives successor-pump and wrap-pump corollaries and lifts the tracked barrier to global root orientation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrier2_Schema.l.boundary: If one tracked affine component already cannot decrease on the duplicating step via unboundedness or pumps, then strict componentwise pair decrease and hence global orientation are impossible.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrier2_Schema.l.conclusion: Tracked-component affine failure rules out 2D componentwise orientation of the duplicating and global steps.
assumptions: unbounded tracked range for main barrier
wrapper positivity built into MatrixMeasure2
succ bias/scale ≥1 or wrap bias ≥1 for pump corollaries

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierArbitrary..summary: Specializes the arbitrary mixed-matrix scalar-dominance barrier to KO7. Assuming an explicit weight, a dominance certificate linking the ambient order to scalarization, and unbounded scalarized range, no global orientation of the KO7 system exists.

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierArbitrary_.summary: Defines unit and all-ones weights with scalarization lemmas. Proves fixed-row and equal-column-sum certificates for RespectsWeight. Derives fixed-row/unit and row-sum/all-ones instances of the arbitrary scalarization barrier for the duplicating step and wraps them to KO7 global orientation barriers.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierArbitrary_.boundary: With unit fixed-row or all-ones row-sum scalarization and unbounded scalarized range, tracked or pointwise strict orientation of the duplicating step and KO7 global orientation are impossible.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierArbitrary_.conclusion: Fixed-row/unit and row-sum/all-ones scalarizations cannot orient the duplicating or global steps when unbounded.
assumptions: weight equals unit or all-ones
unbounded scalarized range

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierArbitrary_.summary: Defines finite natural vectors, scalarization, full mixed matrices with weight-respect laws, and arbitrary measures with explicit scalarization witnesses. Projects each such measure to a scalar affine measure. Proves that unboundedness plus scalar dominance of the ambient order rules out orientation of the duplicating step and global orientation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierArbitrary_.boundary: Whenever the full matrix action scalarizes to an unbounded affine measure and the ambient order is nonincreasing in that scalarization, orientation of the duplicating step and global orientation are impossible.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierArbitrary_.conclusion: Explicitly scalarizable mixed-matrix measures cannot orient the duplicating or global steps under dominance and unboundedness.
assumptions: RespectsWeight laws for all constructors
wrapper scale positivity
unbounded scalarized range
dominance nonincreasing law

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierArcticNatu.summary: Lifts the certificate-free arctic barrier through system, KO7 and full one-hole context layers in nonincreasing, strict and pump-free strict forms. Exhibits a one-dimensional bot-right arctic interpretation that strictly orients the duplicating step, proving finiteness load-bearing. Gives a trace-weight size interpretation with positive wrapper diagonals that is blocked at both root and context layers.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierArcticNatu.boundary: Finite and for nonincreasing comparison positive wrapper diagonals make tracked arctic orientation of root and context-closed steps impossible, while a bot right diagonal strictly orients the duplicating step, so finiteness is sharp.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierArcticNatu.conclusion: Arctic barriers lift to KO7 and full context, and the bot diagonal is a sharp escape.
assumptions: finite positive wrapper diagonals for nonincreasing/strict forms
finite diagonals only for pump-free strict form
finite coordinate value for nonincreasing form
order implies ArcticLe/Lt on tracked coordinate

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierArcticNatu.summary: Develops arctic max-plus order, vectors, matrices and weight-free interpretations with positive versus finite diagonal predicates. Proves nonincreasing, strict and pump-free strict barriers by colliding wrapper-chain growth with a counter-matrix bound. Gives a finite-or-bot dichotomy and a constant fin-0 measure showing positivity is load-bearing for the nonincreasing form.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierArcticNatu.boundary: Positive finite wrapper diagonals block nonincreasing tracked orientation and finite diagonals block strict tracked orientation; with all-zero diagonals nonstrict orientation holds and with bot it can orient strictly, so the premises cannot be dropped.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierArcticNatu.conclusion: Tracked arctic orientation is impossible under the stated diagonal and order premises, and the premises are sharp.
assumptions: positive finite diagonals for nonincreasing form
finite diagonals for pump-free strict form
finite coordinate value where required
order implies ArcticLe/Lt on tracked coordinate

unbounded tracked range or succ/wrap pumps

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierFunctional.summary: This file defines a finite-dimensional matrix-style measure through an explicit natural-weighted scalar projection with affine laws. It proves that strict componentwise decrease cannot orient the duplicating step when the weighted projection is unbounded or admits successor or wrapper pumps. It shows the tracked-coordinate and balanced mixed-coordinate families are instances of this functional barrier via singleton and all-ones weights.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierFunctional.boundary: An unbounded weighted scalar projection, or a successor or wrapper pump on it, rules out strict componentwise orientation of the duplicating step; without such unboundedness or pump the barrier does not apply.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierFunctional.conclusion: No weighted affine matrix measure with unbounded projection, or with a successor or wrapper pump, can strictly orient the duplicating step componentwise, and the tracked-coordinate and balanced mixed-coordinate families inherit this barrier.
assumptions: nonzero weight support (exists i, 1 <= weight i)
wrapper coefficients 1 <= wrap_left and 1 <= wrap_right
unbounded weighted range or successor/wrap pump hypotheses
classical reasoning in weightedSum_lt_of_vecLt proof

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierLexD_Schem.summary: This module generalizes the tracked-primary lexicographic barrier from dimension 2 to arbitrary fixed finite dimension. It defines the primary index and lexicographic order, shows lexicographic decrease forces primary nonincrease, and projects the primary coordinate to the scalar affine barrier. It proves unbounded-primary, successor-pump, wrapper-pump, strengthened internal-pump, and global no-orientation theorems.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierLexD_Schem.boundary: A primary coordinate that can be pumped arbitrarily high forces a strict primary increase on the duplicating step and hence rules out lexicographic decrease; bounded primary behavior lies on the other side.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierLexD_Schem.conclusion: No finite tracked-primary lexicographic measure with unbounded or pumped primary coordinate can orient the duplicating step, hence no such system is globally oriented lexicographically.
assumptions: wrap coefficients at least 1
unbounded primary range or successor pump with both parameters at least 1 or wrapper pump with 1 <= wrap_const plus wrap_right times c_base

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierLexPermD_S.summary: This module proves conditional barriers for lexicographic vector orders after a supplied coordinate permutation. It projects that coordinate to the affine barrier and derives unbounded-primary, successor-pump, wrapper-pump, strengthened internal-pump, and global theorems.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierLexPermD_S.boundary: An unbounded or pumped permuted-primary coordinate rules out permuted lexicographic orientation; the capped versions show finite diagonal plus finite retained sibling data also suffice to block orientation.

finite right or left diagonal or wrapper bias for capped versions

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierMix2_Schem.summary: This module proves a conditional barrier for a balanced two-coordinate mixed projection. It defines coordinate sums, balanced 2x2 maps, and a mixed affine measure whose sum projection is affine. It shows strict pair decrease forces strict sum decrease and derives sum-pump duplicating-step and global no-orientation theorems from the scalar affine barrier.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierMix2_Schem.boundary: An unbounded coordinate sum blocks strict pair orientation of the duplicating step, while bounded sums escape this barrier.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierMix2_Schem.conclusion: No balanced mixed-coordinate measure with unbounded coordinate sum can orient the duplicating step under strict pair order, hence none globally orients its system.
assumptions: balanced 2x2 coefficient maps
positive wrap sum coefficients
unbounded coordinate-sum range

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierNatural.le.summary: This module instantiates the certificate-free natural-matrix barrier at KO7 for strict tracked, nonincreasing, componentwise, EWZ, and lexicographic orders. It proves a unit-weight certificate implies wrapper-diagonal positivity, hence the certificate-free barrier applies. It supplies a one-dimensional size witness and a two-dimensional mixed witness whose wrapper matrices share no nonzero weight, separating the certificate-free barrier from all certificate-backed barriers.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierNatural.le.boundary: Positive wrapper diagonals alone block strict tracked orders, while merely nonincreasing orders need one positive coordinate value; the mixed two-dimensional witness lies inside the certificate-free barrier but outside every certificate-backed barrier.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierNatural.le.conclusion: Positive wrapper diagonals block all tracked strict and, with one positive value, nonincreasing orders without certificates or pumps, and the mixed witness separates this barrier from every certificate-backed barrier.
assumptions: positive wrapper diagonal entries at the tracked coordinate
one positive value of the tracked coordinate for merely nonincreasing orders
no weight vector, certificate, pump or positivity premise for strict orders beyond the diagonal

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierNatural_EW.summary: This file shows EWZ strict monotonicity forces positive wrapper diagonals, so the certificate-free natural-matrix barrier applies with no extra premise. It proves duplicating-step and global failures under EWZ, componentwise, and positive lexicographic orders. It compiles the zero-diagonal interpretation as a non-example where nonstrict comparison holds but EWZ monotonicity and diagonal positivity fail.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierNatural_EW.boundary: EWZ monotonicity of every constructor matrix forces wrapper-diagonal positivity and hence blocks EWZ, componentwise and lexicographic orientation, while the zero-diagonal interpretation shows monotonicity is load-bearing.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierNatural_EW.conclusion: Every EWZ-monotone natural matrix interpretation fails the duplicating step under EWZ, componentwise and positive lexicographic orders, and the zero interpretation shows the diagonal hypothesis cannot be dropped.

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierNatural_Sc.summary: This schema proves a certificate-free, dimension-uniform natural-matrix barrier over Nat. It defines NatMatrixMeasure and wrapper-diagonal positivity and shows the wrapper dominates argument coordinates. It proves unconditional failure for orders forcing strict tracked decrease and conditional failure with one positive value for merely nonincreasing orders. It instantiates componentwise, EWZ, lexicographic, priority, Pareto, cone, and norm orders and their global forms.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierNatural_Sc.boundary: Positive wrapper diagonals block every order forcing strict tracked decrease unconditionally, and block merely nonincreasing orders once one positive coordinate value exists; without that positive value nonincreasing orientation may survive.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierNatural_Sc.conclusion: Positive wrapper diagonals alone rule out all tracked-strict orders and, with one positive value, all tracked-nonincreasing orders without certificates or pumps.
assumptions: WrapDiagPositive at the tracked coordinate for both wrapper matrices
one positive value of the tracked coordinate for merely nonincreasing orders
no weight vector, certificate or pump

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierOrderedFie.summary: This schema lifts the natural-matrix barrier to nonnegative elements of ordered semirings. It defines field vectors, matrices and measures with nonnegativity, proves wrapper lower bounds, boundedness under nonincrease, strict boundedness with cancellation, doubling along wrapper chains, and Archimedean unboundedness. It gives unbounded, Archimedean positive, and unconditional strict barriers, shows positivity is necessary via a zero evaluation with unit diagonals, and coerces Nat measures to NNRat and NNReal.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierOrderedFie.boundary: Positive wrapper diagonals block strict tracked orientation unconditionally, while merely nonincreasing orientation needs Archimedean plus one positive value; the zero evaluation shows positivity is necessary for the nonincreasing form.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierOrderedFie.conclusion: Positive wrapper diagonals block strict tracked matrix orientation over ordered semirings unconditionally and block nonincreasing orientation under Archimedean positivity, with NNRat and NNReal instances by coercion.
assumptions: CommSemiring with PartialOrder and IsStrictOrderedRing on K
Archimedean for the merely nonincreasing version
nonnegative entries and evaluations
FieldWrapDiagPositive with both wrapper (i,i) entries at least 1
positive tracked value for nonincreasing form; unbounded range variant needs explicit unboundedness

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierTropicalCo.summary: This file proves a tropical context obstruction for min-plus matrix interpretations. It defines the wrapper-context closure, canonical chains and stages, and finite tropical caps, then shows a strict right step forces a finite right contribution that bounds all left contributions against arbitrarily long recursor runs. It derives universal, finite-bias, and finite-cap no-go theorems, transfers them to free syntax and full KO7 contexts, exhibits the root-versus-context split, and classifies which wrapper-congruence policies remain orientable by one-sided measures.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierTropicalCo.boundary: Every tropical matrix interpretation orients root duplicating rules but none strictly orients their wrapper-context closure; retaining one wrapper congruence can restore orientability, as the one-sided classification shows.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierTropicalCo.conclusion: No tropical matrix interpretation strictly orients the wrapper-context closure, while root orientation exists and one-sided wrapper policies are exactly those that remain orientable.
assumptions: no finite diagonal or supplied bound for the universal context theorem
finite right diagonal plus finite retained sibling value, or finite wrapper bias, or finite left cap for capped versions

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierTropicalNa.summary: This file defines the tropical natural semiring, vectors, matrices and their min-plus action, plus tropical matrix interpretations of step-duplicating schemas. It proves the diagonal entry is an upper bound for the action, reversing the lower-bound pump used over natural and arctic semirings. It compiles an explicit one-dimensional witness with positive wrapper diagonals that strictly orients the root duplicating step, killing the certificate-free tropical barrier, and shows the witness lacks scalar dominance and fails wrapper-context compatibility.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierTropicalNa.boundary: Over the natural and arctic semirings the wrapper diagonal gives a lower bound that pumps to a barrier, while over the tropical semiring it gives only an upper bound so the pump fails; the witness orients every root duplicating step but no wrapper-context closure of that step.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixBarrierTropicalNa.conclusion: The certificate-free tropical matrix barrier is false via an explicit one-dimensional orienting witness that does not extend to wrapper contexts.
assumptions: No sorry, axiom, native_decide or classical choice in the code.
Main orientation claim assumes positive finite wrapper diagonal entries and a finite tracked coordinate.

It proves projection payloads saying each weak-monotone family scalarizes for every weight and the scalarizable family carries its own dominance certificate. It also records that import-dependent matrices are licensed escapes and the unconstrained relation is not yet a method class.

OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixUnrestrictedSplit.summary: This acyclic core splits the unconstrained matrix surface into six certificate kinds with structural carriers for row-column, cone, norm and non-scalarizable orders. It proves per-kind unconditional payloads by scalarization or licensed arctic and tropical barriers, plus unique classification of every relation. The headline bundles exact six-kind enumeration, per-kind closure and unique classification.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixUnrestrictedSplit.boundary: The previously open unconstrained matrix surface splits exhaustively into six kinds, each unconditionally closed, leaving no open residual.
OperatorKO7/Meta/MatrixUnrestrictedSplit.conclusion: Every matrix relation classifies uniquely into six unconditionally closed certificate kinds.
assumptions: No axiom, sorry or classical choice in the code; the header states the core is theorem-only.
Scalarizable closure reuses stored dominance; row, cone and norm closures assume weak monotonicity.
Arctic and tropical closures assume weight, scalarize and unbounded-range hypotheses.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/AdmittanceInapp.summary: This file defines counter depth, matched and recursive counters, the strict-subterm relation and admittance predicates for ten ledger rows. It proves the recursive call is the strict predecessor with smaller depth and that the subterm relation is well founded. It anchors five admittance rows for HORPO, CPO, general schema, sized types and Coq guard, two typing-barrier rows for linear logic and ramified recursion, and abstraction, size-change and infinitary rows.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/AdmittanceInapp.boundary: Structural-descent criteria admit the duplicating recursor because the recursive counter strictly descends, whereas linear and ramified resource disciplines reject it because the payload count grows from 1 to 2.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/AdmittanceInapp.conclusion: Every structural-descent definitional criterion admits the duplicating recursor, while no resource-sound linear or ramified typing admits it, and the full contextual relation is well founded with no infinite reduction.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/AlgebraicInterp.summary: This file defines affine, truncated, max, bounded polynomial, multilinear, natural and ordered-field matrix, arctic and tropical, triangular, tuple and Archimedean measures with fourteen row claims. It proves none of those classes orient the duplicating step under the stated dominance, monotonicity or projection premises. It compiles cross-coupled orienting witnesses showing the premises are load-bearing and that the certificate-free tropical strengthening is false.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/AlgebraicInterp.boundary: Affine, truncated, max, dominated polynomial and multilinear, monotone matrix and affine-projection tuple methods cannot orient the duplicating step, while unrestricted cross-coupled witnesses outside those classes can. For tropical matrices the primary-projection block is unconditional but the wider certificate-free block is false.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/AlgebraicInterp.conclusion: No member of the listed algebraic classes orients the duplicating step, with dominance and affine-projection premises proved load-bearing by explicit orienting counterexamples.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/DependencyPairT.summary: This file defines the counter-projection core, reduction pairs and triples, formative and neutral processors, typed and order-sorted transports, context-sensitive closures, rule-schema catalogs and constrained encodings. It proves the single extracted pair decreases in counter depth and discharges every dependency-pair row. It proves unconditionality collapses conditional and two-dimensional notions and that no Bellantoni-Cook tier assignment is admissible.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/DependencyPairT.boundary: Counter-projection decrease yields termination for all dependency-pair, typed, order-sorted, context-sensitive and constrained variants, whereas the Bellantoni-Cook safe and normal split admits no tier assignment because payload duplication violates the resource inequality.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/DependencyPairT.conclusion: The single counter-decreasing dependency pair discharges all dependency-pair and typed rows and conditional variants collapse to the unconditional case, while no Bellantoni-Cook tier assignment can accommodate the duplicating rule.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/DiagonalForkSch.summary: This file defines the generic diagonal-fork schema, its smallest three-element inhabitant and three extension predicates for equality query, injective pairing and infinite carrier. It proves the tiny fork lacks all three, so the bare schema forces none of them. It proves KO7 traces supply infinite generation and injective merge pairing while the guarded relation supplies the parameterized equality query, combined in one fence theorem.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/DiagonalForkSch.boundary: A bare diagonal fork supplies two distinct exits but does not force an equality query, injective pairing or infinite carrier, whereas KO7 syntax plus its guarded equality rules does supply all three.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/DiagonalForkSch.conclusion: The generic diagonal-fork schema does not force equality, pairing or infinity, while KO7 realizes all three, as recorded once in the fence theorem.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/ExactPromotionC.summary: This file defines six closed singleton carriers for counter-only filtering, neutral processing, single-call size-change, guarded Cichon bounds, merge-commutativity quotient and shared-node substrate. It proves each inhabitant equals the existing KO7 object and satisfies an exact certificate with load-bearing graph, rank and nonconservativity facts. It proves filtering and size-change ranks coincide as functions with the common dependency-pair confession core.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/ExactPromotionC.boundary: Each closed method has exactly one KO7 inhabitant that certifies, while sharing and quotient rows mark substrate limits because read-back is non-injective, shared size does not factor through read-back and merge commutativity identifies distinct root-normal forms.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/ExactPromotionC.conclusion: Every closed exact carrier is the concrete KO7 method and satisfies its certificate, with filtering and size-change ranks equal to the common dependency-pair projection.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrderedMatrixIn.summary: This file defines delta-margin comparison, field matrix operations and ordered matrix methods with genuinely field coefficients. It proves margin preservation is equivalent to a diagonal of at least one and well-foundedness via natural floor. It proves no such method orients the duplicating step, with scaled size and fractional instances showing genuine field use.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrderedMatrixIn.boundary: Every ordered-field matrix method with positive margin and diagonal at least one fails to orient the duplicating step, even though scaled and genuinely fractional instances exist.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrderedMatrixIn.conclusion: No ordered-field matrix interpretation with the stated monotonicity orients the duplicating step over the rationals or reals.
assumptions: Field K
LinearOrder K
IsStrictOrderedRing K
FloorSemiring K for well-foundedness
NeZero d for positive dimension
0 < delta for strict margin

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file studies two ablations of the step-duplicating free syntax. It defines tree size and a non-duplicating recursor rule, proving tree size strictly decreases and its reverse is well founded. It defines a payload-blind counter projection that orients the original duplicating successor yet fails wrapper left-sensitivity. The final theorem packages the independence of payload duplication and payload sensitivity.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Without payload duplication ordinary tree size strictly decreases on both root rules. With duplication retained, tree size can increase, while a payload-blind counter still orients successors but fails wrapper left-sensitivity.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Payload duplication and payload sensitivity are independent obligations, with size descent available only after removing duplication and orientation available from a payload-blind counter that is not wrapper-sensitive.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file builds concrete native interpretations for the algebraic rows previously stated only as row propositions. It defines truncated-debt, max, bounded-polynomial, multilinear, ordered-field matrix, higher-order tuple, Archimedean and finite Arctic measures with non-triviality controls. Each concrete method is shown to be blocked from uniform duplicator orientation by the corresponding universal barrier. Two-sided polynomial and multilinear boundary witnesses pair an inside member with a cross-coupled orienter outside, and all data are packaged in a capstone bundle.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Each inhabitant meets its row activeness or nonconstancy premise yet is blocked from uniform duplicator orientation. The polynomial, multilinear and Arctic witnesses mark an inside versus outside boundary where the dominated or finite-diagonal member is blocked while a cross-coupled or diagonal-violating member orients.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: All ten algebraic rows receive concrete native method data with activeness controls, universal barriers blocking uniform orientation, and a capstone bundle pairing each blocked inhabitant with its boundary escape where one exists.
assumptions: noncomputable definitions for orderedFieldMatrixFamily and algebraicNativeBundle, using classical choice
no sorry, axiom or native_decide visible

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file defines counter and payload observations and closed towers realizing every natural value. It proves every counter, payload and positive increment occurs as an actual successor root step at every variable type via a closed embedding that preserves both observations and root steps. Orientation of successors by a profile is then equivalent to the numeric duplicating-step condition, hence carrier-independent, with payload blindness as a consequence.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: A profile measure orients all successor instances at a carrier exactly when its numeric function satisfies the duplicating-step condition. Orientation is thus carrier-independent, and every orienting successor profile is payload-blind.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Every counter, payload and positive increment occurs as a successor profile at every carrier, so successor orientation is equivalent to the numeric duplicating-step condition and is carrier-independent.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file defines a pure-power test and an exact polynomial checker for certificates of the free recursor. It proves that a natural-coefficient interpretation is strictly monotone in every argument exactly when each argument has a positive pure-power monomial, and that the exact checker accepts exactly the unit-slope interpretations that orient both root rules and satisfy all strict context laws. It also proves a boundary theorem that rejects affine, matrix and Knuth-Bendix certificates, agrees with the old checker on multilinear certificates, and accepts the square-wrapper certificate.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: A polynomial certificate is accepted exactly when its interpretation orients both root rules and is strictly monotone in every wrapper and recursor argument; affine certificates keeping both wrapper arguments, all matrix certificates and all Knuth-Bendix certificates are rejected, while the counter-projection, coupled region and square-wrapper certificates are accepted.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: The exact checker accepts precisely the unit-slope polynomial interpretations that orient both root rules and are strictly monotone in every argument, rejecting all affine-keeping, matrix and Knuth-Bendix certificates while accepting the square-wrapper certificate that the old checker rejected.
assumptions: unit successor slope (interpretation polyInterpretation z 1 a W R)
natural-number coefficients
Lean kernel only according to file Trust notes

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file proves normalization for the two-rule free recursor on terms with variables in an arbitrary type. It defines bottom-up contextual and root normal-form functions and shows reachability of those forms and their normality. It concludes that both root and contextual rewriting terminate and are confluent, and that joinability in each relation is equivalent to agreement of the corresponding normal forms.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: none
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Root and contextual rewriting of the free recursor terminate and are confluent on terms with variables, with computable normal forms deciding joinability.
assumptions: arbitrary variable type nu : Type u
axioms of main_free_contextual_termination
axioms of main_free_root_termination
no sorry, axiom, native_decide or classical choice visible in this file

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: weight t is the natural value of coupledInterpretation 1 2 evaluated at the valuation fun _ => 0 on term t.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.AuditUpgrades.FreeTermNormalization.recNormal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: recNormal b s maps .zero to b, .succ n to .wrap s (recNormal b s n), and leaves .var, .wrap and .recur rooted terms as .recur b s of themselves.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.AuditUpgrades.FreeTermNormalization.normalize
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: normalize is defined bottom-up as variables to variables, zero to zero, .succ, .wrap and .recur to the corresponding constructors applied to normalized subterms with recNormal for the recursor case.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.AuditUpgrades.FreeTermNormalization.rootNormalize
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: rootNormalize leaves variables, zero, succ and wrap unchanged, maps .recur b s .zero to rootNormalize b, .recur b s (.succ n) to .wrap s (.recur b s n), and leaves recursor terms whose counter is a variable or a constructor-rooted non-numeral unchanged.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.AuditUpgrades.FreeTermNormalization.ctx_terminating
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every variable type nu, WellFounded (fun u t : FreeTerm nu => ContextStep t u).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.AuditUpgrades.FreeTermNormalization.ctx_confluent
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every variable type nu and all a, b and c : FreeTerm nu, if Relation.ReflTransGen ContextStep a b and Relation.ReflTransGen ContextStep a c then there exists d reached contextually from both b and c.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.AuditUpgrades.FreeTermNormalization.ctx_normalization_certificate
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every variable type nu and every t : FreeTerm nu, Relation.ReflTransGen ContextStep t (normalize t) and for all u, not ContextStep (normalize t) u.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.AuditUpgrades.FreeTermNormalization.ctx_unique_normal_form
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all a and b : FreeTerm nu, if Relation.ReflTransGen ContextStep a b and for all u not ContextStep b u, then b = normalize a.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.AuditUpgrades.FreeTermNormalization.ctx_joinable_iff
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all a and b : FreeTerm nu, a and b are contextually joinable to a common d if and only if normalize a = normalize b.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.AuditUpgrades.FreeTermNormalization.root_terminating_confluent
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: WellFounded (fun u t : FreeTerm nu => RootStep t u) and for all a, b and c : FreeTerm nu, root-reachability from a to b and to c implies existence of a common root-reduct d.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.AuditUpgrades.FreeTermNormalization.root_joinable_iff
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all a and b : FreeTerm nu, a and b are root-joinable to a common d if and only if rootNormalize a = rootNormalize b.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.AuditUpgrades.FreeTermNormalization.free_term_normalization
keyDeclarations.paper_reference: Theorem 5.14 of the Orientation Boundary paper
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The conjunction that root rewriting is well-founded, contextual rewriting is well-founded, root rewriting is confluent, contextual rewriting is confluent, every t reaches normalize t which is contextually normal, every t reaches rootNormalize t which is root-normal, contextual joinability is equivalent to normalize equality, and root joinability is equivalent to rootNormalize equality, for every variable type nu.

relations.explanation: Root joinability is decided by equality of the computed root normal forms.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file defines direct orienters and a thirteen-family direct universe over every step-duplicating schema. It proves that a uniform orienter of the duplicating step is representable in none of those families. It packages this as an escape trichotomy and as a natural-valued escape theorem for step-duplicating systems.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: A uniform orienter of the duplicating step lies outside all thirteen direct families, so no measure from those families orients any relation containing the duplicating step.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: No uniform orienter of the duplicating step is representable in any of the thirteen direct families on any step-duplicating schema.
assumptions: arbitrary step-duplicating schema S and system Sys
axioms of the thirteen family barrier theorems
no sorry, axiom, native_decide or classical choice visible in this file

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: SchemaDirectOrienter S is the inductive type with constructors nat (mu : S.T -> Nat), vec (d : Nat) (mu : S.T -> Fin d -> Nat), lex (d : Nat) (mu : S.T -> Fin (d+1) -> Nat), and pair (mu : S.T -> Vec2).

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Orients O holds when for all b, s and n : S.T the duplicating-step pair is strictly ordered in the order of the orienter: < for nat, VecLt for vec, VecLexLt for lex, and PairLt for pair.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: primaryScalar maps .nat mu to mu, .vec d mu to the coordinate sum, .lex d mu to the primary coordinate, and .pair mu to the sum of the two pair coordinates.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.AuditUpgrades.SchemaEscapeUniverse.SchemaDirectRepresentable
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: SchemaDirectRepresentable O is the inductive proposition with thirteen constructors recording that O is the evaluation of an additive, transparent compositional, affine, quadratic, bounded cross-term, bounded multilinear, bounded polynomial, max-plus, max-depth, componentwise matrix, positive lexicographic matrix, balanced mixed, or weighted-projection measure, with the stated side conditions on compositional transparency, cross-term boundedness, multilinear domination, eventual domination and lexicographic positivity.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every schema S and orienter O, if O.Orients then not SchemaDirectRepresentable O.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.AuditUpgrades.SchemaEscapeUniverse.schema_direct_escape_trichotomy
keyDeclarations.paper_reference: Theorem 5.22 of the Orientation Boundary paper
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every schema S and orienter O, if O.Orients then not WrapSubtermSensitive S O.primaryScalar or not TransparentAtBase S O.primaryScalar or not SchemaDirectRepresentable O, with the proof supplying the third disjunct.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.AuditUpgrades.SchemaEscapeUniverse.system_nat_escape_leaves_universe
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every step-duplicating system Sys and mu : Sys.toStepDuplicatingSchema.T -> Nat, if GlobalOrients Sys mu (.<.) then not SchemaDirectRepresentable (.nat mu).

relations.explanation: A uniform orienter cannot be represented in the direct universe.

relations.explanation: The system-level natural-valued escape is the restriction of the schema-level escape to the duplicating steps of a system.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file strengthens the mixed-matrix barrier to strict scalar dominance. It shows that orientation at the base instance supplies the positive scalarized value needed by the nonstrict barrier, so no positivity premise is required. It combines both strict and nonstrict forms and lifts the strict form to global orientation of step-duplicating systems.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: A mixed-matrix interpretation whose scalarization strictly decreases along the ambient strict comparison cannot uniformly orient the duplicating step, so it cannot globally orient any system containing that step.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Strict scalar dominance alone rules out uniform orientation of the duplicating step by any mixed-matrix interpretation.
assumptions: affine interface on the scalarization weight
axioms of the nonstrict mixed-matrix barrier
no sorry, axiom, native_decide or classical choice visible in this file

keyDeclarations.paper_reference: Theorem 5.5 of the Orientation Boundary paper
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every schema S, dimension d, MatrixArbitraryMeasure M and relation R, if either strict scalar decrease holds for all R-related pairs or both nonstrict dominance and existence of t with 1 <= matrixScalarize M.weight (M.eval t) hold, then uniform R-orientation of the duplicating step is impossible.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.AuditUpgrades.StrictScalarDominance.no_global_orients_matrixArbitrary_of_strict_scalar_dominance
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every step-duplicating system Sys, dimension d, MatrixArbitraryMeasure M on its schema and relation R on MatrixVec d, if R u v implies matrixScalarize M.weight u < matrixScalarize M.weight v then not GlobalOrients Sys M.eval R.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file defines a total capture-avoiding substitution for the named higher-order syntax. It introduces free variables, all names, maxima, depth, bound renaming and fresh-name generation with correctness lemmas. Fuel recursion with alpha-renaming of conflicting binders yields the public operation, certified by an explicit derivation relation. Concrete controls contrast the legacy capturing substitution with the renaming, shadowing and preservation behavior of the new operation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Naive substitution captures the replacement variable under a conflicting binder where capture-avoiding substitution alpha-renames the binder and keeps the inserted variable free.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Every call to capture-avoiding substitution carries a capture-avoidance derivation, and the controls show it renames conflicting binders instead of capturing.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file splits every natural-valued interpretation at fixed base and counter by boundedness of wrapper margin and counter gain. It proves the dichotomies, four-cell coverage, and that the unbounded-wrapper and bounded-gain cell excludes orientation. On the free schema it exhibits a counter orienter and zero non-orienter in the bounded and bounded cell, coupled and doubled-wrapper witnesses in the unbounded and unbounded cell, and bounded-wrapper and alternating-gain witnesses for the bounded and unbounded cell, packaged as a catalog showing each non-barrier cell has both verdicts.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: The unbounded-wrapper and bounded-gain cell cannot orient the step-duplicating rule, while each of the other three cells contains both an orienter and a non-orienter.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: The barrier cell excludes orientation and every non-barrier cell contains both an orienter and a non-orienter.
assumptions: classical reasoning via the classical tactic for the bounded versus unbounded dichotomies

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file places each direct barrier family in the wrapper and gain growth cells at the base pair. It proves retention, threshold and dominance lemmas showing additive, affine, quadratic, max, compositional, cross-term, multilinear and polynomial measures lie in the barrier cell or fail past a threshold, and derives each family barrier from the cell theorem. Vector families are reduced to their tracked affine scalar, and the scalar grammar is characterized through cells on the free schema.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Each family is either in the unbounded-wrapper and bounded-gain barrier cell or fails at a concrete instance past a threshold, so uniform duplicator orientation is excluded in all cases.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: All direct families are recovered as cell corollaries lying in the barrier cell or failing pointwise, and grammar orientation is equivalent to absence of barrier cells plus counter strictness.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file states regression controls for certificates, extraction, connectors, size-change graphs, neutral processors and pair chains. It checks that certificates store canonical interpretations and are unique, that erasing one row breaks sixty-row coverage, and that extraction returns the recursive call occurring in the true right-hand side but rejects altered payloads and call-as-rhs. It also checks resetting connectors defeat chain well-foundedness, strictness only at the counter coordinate, rejection of empty neutral outputs, and that pair-chain well-foundedness does not imply source termination.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Pair-chain well-foundedness can hold while source termination loops, and a resetting connector preserves pair well-foundedness while breaking chain well-foundedness.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Mutation controls pin canonical certificates, extraction correctness, coordinate strictness, neutrality, and the separation between pair-chain well-foundedness and source termination.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: The file defines four certificate kinds for termination of the free recursor, namely polynomial, matrix, Knuth-Bendix and dependency-pair certificates, with an executable checker that dispatches to kind-specific decision procedures. For polynomials it proves soundness and, under the positive linear monomial test, completeness for root orientation, and on the multilinear class equivalence between acceptance, root orientation and strict monotonicity in every argument. It proves that no retentive affine polynomial, matrix or Knuth-Bendix certificate is accepted, while the counter-projection dependency-pair certificate and a coupled polynomial certificate are accepted. The Knuth-Bendix and dependency-pair checkers are proved sound and complete for their orders and criteria, and a final boundary theorem conjoins the rejections, acceptances, soundness and equivalences.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: On multilinear certificates acceptance coincides with root orientation plus strict monotonicity in every argument, but outside that class orienting and strictly monotone certificates are rejected. No retentive affine polynomial, matrix or Knuth-Bendix certificate is ever accepted, while the coupled polynomial and counter-projection dependency-pair certificates are.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Every accepted certificate proves termination, yet no retentive affine, matrix or Knuth-Bendix certificate is ever accepted while the coupled polynomial and counter-projection certificates are.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: The file defines orientation of the free contextual closure and proves that any contextual orienter restricts to a root orienter. It proves that measures in the barrier cell with unbounded wrapper cost and bounded counter gain cannot orient the context closure, and that tree size lies in that cell at every pair so it never orients contexts. In the positive direction it shows strict context laws lift root orientation to contextual decrease and to well-foundedness of the reverse contextual relation. Two controls separate the premises: a minimum-wrapper interpretation orients both root rules but fails context orientation, and a zero-step simulation does not transfer termination.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Root orientation holds on one side and contextual orientation on the other: barrier-cell measures and the minimum-wrapper interpretation orient roots yet fail on contexts, while strict context laws plus root orientation lift to termination of the contextual closure.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Strict context laws lift root orientation to contextual termination, while barrier-cell measures and the minimum-wrapper interpretation show root orientation alone does not imply contextual orientation.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: The file collects standalone controls: the singleton schema where the duplicating rule is a self-loop no measure orients, scalar-grammar classifications including payload-reading products, payload-blind zero multiples and orienting counter recodings, and a rational shrinking measure that decreases along a nonterminating step while a separated comparison on nonnegative rationals is well founded. It shows adding a self-loop keeps every coupling barrier but loses termination, dropping the duplicating rule for a linear successor rule admits an orienting size measure meeting all barrier hypotheses, and the same linear certificate fails after altering the source rule. It also exhibits a well-founded fan with arbitrarily long finite branches and no natural rank, and the empty system with empty dependency-pair problem and termination.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Rational decrease does not imply termination and well-foundedness does not imply a natural-valued rank. Coupling barriers persist under added self-loops but do not transfer to extensions that drop the duplicating rule, where orientability and termination come apart.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: The controls isolate each hypothesis by showing rational decrease, well-foundedness, barriers and certificates do not survive the corresponding weakening or extension.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: The file gives the cell form of the coupling corollary: a wrapper-retentive orienter with unbounded payload values lies in the unbounded-wrapper unbounded-gain cell. It defines the counter projection that drops the wrapper payload and an affine recursive-drop measure with zero recursive-result coefficient, computing wrapper cost zero and minus counter value respectively and counter gain one for both. Both measures orient every successor instance, fail retention at every cost, and violate the coupled gain inequality, providing expected-negative controls for each half of the retention premise.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: A retentive orienter with unbounded values forces unbounded wrapper cost and gain. The counter and recursive-drop controls orient every successor instance yet fail retention at every cost, so orientation alone does not imply the coupling conclusion.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Both the counter projection and the recursive-drop measure orient all successor instances while failing retention at every cost.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: The file defines integer wrapper cost and counter gain for natural-valued interpretations and proves pointwise and uniform equivalences between orientation of the duplicating rule and cost below gain. It proves that wrapper retention plus orientation forces counter gain above the retained payload value, so bounded gain with unbounded payload precludes orientation. It reuses the unconstrained direct-law barrier as the bounded-gain corollary and computes the exact gain of the polynomial witness with its tight coupling margin.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Orientation requires wrapper cost below counter gain at each instance. Under retention, bounded gain conflicts with unbounded payload, forcing gain above every retained value.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Retention with bounded gain and unbounded payload makes orientation impossible, with the polynomial witness attaining the bound tightly.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: The file defines same-system dependency-pair problems, native reduction pairs and triples with explicit weak and strict relations, and a source lexicographic bridge for recovering source termination. It gives polynomial and gap-two reduction pairs with different strict relations, proves every native pair certifies well-foundedness of the pair problem, and shows pair well-foundedness alone does not imply source termination via a pair-free self-loop. It adds fixture conditions, a two-dimensional pair relation, constrained certificates and higher-order substitution controls, packaged in a concrete native bundle.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Pair well-foundedness does not imply source termination, as the pair-free self-loop shows. Source termination requires the extra lexicographic bridge, and the two reduction pairs are separated by their strict gap requirements.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Native pairs certify pair well-foundedness, but source termination needs the separate lexicographic bridge, as the pair-free self-loop shows.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: Defines strongly normalizing terms, single-argument rewrite steps, defined symbols, subterms, minimal dependency-chain steps between calls, call reduction pairs and the subterm criterion with a call projection for finite first-order rewrite systems. Proves that well-foundedness of the minimal chain relation implies every term is strongly normalizing under the condition that right-hand-side variables occur in the left-hand side, and derives termination from a call reduction pair and from the subterm criterion. Shows the variable condition is necessary through the one-rule system c -> x, which has an empty hence well-founded chain relation but loops. Instantiates the criterion on a free recursor with zero and successor rules, proving termination by the counter projection and that wrapper-rooted pairs are not chain steps.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Termination from a well-founded minimal chain relation holds on the side where every rule's right-hand-side variables occur in its left-hand side and fails without it, as the looping system c -> x has no dependency pairs and a well-founded empty chain relation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Well-founded minimal dependency chains imply termination under the variable condition, with reduction-pair and subterm criteria as consequences, and the condition is sharp as shown by c -> x.
assumptions: DecidableEq nu for substitution lemmas and main termination theorems
variable condition Term.vars rule.rhs subset Term.vars rule.lhs for soundness theorems
WellFounded minimal-chain or strict-order hypothesis for termination corollaries

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: Defines package law structures ORI1Laws through ORI6Laws that restate blocked, well-foundedness and orientation facts about the stored native interpretation objects for path orders, algebraic interpretations, semantic-structural methods, dependency-pair methods, higher-order methods and substrate-change methods. Defines the row-indexed predicates NativeMethodLaws and NativeRowWitness that attach to each MissingNativeInterpretation constructor the laws and witness about its exact stored package object, and the DependentNativeCertificate structure pairing an interpretation with both. Proves every row-indexed interpretation satisfies its laws and witness, and that the canonical dependent certificates select the same sixty method families as the native interpretation layer with exactly sixty rows. Shows membership in those rows yields a certificate whose laws speak about its own stored interpretation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Each native method is certified as well-founded or orienting on certain calls on one side and provably blocked or non-orienting on the duplication pair dupSrc versus dupTgt on the other, marking the exact limit of what that interpretation can orient.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Exactly sixty method families carry interpretation-dependent certificates whose laws and row witnesses speak about their own stored interpretation.
assumptions: noncomputable dependentNativeCertificate definition
decidable equality via decide for row-list equality
