OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: The file defines the recursive path order with multiset and lexicographic status, its Dershowitz-Manna extension, and its quotient by permutative congruence, proving well-foundedness, stability, monotonicity and termination soundness. It defines the polynomial path order POP* and proves containment in the multiset path order, hence irreflexivity, well-foundedness and termination, plus an exact acceptance characterization for the free recursor. It instantiates five method rows on the free two-rule system with soundness theorems, witnesses, acceptance equivalences and mutations, and proves POP* is not transitive, not context-closed, not substitution-closed, with linear innermost scope but exponential derivational complexity.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Each row accepts the free recursor only on one side of a precedence or safe-position choice: wrap below recur and counter normal accept, while reversing the precedence or making the counter safe rejects the duplicating rule. POP* is well-founded and terminating but neither transitive nor closed under contexts or substitutions, and its linear innermost bound does not extend to derivational complexity, which is exponential.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: The recursive, permutative, polynomial, AC and simplification orders all orient the free two-rule recursor and prove termination of its contextual relation, while POP* provably fails transitivity, context closure, substitution closure and derivational-complexity extension.
assumptions: Well-founded and transitive precedence for RPO and POP* soundness and transitivity results
Irreflexive precedence for pop_recCall_forces and pPrec results
classical tactic used in DM.trans_local, RPO.of_DM, RPO.kappa_bind and Pop.toMPO
noncomputable classical choice of term linear order for sortTerms, canonArgs, kappa and kappaP representatives
No sorry, axiom or native_decide visible in the file

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.RPO
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Inductive recursive path order with status on first-order terms: subterm, iterated subterm, precedence to a smaller head, equal-head multiset comparison via a Dershowitz-Manna witness, and equal-head lexicographic comparison with agreed prefix, strict cut and domination of remaining arguments.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.RPO.wf
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If the precedence pr is well-founded then the reverse recursive path order with any status is well-founded.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.RPO.step_wf
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If pr is well-founded and every rule of a TRS R satisfies RPO pr st lhs rhs, then full rewriting Step R terminates.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.RPOm
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Recursive path order modulo permutative congruence: RPO comparison of kappa-canonical representatives whose multiset-status argument lists are sorted.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.permEq_iff_eqvGen
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Two terms have equal kappa representatives iff they are connected by the equivalence closure of single multiset-status argument permutations.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.RPOm.step_wf
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If pr is well-founded and every rule of R is oriented by RPOm pr st, then Step R terminates.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.rpom_succ_rule_iff
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: RPOm orients the duplicating rule recur b s (succ n) to wrap s (recur b s n) exactly when pr relates wrap below recur.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.rpoModuloPermutation_sound
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If the row laws hold, namely transitive and well-founded precedence, and both free rules are accepted in RPOm, then ContextStep is well-founded for every variable type.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.rpoModuloPermutation_mutation
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Keeping the witness status fixed but replacing its precedence by the opposite order makes the row reject the free two-rule system.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.PopAux
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Auxiliary order greater-pop with subterm up to safe equivalence, iterated subterm, and precedence to a head whose arguments are BelowF or recursively below.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.Pop
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Polynomial path order greater-pop-star with safe-equivalence subterm clauses, a precedence clause splitting normal arguments handled by PopAux and safe arguments by Pop with at most one recursive call, and equal-head normal and safe multiset comparisons on representatives.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.Pop.toMPO
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Every Pop comparison for data D yields an RPOm comparison for the same precedence with multiset status.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.Pop.step_wf
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If prec is well-founded and every rule of R lies in Pop, then Step R terminates.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.popStarFamily_accepts_iff
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Under irreflexive and transitive precedence, POP* accepts both free rules iff prec relates wrap below recur and the counter position of recur is normal.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.popStarFamily_sound
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If the POP* admissibility laws hold and POP* accepts both free rules, then ContextStep is well-founded for every variable type via containment in the multiset path order.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.popStarFamily_mutation
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Keeping the witness precedence fixed but making the counter safe makes POP* reject the free two-rule system.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.popStar_not_transitive
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: There exist terms s, t and u with Pop s t and Pop t u but not Pop s u.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.popStar_not_context_closed
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Pop relates S[z] to z but does not relate F[x, S[z]] to F[x, z] in the safe position of the defined symbol F.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.popStar_not_subst_closed
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Pop relates F[S[x], y] to C[y, F[x, y]] but the tbind instance under y to F[z, w] is not a Pop comparison.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.popStarFamily_complexity_scope
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If b, s and n are recur-free then every k-step contextual derivation from recur b s n satisfies k below succDepth n plus one.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.popStarFamily_derivational_outside_scope
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The family expFam k has size 5*k+1 and admits a derivation of length m with 2^k below m+1, so derivational complexity is exponential.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.acRPO
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: AC-RPO comparison defined as RPO on AC-flattened representatives that splice nested arguments of the same AC head.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.acRPO_sound
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If the AC laws hold, namely transitive and well-founded precedence with multiset status on AC symbols, and both free rules are AC-accepted, then ContextStep is well-founded for every variable type.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.acRPO_accepts_iff
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The AC row accepts both free rules iff prec relates wrap below recur, since flattening is the identity on the rule schemas.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.acRPO_mutation
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Keeping witness status and AC symbols fixed but using the opposite precedence makes the AC row reject the duplicating rule.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.simpleTerminationOrderType_scope_proven

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsPathOrders.cichonSlowGrowing_sound

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: The file defines a finite synchronous pi-calculus fragment with processes, communication steps, sender/receiver sessions, and a counter encoding with its depth measure, proving each step decreases size or depth and is well-founded. It implements the pi-calculus termination-translation row as level/data certificates with laws, acceptance, verdict, witness, mutation and scope, plus a carrier-independent termination-reflecting translation used for global countdown simulations. It defines erasing-head lambda-mu terms, beta contraction, size and a continuation-passing translation, implementing the lambda-mu strong-normalisation row with the same P5 contract and a rank into natural-number descent. Soundness, scope and method-identity theorems discharge both rows and state the exact translation principles used.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Termination holds on the side where channel levels separate the server and the data or CPS image strictly decreases; it fails for constant data, constant translation, or unseparated levels. The finite level-data certificate is bounded while the countdown simulation and erasing-head beta result are global.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Both the synchronous process counter simulation and the erasing-head lambda-mu CPS rank yield well-founded relations, with fully proved scopes and exact method identities.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsProcessCalculi.PiProc

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsProcessCalculi.PiCounterStep

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsProcessCalculi.encCounter
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: encCounter n is nil when n is zero and output on channel 1 prefixing encCounter n when the argument is successor.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Data consists of a channel level function Nat to Nat, a bound Nat, and a data measure Nat to Nat.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsProcessCalculi.piCalculusTerminationTranslationLaws

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: The file implements three semantic-framework rows for the free recursor: an abstract-interpretation ranking abstraction with simulation and rank decrease, a powerset-coalgebra categorical row with morphism laws and no-infinite-path verdicts, and a higher-order constrained rewriting row with projection laws and the value criterion. Each row provides data, laws, acceptance, verdict, witness, mutation or loop counterexample, scope and method-identity theorems, with soundness proved via coupled polynomial interpretation, accessibility, and constrained dependency-pair chains. A generic ranking-abstraction theorem, Taylor well-founded coalgebra lemmas, and the applicative higher-order recursor with its constraint semantics support the three instances.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Termination is certified when abstract transitions simulate concrete steps and strictly decrease a rank, and when coalgebra morphisms are exact with accessible images. The higher-order value criterion certifies only under the x greater than zero constraint; coarse graphs, looping coalgebras, raised bounds, or dropped constraints lie on the failing side.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Ranking abstractions, well-founded powerset coalgebras, and the higher-order value criterion each prove termination of their free-system instances with fully proved arbitrary-carrier scopes.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: The file builds restricted rewriting with admitted substitutions and active positions, its minimal chains, chain soundness and subterm criterion. It instantiates this to context-sensitive rewriting with a replacement map, to many-sorted type introduction with Zantema's condition and the Toyama system, to order-sorted rewriting, and to a layered many-sorted persistence proof with projections and principal subterms. Each row has laws, an acceptance criterion, a soundness theorem, a concrete witness for the free recursor, feature examples and mutations showing the hypotheses are necessary.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Sorted termination holds for well-sorted terms while unsorted termination can fail, and active or replacing positions orient while blocked, ill-sorted or migrating-variable positions do not; the file proves exactly which sorted criteria cross this boundary and where Zantema's side condition and conservativeness are load-bearing.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: The free recursor terminates unsorted via the native two-sort many-sorted witness, and more generally rule-typed sorted termination is equivalent to unsorted termination.
assumptions: classical choice used in noncomputable proj/projection definitions via fnf and inside freeRecursor_sorted_persistence
DecidableEq S for proj0, proj, aliens layer definitions and persistence theorems
no sorry, axiom or native_decide visible in the file

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: The file defines string and cycle rewriting on words, rewriting modulo finite equations, and maximally shared term-graph rewriting, all applied to the free recursor with free terms, contexts and steps imported from earlier files. It proves bounded length growth for finite string and cycle systems and a general encoding barrier saying no bounded-growth word relation performs every ground duplicating recursor step under compositional-length encodings. It packages four method rows with universal barrier or transfer theorems, concrete witnesses including the 01 to 10 rule, commutativity of wrap, a cost-doubling shared step and the Toyama system, and mutations with degenerate empty encoding, looping ground equation and stutter policy showing sharpness. It also proves transfers from cycle to string termination and from modulo and sharing termination to free termination, while exhibiting non-conservation of normal forms, step counts and the converse termination direction.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Finite string and cycle systems lengthen words only by a system-bounded constant, so under any compositional-length encoding they cannot perform the duplicating recursor step whose length gap grows with the payload, even though the prefix code injectively represents every term. Termination transfers from cycle steps to string steps and from modulo and shared steps to free steps, but the converse and conservation fail: 01 to 10 terminates on strings but loops on cycles, commutativity merges distinct free normal forms, one shared step needs two term steps, and sharing terminates on the Toyama start where term rewriting loops.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: No finite compositional-length string or cycle system performs the duplicating recursor step in one step, and quotient and sharing termination transfer to free terms without conserving normal forms, step counts or the converse direction.
assumptions: CompositionalLength: 1 <= cz and additive code lengths for succ, wrap and recur
RegularEquations: both sides of each equation contain the same free variables
Finite rule lists over Nat with length bound sumRhs for string and cycle steps
Simulation hypothesis Simulates ContextStep with policyStep and identity readback for sharing laws
Well-foundedness hypotheses for CycleStep, ModStep and policyStep relations
Termination of free contextual rewriting from main_free_contextual_termination
Ground encodings use FreeTerm Empty while modulo and sharing use FreeTerm Nat

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.SRSStep
keyDeclarations.paper_reference: Book and Otto, String-Rewriting Systems, 1993, Chapter 2
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: A string rewriting step for a rule list R over an alphabet holds between words u and v when some rule in R rewrites u to v by replacing one occurrence of its left-hand side by its right-hand side inside a left context x and a right context y.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.CycleStep
keyDeclarations.paper_reference: Zantema, König and Bruggink, Termination of cycle rewriting, RTA-TLCA 2014
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: A cycle rewriting step for R holds between u and v when there exist intermediate words u' and v' such that u rotates to u', u' rewrites to v' by SRSStep for R, and v' rotates to v.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.srs_wf_of_cycle_wf
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For any rule list R, if the CycleStep relation for R is well-founded then the SRSStep relation for R is well-founded.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.cycleRewriting_feature
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: String rewriting with the single rule 01 to 10 is well-founded, and cycle rewriting with the same rule is not well-founded because the word 01 loops to itself up to rotation.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.CompositionalLength
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For string-method data M with encoding enc and constants cz, cs, cw and cr, CompositionalLength means 1 is at most cz, enc of zero has length cz, and enc of succ t, wrap s t and recur b s n have lengths cs plus length of enc t, cw plus lengths of enc s and enc t, and cr plus lengths of enc b, enc s and enc n.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.encoding_barrier
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For any M satisfying CompositionalLength, any bound K, and any word relation step such that step u v implies length of v is at most length of u plus K, it is false that step sends enc of recur b s (succ n) to enc of wrap s (recur b s n) for all ground b, s and n.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.stringRewritingInapplicabilityLaws
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: String-rewriting inapplicability laws for M hold exactly when CompositionalLength M holds.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.stringRewritingInapplicabilityResult
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: String-rewriting inapplicability verdict for M holds exactly when it is not the case that every ground duplicating step from enc of recur b s (succ n) to enc of wrap s (recur b s n) is a one-step SRSStep with M.rules.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.stringRewritingInapplicability_universal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every M, if stringRewritingInapplicabilityLaws M holds then stringRewritingInapplicabilityResult M holds, so under CompositionalLength no finite string system performs every duplicating step in one step.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.stringRewritingInapplicability_mutation
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The degenerate data with empty-word encoding and the single empty rule does not satisfy Laws because it violates 1 is at most cz, but it does satisfy Accepts because the empty rule rewrites the empty word to itself.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.cycleRewritingInapplicabilityLaws
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Cycle-rewriting inapplicability laws for M hold exactly when CompositionalLength M holds.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.cycleRewritingInapplicabilityResult
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Cycle verdict for M holds exactly when it is not the case that every ground duplicating step is a one-step CycleStep with M.rules.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.cycleRewritingInapplicability_universal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every M, if cycleRewritingInapplicabilityLaws M holds then cycleRewritingInapplicabilityResult M holds, so under CompositionalLength no finite cycle system performs every duplicating step in one step.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.cycleRewritingInapplicability_mutation
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The degenerate empty-word data does not satisfy cycle Laws but does satisfy cycle Accepts by viewing its empty string step as a cycle step.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.ModStep
keyDeclarations.paper_reference: Jouannaud and Kirchner, SIAM J. Comput. 1986
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Rewriting modulo a finite equation list E holds between t and u when there exist t' and u' such that t is E-congruent to t', t' takes a free ContextStep to u', and u' is E-congruent to u.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.equationalQuotientNonConservativityLaws
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Equational-quotient laws for E hold exactly when every equation in E is regular, meaning both sides contain the same free variables.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.equationalQuotientNonConservativityResult
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Equational-quotient verdict for E holds exactly when ModStep E is well-founded and free ContextStep on FreeTerm Nat is well-founded.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.equationalQuotientNonConservativity_sound
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every E, if equationalQuotientNonConservativityLaws E and equationalQuotientNonConservativityAccepts E both hold then free ContextStep is well-founded.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.comm_merges_normal_forms
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The terms nfLeft equals wrap zero (succ zero) and nfRight equals wrap (succ zero) zero are distinct, no ContextStep leaves either term, yet E-congruence for commutativity of wrap identifies them.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.equationalQuotientNonConservativity_mutation
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The single regular ground equation zero equals recur zero zero zero satisfies Laws, its ModStep is not well-founded because zero loops to itself, while free ContextStep remains well-founded.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.SharedStep
keyDeclarations.paper_reference: Plump, Term graph rewriting, Handbook of Graph Grammars 1999
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: A maximally shared step holds between t and u when for some redex a and contractum b with RootStep a b occurring in t, u equals replaceAll a b t, contracting every occurrence at once.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.sharedStep_simulates
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Every SharedStep with identity readback is a nonempty TransGen sequence of ContextSteps, so SharedStep is simulated by ContextStep.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.sharing_cost_control
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: SharedStep sends wrap costRedex costRedex to wrap costContractum costContractum, no single ContextStep does so, but two ContextSteps do, witnessed by RelPow ContextStep 2.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.ToyamaShared
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Maximally shared Toyama rewriting holds between t and u when for some ToyamaRoot a b with ToyamaOccurs a in t, u equals toyamaReplaceAll a b t.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.toyama_sharing_nonconservative
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Maximally shared rewriting is accessible from toyamaStart equals f of g zero one three times, while Toyama term rewriting is not accessible from the same start because term rewriting loops.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.policyStep
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The step of a SharingPolicy is ContextStep for tree, SharedStep for maximal, and equality with u equals t for stutter.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.sharingNonConservativityLaws
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Sharing laws for a policy M hold exactly when every policyStep M step reads back to a nonempty term-step sequence, namely Simulates ContextStep with policyStep M and identity.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.sharingNonConservativityResult
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Sharing verdict for M holds exactly when policyStep M is well-founded.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.sharingNonConservativity_universal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every policy M, if sharingNonConservativityLaws M holds then sharingNonConservativityResult M holds, so simulation plus free termination gives policy termination.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsSubstrate.sharingNonConservativity_mutation
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The stutter policy does not satisfy Laws because simulation would give a TransGen loop on zero contradicting free termination, and does not satisfy Result because it loops on zero with u equals t.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: The file defines simply typed applicative terms over System T sorts, typed signatures, applicative rewriting, and the typed iterator and Godel recursor rules with an adapter from the free first-order schema. It formalises four typed termination methods: the higher-order recursive path ordering, the computability path ordering, the general-schema computable closure, and sized types, each with clauses, acceptance, laws, witness and soundness statements. Each row is proved sound by embedding its clauses into the recursive path order with application minimal, yielding termination of the typed iterator rules and by transfer of the free schema. It also proves that all four methods admit Godels recursor rules and hence terminate System T recursor rewriting.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Each method admits the iterator and recursor rules when its type, accessibility, precedence and size-freshness checks hold. It rejects rules breaking those checks, such as a recursive call on the unchanged or larger counter, a binary flattening with an ill-typed middle term, or a looping rule accepted only under non-fresh size labels.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: All four typed methods admit Godels System T recursor rules and yield termination of recursor rewriting, hence of the typed iterator rules and of the free schema.
assumptions: WellFounded strict precedence and transitivity used in all rows
Admissible type ordering and accessible arguments for the CPO row
Stage-variable freshness for size labels in the sized-types row
No sorry, axiom, native_decide or classical choice appears in the code

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsTypedCalculi.Horpo
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Given a signature sig, variable typing Gamma, precedence pr and status assignment st, Horpo is the inductive HORPO relation in modes strict, weak and domination generated by reflexivity, strict-in-weak, the two domination clauses, and the strict subterm, precedence, multiset, lexicographic and applicative-right clauses, where every strict clause requires equal computed types.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsTypedCalculi.Horpo.toRPO
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If Horpo sig Gamma pr st m s t holds then its reading in the recursive path order with precedence apPrec pr and status apStat st holds for s and t in the same mode.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsTypedCalculi.horpo_rec_succ
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every result type A, precedence pr and status st, Horpo with tSig and recCtx A relates the left side recSuccL A strictly above the right side recSuccR A.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsTypedCalculi.horpoAdmittance_sound
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every horpoAdmittanceData M, if horpoAdmittanceLaws M holds and horpoAdmittanceAccepts M holds then TypedFreeTermination holds.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsTypedCalculi.horpoAdmittance_systemT_terminates
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every horpoAdmittanceData M with horpoAdmittanceLaws M, every result type A and variable type nu, applicative rewriting AStep with recRules A is well-founded.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsTypedCalculi.Cpo
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Given sig, Gamma and ingredients P with precedence, status, type ordering and accessible positions, Cpo is the inductive CPO relation in modes gt, gtT, geT, ge and st generated by typing, reflexivities, strict inclusions, status clauses with accessible subterms, and the rules fbSub, fbEqMul, fbEqLex, fbPrec, fbAp, apSubL and apSubR.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsTypedCalculi.Cpo.toRPO
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If Cpo sig Gamma P m s t holds then its reading in the recursive path order with precedence apPrec P.prec and status apStat P.stat holds for s and t.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsTypedCalculi.cpo_rec_succ
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every result type A and ingredients P, Cpo with tSig and recCtx A relates recSuccL A above recSuccR A in mode gtT.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsTypedCalculi.cpoAdmittance_sound
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every cpoAdmittanceData M, if cpoAdmittanceLaws M holds and cpoAdmittanceAccepts M holds then TypedFreeTermination holds.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsTypedCalculi.cpoAdmittance_systemT_terminates
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every cpoAdmittanceData M with cpoAdmittanceLaws M, every A and nu, applicative rewriting AStep with recRules A is well-founded.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsTypedCalculi.GSClosure
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Given inductive declaration D, signature sig, typing Gamma, precedence pr, status assignment st, head f and argument list l, GSClosure holds for r in the computable closure of f of l by variables, accessible subterms, application, smaller symbols and recursive calls decreasing in StatGt.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsTypedCalculi.FollowsGS
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: FollowsGS D sig Gamma pr st lhs rhs holds when lhs equals app of fn f to l for some f and l with GSClosure of rhs from f of l and every variable occurring in rhs accessible in l.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsTypedCalculi.GSClosure.toRPO
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If GSClosure D sig Gamma pr st f l r holds and every variable occurrence in r is accessible in l then the recursive path order with apPrec pr and apStat st relates app fn f l above r.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsTypedCalculi.gs_rec_succ
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every A, pr and st, FollowsGS with tInd, tSig and recCtx A relates recSuccL A to recSuccR A.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsTypedCalculi.generalSchemaAdmittance_sound
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every generalSchemaAdmittanceData M, if generalSchemaAdmittanceLaws M holds and generalSchemaAdmittanceAccepts M holds then TypedFreeTermination holds.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every generalSchemaAdmittanceData M with generalSchemaAdmittanceLaws M, every A and nu, applicative rewriting AStep with recRules A is well-founded.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: With rank precedence and multiset status, for every A HORPO admits recSuccL to recSuccR with multiset and with lexicographic status, rejects domination of app s n via binary flattening, rejects strict comparison to step argument s while RPO accepts it, and rejects strict comparison to the same-counter call.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: With rank precedence and multiset status, for every A recSucc follows the schema, n is accessible in succ n with ArgGt, the larger-counter call is rejected, and the iter call from rec is forbidden at equal rank but follows the schema when iter is below rec.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file formalizes four typing disciplines as method rows for the free recursor with base, payload and counter. It defines linear typing with exponentials, tiered ramified recurrence, Bellantoni-Cook safe recursion, and the Rocq guard condition with call-by-value evaluation. Each row proves soundness in the form of resource preservation, polynomial height or size bounds, or termination, and determines whether the duplicating successor rule is admitted. Witnesses, mutations that flip each side condition, and scope statements delimit the omitted material for every row.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Exponential-free linear typings preserve variable occurrences and cannot derive the duplicating successor rule, while allowing the payload type bang B restores derivability with exactly one contraction. Tiered, safe-normal and guarded definitions admit the recursor only when the counter is above the result, the payload is normal, or recursive calls are structurally smaller, and dropping each side condition breaks the bound, acceptance or termination claim.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: The file proves that exponential-free linear typing rejects the duplicating recursor while tiered, safe-normal and guarded disciplines admit it with polynomial bounds or termination under sharp side conditions.
assumptions: DecidableEq on rule variables for occurrence counting
Exponential-free context with no IsBang entries for the linear barrier
Tier inequality between result and counter for ramified recurrence
Normal counter and payload positions for Bellantoni-Cook admission
Decreasing index below 3 for guard soundness
No sorry, axiom, native_decide or classical choice visible

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodRowsTypingDisciplines.bsafe_size_bound

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file formalizes usable-rules and formative-rules rows for dependency-pair problems over a generic first-order library. It defines the least usable symbol and rule sets generated from pair-target roots and proves closure, leastness, and replay of rewriting and chains inside the generated rules. For the free two-rule recursor the usable symbols collapse to the recursor while the duplicating rule is retained, yielding finiteness on usable-rooted calls. It then defines formative rule and pair catalogs selected from the actual eight-schema source and proves sufficiency, closure, exactness and well-foundedness.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Finiteness over the generated usable rules transfers to the original problem only for usable-rooted calls, and the transport for non-usable-rooted calls is explicitly not claimed. The formative catalog is exact for the actual pair relation exactly when the recSucc selectors are retained, and omitting them loses sufficiency and exactness.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: The file proves that the generated usable rules are the least closed set and carry chain finiteness to usable-rooted calls while retaining duplication, and that the selected formative catalog is exact and well-founded for the actual pair problem.
assumptions: Variable condition that right-hand side variables are contained in left-hand side variables
Pair problem is a subrelation of the dependency pairs of the system
No sorry, axiom, native_decide or classical choice visible

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: The file defines statusAdmits, which records which closure verdicts each finer-table status allows. It proves that for each of the 76 termination method families, the status assigned by statusOf admits the verdict assigned by methodVerdict. It derives directional consequences for barrier and escape cases and shows that an escape-status row carries the orienting MethodResult proved by the closure table. It also records the statuses of seven named methods discussed in the paper methods table.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Barrier-status rows admit the barrier verdict and escape-status rows admit the escape verdict, separating methods that block orientation from methods that carry an orienting result.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: For every one of the 76 methods, the finer-table status admits the closure-table verdict.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every method family f, if statusOf f equals barrier then methodVerdict f equals barrier.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.MethodStatusAgreement.methodVerdict_of_statusOf_escape
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every method family f, if statusOf f equals escape then methodVerdict f equals escape.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every method family f, if methodVerdict f equals barrier then statusOf f equals barrier or equals conditional_barrier or equals not_applicable.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: The file unifies 76 termination-method catalogue rows over the free recursor. It defines per-family data, laws, acceptance and result predicates, a four-valued barrier-escape verdict, and uniform soundness, feature and mutation statements assembled from the row modules. It constructs a witness for each family and proves the witnesses satisfy the laws and results, the uniform soundness, feature and mutation theorems, and exact identity theorems for 13 repaired named methods. It packages witnesses as row certificates, shows the certificate list covers exactly the full family list, and shows deleting any certificate breaks coverage.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Each method family is classified as barring or escaping the free duplicating rule on the free recursor, with fragment variants for restricted fragments. Deleting any one row certificate breaks exact coverage of the full family list.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Every one of the 76 method families has witness data satisfying its laws and its row result on the free recursor.
assumptions: set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxRecDepth 4000
noncomputable constructions for methodWitness, rowCertificate, certificates and coveredRows

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file binds each of the 76 RDRS method-family rows to method-native semantics. The sixteen rows already covered by the legacy evidence interface are assigned False and return none, while the other sixty rows receive exact row propositions, indexed interpretation objects, and proof-bearing evidence. It proves the interpretation list and evidence list both have length 60, coincide, are duplicate-free, and that the legacy list has length 16 and is disjoint. The capstone structure packages these counts and existence properties as closed coverage.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: The sixteen legacy theorem-backed rows map to False and none and remain owned by the legacy evidence interface, while the complementary sixty rows each carry a native proposition, an indexed interpretation object, and proof-bearing evidence.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: The sixty non-legacy RDRS rows each have a native interpretation object and proof-bearing native proposition disjoint from the sixteen legacy rows, packaged as a closed coverage.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file defines observed steps, the reverse observed relation, factored ranks into arbitrary targets, exact-length paths, and natural-valued ranks. It proves a factored rank into a well-founded target yields well-foundedness of the reverse observed relation with a converse via the identity rank, and that natural ranks exist exactly under bounded heights. It gives a well-founded top countdown with no natural rank, a terminating two-chain whose identifying observation cycles with no factored rank, and a constant collapse with a self-loop.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: An observer admits some factored rank exactly when its reverse observed relation is well-founded, while a natural-valued rank needs uniformly bounded finite path lengths. Coarsening or collapsing the observation can introduce cycles or self-loops so a terminating source has no factored rank.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Well-foundedness lifts through an observer exactly when the reverse observed relation is well-founded, but natural-valued ranks need bounded heights and collapsing observations can destroy termination.
assumptions: classical reasoning via classical tactic in natRank_iff_boundedHeights

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.ObserverRanks.FactoredRank
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Defines a rank on observer values into an arbitrary target relation: for all x y, R x y implies lt (rank (q y)) (rank (q x)).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.ObserverRanks.factoredRank_observed

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.ObserverRanks.observedRev_wellFounded_of_factoredRank

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file defines when an observer licenses a well-founded rank and compares licensing observers with the counter of a counter system. It proves a counter-factored observer licenses exactly when the factoring map is injective, equivalently when kernels agree, and that observers sufficient for the counter are exactly kernel refinements with quotient isomorphic to Nat. On the free recursor call relation it builds two incomparable licensing observers whose common coarsenings license none, refuting a coarsest licensing observer, and shows fiber-constant ranks are strict recodings while arbitrary ranks have infinitely many orders.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: A counter-factored observer licenses a rank exactly when it is injective on counter values; merging two values closes an observed cycle. No licensing observer is coarser than all natural-valued licensing observers, since two incomparable licensing observers have only non-licensing common coarsenings.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Counter-factored licensing is exactly injectivity while the free call relation has two incomparable licensing observers with no coarsest licensing observer and infinitely many rank orders without fiber constancy.
assumptions: Classical.choose in sufficient_observer_licensesRank and counterKernelQuotient constructions
CounterSystem structure with counter, states, decreases, step_succ, and counter_state laws

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.ObserverSufficiency.not_licensesRank_of_cycle

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Methods.OrientationClosure.ObserverSufficiency.counterFactored_licensesRank_iff_injective

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every counter system C and g, the counter-factored observer licenses a rank if and only if its kernel equals the counter kernel on all pairs x y.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every variable type and observer codomain, there is no licensing observer coarser than every natural-valued licensing observer of the free call relation.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For the free call counter system, counter ranks are equivalent to strict recodings, the order quotient is equivalent to PUnit, and fiber-constant natural ranks are exactly same-order recodings.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file presents the Orientation Boundary as a set of reflected grammar expressions with semantic and syntactic descriptions. It proves the set orienting all successor instances equals the payload-blind counter-strict set at every variable type, hence carrier-independently and in intersection over all types, with the counter inside and payload and constants outside. It defines four growth cells and proves every measure lies in some cell and at most one, with the barrier cell excluding uniform orientation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: A grammar expression orients all successor instances exactly when it is payload-blind and counter-strict, with the counter inside and payload and constants outside. A measure at a base-counter pair lies in the barrier cell exactly when wrapper cost is unbounded and counter gain is bounded, which excludes uniform orientation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: The set of expressions orienting all successor instances equals the payload-blind counter-strict set independently of carrier, and every measure lies in exactly one of four growth cells with the barrier cell excluding uniform orientation.
assumptions: Classical.choice via Classical.choose in growthCell, noncomputable definition

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file packages paper-facing consequences of existing Orientation Boundary families without new measure language or decision problems. It proves the per-carrier equivalence between successor orientation and payload blindness with strict counter response, its all-carriers corollary, and the counter-admissible variant reducing to payload blindness. It also proves a payload-erasing step admits no decisive payload-sensitive certificate.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Successor orientation holds exactly for payload-blind counter-strict measures, and payload-blind alone under counter admissibility. Payload erasure marks the limit where no decisive payload-sensitive certificate exists.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Orientation of successor instances is exactly payload blindness plus strict counter response, and payload-erasing steps admit no decisive payload-sensitive certificate.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file collects the Orientation Boundary hypothesis-necessity results in one theorem. It covers the fourteen direct barrier families with twenty-seven consumed premises, deleted-premise countermodels, restore-and-refute pairs, and three empty-premise families. It also covers necessity of both barrier-cell growth hypotheses and necessity statements and kind counts for all seventy-six method rows.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Each consumed premise is necessary because deleting it admits a countermodel while restoring it refutes orientation; three barrier families need no premises and both barrier-cell growth hypotheses fail individually without their condition.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: All fourteen barrier families with twenty-seven premises and all seventy-six method rows have exact necessity statements with the stated class counts.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file defines native path-order semantics for the ten ORI-1 rows with computations from method weights, precedence, status, AC theory, ordinal weights, applicative encoding, and polynomial functions. It proves each comparison carries the variable condition and is well-founded where claimed, with concrete witnesses including multiset status, collapsing precedence, ordinal weights, and nonlinear polynomials. It shows every variant blocks the duplicating schema rule and packages all rows with nontriviality controls into a concrete ORI-1 semantics.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Each native comparison orients only pairs satisfying the variable condition, so the duplicating rule with an extra payload occurrence is never oriented, while genuine weight, precedence, status, AC, ordinal, applicative, and polynomial controls remain inhabited.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: All ten ORI-1 path-order methods have native weight, precedence, status, AC, ordinal, applicative, and polynomial semantics that are well-founded where claimed yet uniformly block the duplicating rule.
assumptions: CommSemiring K with strict order laws for generalized KBO
noncomputable ordinal-weight definitions using classical choice

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file defines constructor-local natural-coefficient polynomial interpretations with monomial lists W and R and the predicates OrientsSucc and OrientsZero. It proves exact univariate orientation criteria for wrappers with y-coefficient 0, 1 or covered by AllHigh, plus failing triples for y-square, y-payload and large leading coefficients. It implements the executable check ltAllB and the partial decision decideSuccAff with soundness, failing witnesses and an exact description of the open class, total for unit successor. It classifies affine-multilinear and restricted-quadratic families and transports the unit decision to arbitrary signatures.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: For unit successor the decision is total, while for beta >= 2 it leaves a residual class that contains both orienting and non-orienting members. A wrapper with y-degree at least two, a y-payload monomial, or y-coefficient at least beta^d+1 fails orientation, where d is the maximal counter degree.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Unit-successor root orientation of the free recursor is decided soundly and completely with failing witnesses, while larger slopes leave an explicitly mixed residual class.
assumptions: 1 <= beta for successor-table lemmas
classical case distinction on variable type in signature transport
no sorry, axiom or native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file defines successor, wrapper and coupled recursor evaluations and the predicates for orienting the successor rule, zero rule and both rules. It proves alpha >= 1 and beta >= 2 sufficient for both rules with an explicit margin, and necessary by evaluating at zero and at payload beta+1. It generalizes to r-fold wrapper iteration with the exact threshold r <= alpha and r+1 <= beta, whose r=1 case is the main (1,2) construction.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Both free rules are oriented exactly when alpha >= 1 and beta >= 2. For r-fold wrapper iteration the boundary is r <= alpha and r+1 <= beta.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: The coupled interpretation orients both free recursor rules iff alpha >= 1 and beta >= 2, with (1,2) as the minimal instance.
assumptions: 1 <= alpha and 2 <= beta as sufficiency hypotheses
no axioms, sorry or classical choice

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This module turns each native reduction pair into a connector-aware chain reduction pair and proves that every actual pair-plus-connector chain step is strict and well-founded. It instantiates the theorem for the polynomial and gap-two pairs, whose strict relations differ. It gives a Boolean reset pair and connector showing that well-foundedness of the pair alone does not imply well-foundedness of the composed chain.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Well-foundedness of the pair relation alone does not imply well-foundedness of pair-plus-connector chains; the reset pair is well-founded alone but its chain with the reset connector self-loops.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Every native reduction pair certifies the full pair-plus-connector chain, while pair well-foundedness alone does not.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file defines calls, minimal chain steps, finite dependency-pair problems and the dpPairs relation, proving that finiteness gives termination and is monotone with an exact identity processor. It defines reduction triples and proves the triple processor sound, with a counterexample for swapped weak roles. It gives argument filtering, equational quotients and sharing simulations with exact cost preservation, each accompanied by controls showing deleting a live edge, quotienting the converse, or sharing without simulation is unsound.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Finiteness survives removing only strictly decreasing edges and forward quotient or stepwise simulation, but deleting a live self-loop, quotient-identifying distinct normal forms, or sharing with identical readback but no stepwise simulation breaks termination.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Finiteness of the dependency-pair problem implies termination and is preserved by reduction-triple, filtering, quotient and simulation processors whose side conditions are necessary.
assumptions: DecidableEq on variables and rhs-vars subset of lhs-vars for termination transfer
strongly normalizing arguments at both chain ends
no sorry, axiom or native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file defines r-ary duplicating schemas with retention, integer counter gain and wrapper cost, proving orientation is exactly cost below gain. It shows retention forces gain above r copies plus cost, hence with uniformly bounded gain and unbounded payload no measure orients the rule at any r >= 1. It shows r >= 1 is necessary by an orienting arity-zero example, and identifies arity one with the binary P3.1 barrier.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: With retention, uniformly bounded counter gain and unbounded payload values, no measure orients the r-ary duplicating rule for any r >= 1; at r = 0 such a measure exists, so r >= 1 is sharp.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Retention plus bounded gain cannot orient the duplicating rule at any positive arity, and arity one is exactly the binary barrier.
assumptions: 1 <= r for the barrier
retention at cost c_w
uniform counter-gain bound g
unbounded payload values

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file defines proof-bearing capstone structures ORI-1 through ORI-6, each field being the exact method-native row proposition from its implementation module. It proves each package closed from its native bundle and row anchors, without classifier equalities or True surrogates. It combines them with the generalized existing sixteen into a joint closure with exactly sixty complementary rows and preserved evidence.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: The categorical field stays a scoped relational-category separation rather than a topos-wide theorem, and HORPO and CPO keep explicit first-order admittance scope without claiming a complete higher-order calculus.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: The six packages jointly close the sixty-row complementary wave plus the sixteen historical rows with typed evidence.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file proves hypothesis necessity for twenty conditional, typed, typing, graph, process and semantic rows on the free duplicating rule. Each escapable row exhibits a lens, a witness and a mutated value that keeps the row laws but loses acceptance, while inescapable rows prove laws determine the verdict with no separating feature change. It includes the barrier-premise linear-logic case and flat-wrap and heavy-share mutations for graph rows.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: For each escapable row a single feature change preserves the laws while flipping acceptance from true to false; for inescapable rows the laws fix acceptance so no feature lens separates verdicts.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Each row's characteristic law or data feature is necessary for acceptance, except where laws alone fix the verdict.
assumptions: lawful witness datum per row
concrete mutated feature value distinct from the witness
no axioms, sorry or native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file proves hypothesis necessity for thirteen dependency-pair, usable-formative and substrate method rows for the free duplicating rule and related systems. Each row gets a necessity kind, a necessity statement on its own laws and acceptance predicate, and a proof by a concrete lawful accepted witness plus a feature change or deleted clause that preserves the remaining laws while losing acceptance. Three rows instead prove that the laws determine the verdict, so no feature change separates acceptance from rejection.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Acceptance holds for the lawful witness with its characteristic feature present and fails after changing only that feature or deleting only that clause while keeping the remaining laws. Rows whose laws fix the verdict have no separating feature change.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Each of the thirteen dependency-pair, usable-formative and substrate rows satisfies its stated escape-feature, barrier-premise or laws-determine-verdict necessity property.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file proves hypothesis necessity for the fifteen interpretation rows, from linear polynomials over Q and R through max, nonlinear, multilinear, matrix, arctic, tropical, triangular, tuple, strict and extended algebras to finite models. Barrier rows delete one positivity, monotonicity, irreflexivity or finiteness clause and keep an accepted countermodel, while escape rows change one successor, recursor or strict-order feature. The arctic and tropical rows use a deleted wrapper-recursor pair with a covered split in which each part alone forces the contextual barrier.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Each interpretation orients the free duplicating rule when its characteristic monotonicity, positivity or finiteness condition holds, and a mutant dropping only that coefficient, entry or clause stays otherwise lawful but is no longer accepted. The arctic and tropical rows need the wrapper-recursor finiteness pair jointly, with each part alone still forcing the barrier.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Each of the fifteen interpretation rows satisfies its stated deleted-barrier-premise or deleted-escape-feature necessity property, with the arctic and tropical rows additionally satisfying the covered two-part barrier with nonduplicating and contextual controls.
concepts: linear polynomials over Q and R
assumptions: Classical.choice
noncomputable definitions
Countable and Infinite instances for expression types

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file proves hypothesis necessity for thirteen labelling, match-bound and sorted or constrained rows for the free recursor and schema. Escape rows change one labelling, system, position or order feature and lose orientation or the free-step adapter, while barrier rows delete height decrease or linearity and keep an accepted countermodel. Type introduction is a universal barrier rejecting the free recursor everywhere, and many-sorted and order-sorted rows have their verdicts fixed by the laws.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Acceptance requires the named labelling, bound, linearity, height-decrease or sort side-condition, and dropping only that hypothesis while keeping the remaining laws yields a lawful but rejected mutant or an accepted countermodel. Type introduction has a universal barrier with no lawful acceptance, while many-sorted and order-sorted laws fix acceptance outright.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Each of the thirteen labelling, match-bound, forward-closure, quasi-decreasingness, context-sensitive and sorted rows satisfies its stated escape-feature, barrier-premise, universal-barrier or laws-determine-verdict necessity property.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file states necessity for fifteen method rows for orientation closure. For barrier rows it shows a lawful witness exists, the duplicating rule is rejected at every datum, and a nonduplicating zero rule is oriented. For escape rows it shows a single feature change keeps laws but loses acceptance. For premise-deletion rows it exhibits a countermodel satisfying all other laws but violating the deleted clause while accepting.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Lawful data reject the duplicating rule while orienting the nonduplicating zero rule; deleting one law clause or changing one feature flips the verdict to acceptance or loss of acceptance.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Every listed KBO, path-order and other-calculi row satisfies its stated barrier, escape-feature or fixed-verdict necessity.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file gives an executable decision procedure for the seven-constructor scalar direct-measure grammar. It implements positivity-at-unit and payload-dependence tests and proves them sound and complete. It proves counter sections are monotone and discretely convex, reducing strict response to the first increment. The classifier returns either a proof of orientation or a concrete failed duplicating-step instance, with evaluated controls.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: A scalar expression orients the duplicating step exactly when it is payload-blind and strictly counter-increasing; failure of either yields an explicit failed instance.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: The classifier decides scalar orientation exactly, returning either an orientation proof or a concrete failed duplicating-step witness.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file supplies native semantic and structural witnesses for orientation method ORI-3. It builds a concrete extended monotone algebra, a weak one-point finite model, a raised match-bound certificate for countdown, and labelling and categorical controls. It proves linearity from raised certificates, the absence of any raised certificate for KO7, and the incompatibility of strict finite-model laws.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Finiteness is consistent only without strict wrapper growth, and no raised match-bound certificate exists for KO7 although countdown has one; the strict wrapper law is the incompatible requirement.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Countdown admits a raised match-bound certificate implying linearity, while KO7 admits none and strict finite models are impossible.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file puts successor orientation for polynomial interpretations into separable form. It defines the separable difference and monomial-wise separable sum and proves orientation is exactly positivity of this difference over all bases, payloads and counters. It proves the zero-step necessity and zero-plus-step sufficiency and records the exact residual goal without claiming decidability, showing slope two admits both outcomes.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: The affine successor decision is complete except for the open branch at slope at least two, where both orientation and non-orientation occur and only the exact residual goal remains.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Successor orientation on the open class is exactly separable positivity, which is two-sided at slope two and left as an exact residual goal.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file gives complete executable positivity decisions on two strata of the residual open branch. On base-affine and payload-affine signed polynomials it decides positivity by univariate checks with extracted failing pairs. It proves soundness, completeness and residual adapters and provides controls inside and outside the strata.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Positivity is completely decidable on base-degree at most one and payload-degree at most one strata with extracted counterexamples; biquadratic and higher shapes lie outside.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Positivity on base-affine and payload-affine strata is completely decidable with extracted counterexamples, while biquadratic instances lie outside.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file defines the open residual instance interface and shows a total residual decider would decide zeros of signed bivariate polynomials. It gives a complete decision on the base-counter-monotone stratum via a payload-axis check with a finite coefficient certificate. It also gives complete decisions on payload-only and base-only univariate strata with failing witnesses and separating controls.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: A total residual decision would decide bivariate zeros; completeness holds only on the monotone and univariate strata, with the general case left open.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: A total residual decider would decide bivariate zeros, and the monotone and univariate strata are completely decidable with witnesses.
assumptions: classical reasoning via the classical tactic in residual_decider_implies_bivariate_zero_decider

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file embeds signed bivariate positivity into the slope-two residual branch. It defines natural and signed bivariate polynomials, their evaluation and squares, and the wrapper, lifting and encoding into recursor data. It proves the encoded residual equals the source polynomial and every encoding lies in the open branch, so the open class contains bivariate positivity and zero-existence.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: The slope-two open class is as hard as signed bivariate positivity over Nat times Nat, which limits the successor decision.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Slope-two residuals exactly encode signed bivariate positivity, so the open successor branch contains the full bivariate positivity problem.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file decides positivity for signed polynomials with one positive and one negative monomial. It proves the decision—positive constant dominating a smaller or vanishing negative constant—is sound and complete with extracted failing pairs and residual adapters. It supplies accept and reject controls outside earlier monotone and affine families and a decision table.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: On one-versus-one monomial differences orientation holds exactly for dominating constants; all other shapes fail with an explicit pair.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: One-versus-one monomial positivity is completely decidable by constant domination with explicit failing pairs.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file defines terms, substitution, one-hole contexts and the two recursor root rules over an arbitrary first-order signature with inert symbols. The free schema embeds injectively, its image is closed under root and contextual rewriting, and steps between embedded terms are exactly embedded free steps. The barrier cell and coupling inequality are transported to every signature schema. Strictly monotone inert operations plus root orientation give termination of the full contextual relation, proved by the coupled 1+sum polynomial.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: No measure can orient the duplicating rule inside the barrier cell given by WrapUnboundedAt and GainBoundedAt, for root steps and for contextual steps. Termination of the full signature holds only with strictly monotone inert operations.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: The recursor over every first-order signature terminates contextually via the coupled 1+sum polynomial interpretation.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file defines schema isomorphisms preserving base, succ, wrap and recur, with orientation of the duplicating rule transferring both ways. It identifies the free schema as the empty-inert instance and KO7 as the seven-symbol instance with integrate, merge and eqW inert, matching KO7 recursor rules to signature root steps. It characterizes the embedding image as inert-free terms and generated elements, proving agreement there but exhibiting distinct isomorphisms by variable renaming and by swapping merge with eqW.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Any two schema isomorphisms agree on elements generated from base by the four operations, with uniqueness at empty variable type for the free instance. Global uniqueness fails because a variable permutation and the merge/eqW swap give distinct isomorphisms.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: The free schema and KO7 are exact signature-schema instances with orientation transfer, unique on the generated fragment but not globally.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This file defines size-change graphs of dependency pairs with strict subterm arcs and weak equality arcs, plus soundness of arcs as rewriting descent. It closes pair graphs under composition and states the criterion that every idempotent loop graph carry a strict self-arc. Using the infinite Ramsey theorem for pairs, the criterion implies well-founded minimal chains and termination under the variable condition. The system f(x) to f(x) fails the criterion with an infinite chain, while the free recursor satisfies it.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: If every idempotent closure graph has a strict self-arc then minimal chains are well-founded and rewriting terminates. The loop f(x) to f(x) has only a weak self-arc, so the criterion fails and an infinite minimal chain with nontermination occurs.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: The size-change criterion is sound for minimal chains and proves the free recursor terminating, while its absence permits looping.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This module gives an exact executable extractor for the free recursor successor call with its source-target-call occurrence relation. It proves extraction exactness, strict decrease of a call rank, and well-foundedness of transformed calls. It then proves generic connector-aware chain soundness where strict pairs plus weak connectors yield well-founded chains, keeping source termination as a separate lexicographic bridge. A control with empty calls but a looping source shows pair well-foundedness alone does not imply source termination.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Well-founded transformed calls do not imply well-founded source steps without a separate source bridge. The empty transformed relation is well-founded while the self-looping source with no calls is not.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Exact extraction and connector-aware chain soundness hold, but pair termination alone cannot serve as source termination.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: This module defines target-native ranks for graph, process and CPS carriers that strictly decrease on the existing lift steps, plus a generalized graph with an auxiliary weight. It introduces a finite replication-free pi fragment and a lambda-mu with CPS fragment, proving size-based termination and step-for-step simulation. A sharing-aware quasi-interpretation with strict contraction and a noninjective read-back control is proved. The exact transports and native arguments are assembled into the ORI-6 capstone package.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Each termination claim is confined to its selected fragment, finite pi without replication and the named lambda-mu and CPS syntax, and to the listed native steps. Sharing breaks injectivity of read-back while strictly dropping native size.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Target-native ranks, fragment simulations and sharing contraction assemble into the ORI6 native-method package.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: Defines locally nameless System T terms with iterator It and recursor R and full reduction including beta and congruence rules. Defines the iterator fold from the free step-duplicating schema into System T and proves it is an injective closed embedding whose image is exactly the abstraction-, bound-variable- and recursor-free terms, transporting the exact orientation criterion, coupling inequality, barrier cell and four-cell verdicts and strong normalization to the image. Defines schema morphisms, characterizes maps out of the free schema as folds, and pulls non-barrier verdicts back along surjective morphisms and the image isomorphism. Proves no two-hole context realizes the recursor rule, gives the three-place wrapper with its coupling and barrier theorems, and defines two polynomial weights showing the free weight orients the iterator but fails on the recursor while a squared-counter weight orients both, yielding strong normalization of all abstraction-free terms.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: The iterator image lies inside the orientation framework and inherits orientation, coupling, four-cell classification and termination, while the recursor lies outside the two-hole shape: no two-hole context realizes its rule and the free polynomial weight orients the iterator but fails the recursor uniformly. Adding the squared counter crosses this limit and orients both shapes.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Every abstraction-free System T term is strongly normalizing under full System T reduction with iterator and recursor.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: Defines when a measure orients a relation and proves non-orientability persists under relation extension while well-foundedness persists under restriction. Defines renaming through an equivalence and proves it preserves and reflects termination, and defines positive simulations requiring a nonempty target path for each source step to transfer well-foundedness without injectivity. Gives a looping single-state source simulated by zero steps into an empty terminating target to show reflexive simulation does not transfer termination. Provides two deleted-premise controls: a zero-rule contextual relation oriented by term size that misses the duplicating root step, and a confluent fork-join source whose identity embedding reflects steps with closed image but drops joining steps so the target fork is not joinable.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Termination and non-orientability transfer under subrelations, bijective renaming and positive simulation, but the transfer fails once a source step may use zero target steps, the contextual relation omits the duplicating root step, or an embedding reflects steps without preserving them.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Positive simulations and bijective renamings transfer termination while reflexive zero-step simulations, root-missing contextual relations, and reflection without preservation do not.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.summary: Restates the vector-order results for orientation: all-coordinate strict, genuine lexicographic, and strict-primary-weak comparisons each force payload-blindness of the relevant coordinates. Records that the two standard orders are well-founded while the PrimaryFirstLt compatibility relation is cyclic and ill-founded from dimension three, with counter-only vectors orienting both standard orders and payload-reading coordinates blocking orientation. Introduces the counter-then-payload vector that is lexicographically oriented while keeping payload in later coordinates, showing only the primary coordinate must be payload-blind, and notes matrix fixed-row and row-sum readings are scalar-dominated.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.boundary: Genuine lexicographic and strict-primary-weak orders are well-founded only with a payload-blind primary coordinate, while the PrimaryFirstLt compatibility relation is cyclic and not well-founded in dimension at least three. Lexicographic orientation still permits payload dependence in later coordinates.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/OrientationClos.conclusion: Genuine lexicographic comparison orients the counter-then-payload vector, proving that orientation forces only the primary coordinate to be payload-blind while later coordinates may still read the payload.

OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/PathOrderRows.l.summary: This file defines carriers for eleven path-order rows of the termination-method ledger, including KBO variants with status, quasi-precedence, AC matching, ordinal weights, applicative encoding and polynomial weights, plus equational and permutation RPO certificates and POP* and Cichon rows. It proves that every coefficient-weighted variable-condition order refuses the duplicating rule dupSrc to dupTgt because the payload variable count strictly increases, and that currying and AC rearrangement preserve those counts. It constructs the KO7 LPO and polynomial-rank escapes that orient all root rules and full-context closure, including a nontrivial AC-compatible order, a nonidentity permutation status, and the POP* impossibility and Cichon bound.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/PathOrderRows.l.boundary: Coefficient-weighted variable-condition orders cannot orient dupSrc to dupTgt because the payload count strictly increases, while equational and permutation RPO variants built on the KO7 LPO and polynomial rank do orient all root and full-context steps. The same count increase defeats predicative safe-linear POP* certificates.
OperatorKO7/Meta/Methods/PathOrderRows.l.conclusion: No coefficient-weighted KBO variant or predicative POP* certificate orients the KO7 duplicating rule, while the KO7 LPO and polynomial rank yield nontrivial AC and permutation RPO certificates orienting all root and full-context steps.
assumptions: Generalized KBO rows assume a type K with CommSemiring and PartialOrder instances
Transfinite KBO uses Ordinal weights and transfiniteKBOWitness is marked noncomputable
Lambda-free KBO certificates carry transitivity and well-foundedness fields
