OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.summary: Defines oriented steps, finite traces that store every occurrence, and guarded root, contextual and level-stratified step data with conditional histories. Proves the data faithful: nonemptiness is equivalent to level steps, level conversions and conditional conversion, with reversal, concatenation and occurrence-count laws. Shows identical data reuse is stored twice while erased proofs are equal, so erasure is not injective, and that argument lifting projects while root steps do not.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.boundary: Data stores every step occurrence including repeats and nested condition histories, while the erased Prop conversion forgets counts and admits no recovery function. Projection to an argument holds only under the origin lifting condition and fails for root steps, with outer length bounded by total occurrences.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.conclusion: Nonemptiness of level data and of conditional histories is equivalent to level steps, level conversion and conditional conversion, with explicit length and occurrence laws and sharp failure of erasure injectivity and root projection.
assumptions: Classical.choice to supply nonempty data for each condition slot in contextStepData_faithful
No sorry, admit, axiom, native_decide, partial, unsafe or opaque; kernel checked

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.summary: Provides abstract reflexive-transitive closure, conversion, joinability and confluence with conversion-to-joinability under confluence. Defines conditional rules, oracle-indexed root and context steps, and the level stratification where conditions are discharged by lower-level conversions, with monotonicity. Exhibits a two-rule system with a level-1 step b to c and a level-2 step f(b,c) to a alongside an equal-arguments level-1 firing.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.boundary: Level 0 has no steps and a level n+1 step fires only when its condition instances are convertible with level-n steps, so level 1 needs syntactically equal conditions. The levels form an increasing chain, with genuinely conditional firings appearing at level 2 and above.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.conclusion: Conditional rewriting is stratified into monotone levels with a concrete level-2 example where f(b,c) reduces to a via the condition b convertible to c.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.summary: Studies deletions retaining a normalizing path to each original normal form, proving under UNR they preserve normal forms, normal-form reductions, conversion, weak normalization and confluence with the same normalizer. Encodes policies as products of nonempty successor rows with order, minimality and exact finite counts, plus a sink-SCC realization criterion on finite carriers. Develops rule families as safety plus cut-hitting transversals with finite minima, and exhibits bundled loops, duplicate minima and different-size minima showing minimality forces neither termination nor functionality.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.boundary: Retaining at least one successor at every original redex preserves the prescribed normalizer over a terminating base, while deleting all successors at a redex loses it. A least deletion policy exists only for deterministic bases, and minimal selections can still loop, branch or differ in size.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.conclusion: Conservative deletions preserve normal forms, reductions, conversion and confluence with a common normalizer, classified by successor rows and cut transversals with exact finite counts and sharp minimality counterexamples.
assumptions: SN R for terminating deletion and normalizer classification
Fintype X for finite policy counts and sink-SCC reachability
Classical.choice and Classical.byContradiction for successor and cut choices
LinearOrder W for finite minimum-cost rule selections

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.summary: Develops the tilde algebra over the doubled signature with constructor, destructor and full tildes and their splitting and flip laws. Defines Sigma-closure and CT as the least Sigma-closed extension with unfold, idempotence and variable lemmas. Proves Lemma 29 halves, preservation of constructor compatibility, carrier-relative transitivity criteria, and the matching invariant Lemma 33, substitution lift Lemma 34 and Corollary 35 in direct and bar-tilde forms.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.boundary: Context closure adds no pairs with a variable endpoint, and constructor-compatible relations decompose only on constructor-topped terms. Transitivity is established inside a subterm-closed carrier under base absorption, with no claim outside that carrier.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.conclusion: Constructor-compatible relations lift through substitutions and destructor tildes into context closure, yielding Corollary 35 for two root contractions of one rule.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.summary: Defines constructor-topped terms and constructor compatibility and proves a compatible conversion is consistent. Reduces the consistency half of RTA open problem 79 to compatibility of the constructor translation via Corollary 16. Extends the reduction with Theorem 69 extensions to unique normal forms for conversion and reduction, and shows the hypothesis inhabited by the empty system.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.boundary: Conversion decomposes applications only after the constructor translation; on a raw system with a rule such as f(a) to g(b) it fails. Hence compatibility implies consistency and unique normal forms for the translated system and transfers back, but not without the translation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.conclusion: Constructor compatibility of every translated system in the class plus extensibility yields consistency and UN for conversion and reduction of the original system.
concepts: unique normal forms for conversion and reduction
assumptions: Needs two distinct variables x != y for Theorem 69 extensions
NonOmegaOverlapping and TRS.RhsDetermined for systems in the class
No sorry, admit, axiom, native_decide, partial, unsafe or opaque

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.summary: Builds the doubled signature with constructor, destructor and erasing labellings and the shared destructor-pattern shape. Collects patterns as proper application nodes and defines translated and pattern rules forming the constructor translation. Proves Lemma 13 relabelling, strict and reflexive-transitive forward simulation, the backward step-or-equality dichotomy, and Proposition 15 with Corollary 16 that consistency is preserved and reflected.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.boundary: A translated step either projects to a genuine source step or, for pattern rules, erases to equality. Forward simulation is strict transitive closure with a reflexive-transitive corollary, so conversion is preserved and reflected without a step bijection.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Con.conclusion: A TRS is consistent if and only if its constructor translation is consistent, via exact strict forward simulation and backward dichotomy.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.summary: Proves cancellation for the Dershowitz-Manna order over the linear carrier LevelKey needed by decreasing-diagram pasting. Shows irreflexivity, emptiness below nonempty multisets, and domination by one element, then trichotomy for descending sorted lists and hence totality on unequal multisets. Collapses the reflexive closure to equality or one strict step and deduces left and right cancellation of a common additive context.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.boundary: Equal multisets are never strictly DM-below each other while distinct multisets over linear LevelKey are always comparable, and a common additive context cancels on either side.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.conclusion: The strict DM order is total on unequal LevelKey multisets and both strict and reflexive orders cancel a common additive context.
assumptions: LevelKey is linearly ordered, giving trichotomy of heads
Mathlib Dershowitz-Manna order, its well-foundedness and transitivity, plus Multiset sort

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.summary: This file defines the generic decreasing-diagram certificate carrier: labelled steps, below-label closures, local peaks and the exact van Oostrom valley shape. It proves that with one label and the empty order, every literal diamond is a decreasing peak. It supplies a four-node diamond fixture and checks that it satisfies both the diamond and decreasing-peak properties.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.boundary: With the empty strict order on one label, a literal diamond is decreasing; with a nonempty label order a peak must satisfy the full below-label valley shape to be decreasing.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.conclusion: A literal one-label diamond yields a decreasing local peak for the empty order, exemplified by the four-node diamond.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.summary: This file closes the global decreasing-diagrams metatheorem for the route-R2 label order. It defines mirroring and reflexive base measured joins and proves that every finite labelled peak has a measured joining diagram by well-founded induction on the peak measure. Forgetting labels yields confluence of the unlabelled relation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.boundary: If every local peak is decreasing for the well-founded LevelLabelLt order, every finite labelled peak joins and the unlabelled relation is confluent; without that local hypothesis the induction gives no global join.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.conclusion: Local decreasingness for the route-R2 label order implies confluence of the unlabelled rewrite relation.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.MeasuredJoin.mirror

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.allPeaksMeasured
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Under hypothesis hdec : AllLocalPeaksDecreasing step LevelLabelLt, for all LPath proofs ha : LPath step source left as and hb : LPath step source right bs there is a MeasuredJoin step as bs left right.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.UnlabelledConfluent

relations.explanation: The measured-peak theorem is the induction that forgets labels to give unlabelled confluence.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.summary: This file introduces the non-strict Dershowitz-Manna order and the measured-join structure for two labelled input paths. It proves that each arm of an exact decreasing valley is bounded by the original two-label peak, distinguishing the absent and present optional-step cases. The main theorem turns every decreasing local valley into a measured join meeting the global induction bound.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.boundary: A local decreasing valley stays inside the two-label peak measure, with the optional opposite-label step giving equality when present and a strict drop when absent.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.conclusion: Every route-R2 decreasing local valley produces a measured join satisfying the global lexicographic-maximum bound.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If every element of M is < a then strict DM M {a}.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: A measured join for input label lists records a join state, left and right output label lists, joining labelled paths, and DMLe bounds of each completed arm by the peak measure.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For a peak with hypothesis hdec : peak.Decreasing LevelLabelLt, there is a MeasuredJoin on ([leftLabel],[rightLabel]) satisfying the lexicographic-maximum induction bound.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.summary: This file proves the measured-diagram pasting theorem corresponding to Lemma 3.5. It shows DM comparison preserves strict downsets and that the first diagram's left measure yields a downset inclusion. Pasting two compatible measured joins gives a measured join for the extended inputs with concatenated right outputs.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.boundary: Two measured joins paste into a larger measured join only through the residual inequalities; without those residuals the concatenated outputs need not respect the peak measure.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.conclusion: Two compatible measured diagrams paste into a measured join for the concatenated inputs.
assumptions: classical choice for decidable filtering in noncomputable paste construction

relations.explanation: Pasting composes two measured joins by residual composition on the left and downset absorption on the right.

relations.explanation: The downset inclusion is the step3 consequence of the first diagram's left measure used in the paste.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.summary: This file packages order-theoretic lemmas for Lemma 3.5: downset composition, equivalence of lexMax and list downsets, submultisets below in DM order, and antitonicity of filtering. Its main result is dominated addition, which adds keys dominated by the replacement witness without exceeding the DM bound.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.conclusion: Filtering by generated downsets is antitone and dominated keys can be added without exceeding the DM bound.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If M <= N as multisets then DMLe M N.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If every key below small is below big then DMLe (filter by big) (filter by small).

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Under hMN : DMLe M N, if every q in Q is below N but not below M then DMLe (Q+M) N.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.summary: This file develops whole-prefix downsets and the load-bearing strict-measure lemma for decreasing diagrams. It proves append and partition identities for lexMax and that replacing the downset part by a nonempty lexMax is strictly increasing. The two hypothesis-decrease theorems make recursive peaks with a joining output strictly smaller when the retained input is nonempty.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.boundary: A measured diagram yields a strictly smaller recursive peak only when the retained input side is nonempty; with an empty tau the construction gives no strict decrease.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.conclusion: A measured diagram with nonempty input makes every recursive peak with the joining output strictly smaller.
assumptions: classical choice for decidable downset filtering in removeBelowList and belowListPart

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.BelowList

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.removeBelowList_add
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Filtering a sum by a generated downset distributes over the summands.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.removeBelow_removeBelowList_eq_cons
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Filtering below a head after filtering below the tail equals filtering below the whole cons list.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.lexMax_append
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: lexMax (xs ++ ys) equals lexMax xs plus lexMax ys filtered below xs.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Every key below an actual source label is below some key retained by lexMax of the nonempty list.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If labels != [] then lexMax labels != 0.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: A strict DM decrease followed by zero or more DM decreases is strict.

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If DMLe M N then DMLe (M+K) (N+K).

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.summary: This file turns full measured-join inequalities into residual form by additive DM cancellation of the common input prefix. It proves strict and non-strict DM comparison are preserved by whole-prefix downset filtering. Left and right residuals and their converses rebuild each arm of the measured inequality.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.conclusion: Measured inequalities are equivalent to their residual forms after cancelling the common input prefix.
assumptions: classical choice for decidable downset filtering inherited from removeBelowList

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For D : MeasuredJoin step tau sigma, DMLe (removeBelowList (lexMax D.leftOutput) tau) (lexMax sigma).

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For D : MeasuredJoin step tau sigma, DMLe (removeBelowList (lexMax D.rightOutput) sigma) (lexMax tau).

keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If DMLe (removeBelowList (lexMax output) tau) (lexMax sigma) then DMLe (lexMax (tau ++ output)) (peakMeasure (tau,sigma)).

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.summary: This file implements the induction substrate for decreasing diagrams: label lists, labelled paths, below-label predicates, and the lexicographic-maximum multiset measure. It proves paths compose, forget to ordinary reductions, retain below-label properties, and that below-label lists are strictly below singleton and pair multisets. Peak pairs are ordered by the Dershowitz-Manna extension, proved well-founded.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.boundary: Finite labelled reductions are measured by lexicographic-maximum multisets ordered by the well-founded Dershowitz-Manna order, enabling induction where the raw label lists have no well-founded peak order.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dec.conclusion: Label lists carry a well-founded peak measure via lexicographic maxima and the Dershowitz-Manna order.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Des.summary: This file lifts tight-closure consistency through constructor translation and the Theorem 69 signature extension to unique normal forms. It proves per-extension criteria for UNconv and UNred, transport of syntactic descent, and source-level rhs-below-root corollaries. The capacity system witnesses non-vacuity with unique normal forms, while the KO7 fence fails overlap and is excluded.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Des.boundary: Systems whose constructor-translation right-hand sides descend below the left root have unique normal forms, while overlapping systems like the KO7 fence lie outside the class and the theorem does not apply to them.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Des.conclusion: Non-omega-overlapping right-variable-safe systems with descending right-hand sides have unique normal forms, a class inhabited by the capacity system and excluding KO7.
assumptions: Nontrivial nu for distinct variables in the Theorem 69 extension
Infinite nu for fresh variables and capacity corollaries
WellFounded lt for the source label order

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.SymbolOccurs
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: SymbolOccurs g t holds when g heads some application node of term t.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dow.summary: This file defines the DownStep operator with the corrected destructor-tilde clause and Down as its least closed relation, with six introduction rules and an induction principle but no built-in transitivity. It proves Down contains rewriting, is Sigma-closed, and, in a constructor TRS, is constructor-compatible. With Lemma 28 this gives consistency on variables.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dow.boundary: In a constructor TRS the Down relation is constructor-compatible and consistent. For arbitrary TRSs with no constructor restriction consistency fails, and Down is built without a transitivity clause so transitivity must be proved rather than assumed.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dow.conclusion: In a constructor TRS the least Down relation is Sigma-closed, constructor-compatible and consistent.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dup.summary: Defines rule-labelled rewriting where each step carries its rule's label and proves erasure to ordinary rewriting. For the duplication family R_r with f(x) to g(x,...,x) and a to b it classifies the atom peak g(a,...,a) from f(a) to f(b) and the nested peak g(f(v),...) from f(f(v)) to f(g(v,...)). It shows the atom peak is decreasing exactly when the atom label is below the duplication label, with a priority repair and unconditional valleys for r=0,1, while for r at least 2 the nested peak has no decreasing valley for any irreflexive relation, so no constant-per-rule labeling makes all peaks decreasing although the peak is ordinarily joinable. It also lands the minimum-level refutation with unchanged names and identifies its system as R_2.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dup.boundary: Constant-per-rule labelings repair the atom peak exactly when the atom label is below the duplication label, unconditionally for r=0,1. For r≥2 no such labeling with irreflexive comparison makes every local peak decreasing: the nested peak stays non-decreasing while remaining ordinarily joinable.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Dup.conclusion: For r≥2 no constant-per-rule labeling with irreflexive comparison makes all local peaks of R_r decreasing, and the universal minimum-level closeout is false with its system identified as R_2.
assumptions: label relation is irreflexive `∀ l, ¬ lt l l` for atom classification, nested obstruction and no-go theorems
copy-count hypothesis `2 ≤ r` for atom classification with r≥2 and for nested obstruction
kernel-checked; header states no `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `native_decide`, `partial`, `unsafe` or `opaque`

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Exa.summary: Instantiates Huet's system F(x,x) to A, F(x,G(x)) to B, C to G(C) and proves F(C,C) reaches distinct normal forms A and B, so UNconv and UNred fail while the variable condition holds. It proves finite non-overlap but omega-overlap for Huet, showing finite overlap is insufficient. It instantiates Klop's system A to C(A), C(x) to D(x,C(x)), D(x,x) to E and proves A reaches E and C(E) with C(E) and E non-joinable, so confluence fails although the system is non-omega-overlapping and right-determined.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Exa.boundary: Huet's system is finitely non-overlapping yet omega-overlapping and loses unique normal forms on the omega side. Klop's system is non-omega-overlapping yet non-confluent, so the class does not guarantee confluence.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Exa.conclusion: Huet's system is finitely non-overlapping yet fails UNconv and UNred, and Klop's non-omega-overlapping system has A reaching E and C(E) with E and C(E) non-joinable hence non-confluent.
assumptions: classical reasoning in `ClassExamples.noCommonGeneralisation_of_distinct_nullary_rhs` via explicit `classical`
DecidableEq typeclasses for substituted-variable and matching lemmas
kernel-only; header states no `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `native_decide`, `partial`, `unsafe` or `opaque`

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Fen.summary: Encodes the eight-rule KO7 kernel as first-order rules including the eqW reflexive and difference branches. It proves the two eqW left sides unify, so KO7 lies outside NonOverlapping and NonOmegaOverlapping. It exhibits distinct normal forms void and integrate(void) joined through the eqW diagonal, so UNconv and UNred fail, and proves the diagonal one-step peak has no common reduct. It packages these as an explicit counterexample showing the non-omega-overlap hypothesis is required.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Fen.boundary: KO7 satisfies the right-hand-side variable condition but lies outside NonOverlapping and NonOmegaOverlapping, and on that outside side UNconv, UNred and diagonal joinability all fail.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Fen.conclusion: KO7 satisfies the variable condition but lies outside non-overlap, fails UNconv and UNred, and exhibits a non-joinable one-step diagonal peak, so the non-omega-overlap hypothesis is required.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Fen.summary: Defines the encoding from KO7 traces to first-order terms and proves each of the eight kernel steps is a root contraction of the encoded fence system. It embeds the three-state Fork3 diagram at the eqW(void,void) diagonal and proves the embedding is injective with exact reflection of the step relation. It concludes the diagonal contains the initial Fork3 atom and transports the non-joinable fork to the encoded system.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Fen.boundary: Joinability holds for the simulated kernel steps, but the encoded eqW diagonal pair remains non-joinable, preserving the fence UN failure in the kernel.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Fen.conclusion: Every kernel step simulates as an encoded fence step and the eqW diagonal contains the initial non-joinable Fork3, whose non-joinability persists after encoding.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Fin.summary: Develops a generic inflationary finite saturation with a cardinality bound forcing stabilization. It proves simultaneous first-order matching complete and builds an exact finite root-step table without fresh-variable restrictions. It defines executable one-step and layered tables for the relativized Down relation and proves the bounded iteration computes DownOn exactly, yielding decidable membership directly from carrier and rules.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Fin.conclusion: DownOn over a finite carrier is computed exactly by bounded iteration to card squared and is decidable directly from carrier and rules.
assumptions: DecidableEq on symbols and variables for executable matching and finite tables
Classical choice via letI Classical.decEq in `bounded_saturation` for the mathematical bound
no `sorry` visible; iteration needs no monotonicity hypothesis

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Fin.summary: Enumerates finite class partitions over subterm support and checks symbol and argument compatibility to decide shared omega-unifiability. It proves the Boolean test, the certificate search, and the whole-system non-omega-overlap test sound and complete against the infinite-term semantics, including exact search-size bounds. It shows every positive instance has a rational finite-state solution and exhibits the occurs-check pair as omega-unifiable but not finitely unifiable, plus returned counterexamples for forbidden overlaps.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Fin.boundary: Finite unifiability holds on one side and fails on the other for the occurs-check pair: it is omega-unifiable and rationally solvable but admits no finite substitution unifier.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Fin.conclusion: Shared and ordinary omega-unifiability and whole-system non-omega-overlap are decidable by finite enumeration, every positive case has a rational finite-state witness, and the occurs-check separates omega from finite unification.
assumptions: DecidableEq on symbols and variables for executable decisions and tables
classical reasoning in `finite_certificate_complete` and `rationalOmegaUnifiableShared_of_omega`
M-type infinite-term substitution semantics for soundness and completeness

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/For.summary: The file develops parent-function forests for proof graphs with determinism by construction and termination as well-foundedness of the parent step. It defines chains Reach, the valley equivalence EqvOn, and the relativized constructor tilde hatEq with its compatibility property. It proves chains from one node are comparable, EqvOn is an equivalence containing the edges, and constructor compatibility of DownOn. It proves adding or replacing one parent edge preserves termination exactly when the new target cannot return to the source, with natural-number examples.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/For.boundary: Replacing the parent of a by b preserves termination when there is no old path from b to a and destroys it when such a return path exists.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/For.conclusion: Well-foundedness of a parent graph survives a single edge addition or replacement exactly when the new target cannot reach the source, and the relativized invariant is constructor-compatible.
assumptions: classical reasoning for if-then-else on terms through open scoped Classical and the classical tactic
WellFounded induction on the parent step

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Glo.summary: The file makes failure of unique normal forms first-class as a structure with two normal forms, a conversion between them, and a proof they are distinct. It proves negating UNconv is equivalent to existence of distinct convertible normal forms and to inhabitation of the failure structure, with a positive dual formulation. It instantiates the theory for the KO7 system, where void and integrate void are terminal normal forms with a conversion, yielding a concrete failure object and the corresponding non-UNconv theorems.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Glo.boundary: UNconv holds exactly when no GlobalUNFailure object exists, so inhabitation of the failure type is the precise dividing line between unique and non-unique normal forms.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Glo.conclusion: Failure of UNconv is exactly inhabitation by two distinct convertible normal forms, instantiated by void and integrate void for KO7.
assumptions: classical logic for witness extraction from a negated universal through the classical tactic with push_neg in the ¬UNconv to Nonempty direction

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Gro.summary: The file proves the positive counterpart to open-term obstructions: ground terms behave rigidly under omega-unification. It defines groundness as absence of variable occurrences and shows renamings agree on ground terms so the two rename-apart copies coincide. It proves distinct ground terms never omega-unify, in both finite-closure and infinite-substitution forms, and that a ground term omega-unifying with a left-hand side is a substitution instance via a matcher read off the certificate with classical choice. Consequently no subterm of a ground normal form omega-unifies with a rule left-hand side.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Gro.boundary: Groundness is the dividing line: distinct ground terms never omega-unify and ground overlap collapses to matching, while open normal forms can omega-unify with left-hand sides.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Gro.conclusion: Distinct ground terms never omega-unify and any ground omega-unifier with a left-hand side is a matching instance, so ground normal forms have no omega-unifiable subterms.
assumptions: classical choice to read a matcher off the finite certificate through the classical tactic and choose

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Hub.summary: The file builds the fresh-variable substrate for the generic hub transform over Nat variables. It defines the fresh base above all variables of a rule and the pairing-based fresh codes with a collapse decoder that fixes below-base variables and recovers the original variable from fresh codes. It proves the codes are injective, disjoint from below-base variables, and fix original left- and right-hand-side occurrences, leaving the right-hand side verbatim under collapse.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Hub.boundary: Variables below the base are fixed by collapse while fresh codes lie at or above the base and never collide with them.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Hub.conclusion: Pairing-based fresh codes give a total injective fresh namespace above each rule whose collapse restores original variables and leaves the right-hand side verbatim.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Hub.summary: The file assembles the per-rule hub invariants into the conditional rule hubCRule and system transform linHub. It proves each hubCRule meets the transfer specification LinearizesRule and the method specification with left-linear split left-hand side, hence linHub is a method-faithful linearization. It composes this with the decreasing-diagrams pipeline to obtain UNconv and UNred of the original system from local decreasingness of labellings of linHub, including the fully canonical minimal-level form. It witnesses non-vacuity on a linear rule with no conditions and the nonlinear diagonal with split occurrence and one hub condition.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Hub.boundary: Local decreasingness of the hub linearization yields uniqueness for the original system, and the transform emits conditions exactly when the source is nonlinear.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Hub.conclusion: Any stepwise locally decreasing labelling of the canonical hub linearization gives UNconv and UNred of the original Nat-variable system.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Hub.summary: The file proves validity and coverage invariants for hub conditions generated by the stateful splitter. It shows the executable splitter conditions coincide with a semantic trace over occurrence lists and that every condition has both endpoints in the transformed left-hand side with exact collapse equations. It proves every split variable is fixed or carries its own hub pair, counts conditions, and characterizes emptiness as left-linearity with concrete duplicate examples.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Hub.boundary: Generated conditions vanish exactly on left-linear sources and appear on repeats, with the number of conditions plus final hubs balancing the number of source occurrences.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Hub.conclusion: Every generated hub condition is a valid occurring pair with exact collapse laws and every split variable is fixed or conditioned, with no conditions exactly for left-linear sources.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Hub.summary: The file defines the stateful hub occurrence splitter that keeps the first occurrence as hub and renames later duplicates to fresh pairing codes with equality conditions. It proves collapse after splitting reconstructs the original term whenever all source occurrences lie below the fresh base, with a rule-level corollary. It proves the occurrence counter advances by the source occurrence count and the number of conditions is bounded by that count.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Hub.boundary: Collapse is the identity exactly when every source occurrence lies below the reserved base, with the occurrence counter and condition count tied to the source occurrence list.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Hub.conclusion: Splitting with a global occurrence counter and hub set reconstructs under collapse and emits at most one condition per source occurrence.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Hub.summary: The file proves left-linearity of the representative-hub split via its variable-list semantics. It defines the seen-state update, hub accumulation, and output encoding that emits unseen variables unchanged and seen variables as fresh codes. It shows under the fresh-base bound the encoding is duplicate-free and disjoint from initial hubs, the term splitter traces this encoding exactly, and every rule-specific split left-hand side is left-linear.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Hub.summary: The file proves generic fresh right-hand-side theorems and refutes the unrestricted reconstruction statement. It shows a rule l to y with y absent from l contracts every instance to every term, hence every pair of terms is convertible, with the one-rule FreshRhs system as instance. It formalizes forbidden source overlaps and two reconstruction disjunctions, unrestricted and restricted by the variable condition. It exhibits the three-rule fixture d to z, F(x,x) to a, and F(a,b) to b that is non-omega-overlapping, violates only the variable condition, has universal conversion and failing UNconv, whose hub linearization has a feasible overlap with no omega-unifier and no forbidden overlap.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Hub.boundary: The right-hand-side variable condition is the dividing line: without it the feasible hub overlap need not reconstruct to an original omega-unifier nor a forbidden overlap.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Hub.conclusion: The three-rule system with a bare fresh variable refutes the unrestricted reconstruction disjunction while satisfying non-omega-overlap and violating only the variable condition.
assumptions: noncomputable Classical.choice for the substitution update at an arbitrary variable type through open Classical and noncomputable updateAt
decidable equality for the concrete Nat fixture discharged by decide and simp

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Lem.summary: This file defines heterogeneous valuation of terms across variable types and the three-pair LinkRel relation. It builds the finite closure Cert36 from constructor-compatible equivalence pairs plus LinkRel. It proves the reformulated Lemma 36 that two destructor-headed left-hand sides sharing a root are omega-unifiable when their instances are related, without forming infinite terms.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Lem.boundary: Constructor-compatible symmetric transitive S relating the direct-subterm instances yields omega-unifiable destructor-headed left-hand sides; without that related-instances hypothesis the conclusion need not hold. The finite Cert36 witness replaces the infinitary U-function and Proposition 32, so no infinite rational tree is required for this certificate-level lemma.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Lem.conclusion: Two destructor-headed left-hand sides with a shared root whose instances are related by a symmetric transitive constructor-compatible equivalence are omega-unifiable via the finite Cert36 certificate.
assumptions: classical tactic in proof of lemma36; kernel-only per header, no sorry, admit, axiom, native_decide, partial, unsafe, opaque or axioms

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Cert36

relations.explanation: Cert36 is the finite closure witness supplied to prove OmegaUnifiable, avoiding infinite terms and Proposition 32.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Lem.summary: This file proves Lemma 52 that a deterministic terminating grey subrelation has its equivalence closure inside DownOn with constructor-topped pairs in the graph's constructor tilde. It deduces Corollary 53 one-edge extension and Lemma 56 constructor-closure of complete graphs. It defines destructor steps, destructor-class reachability, quotient classes, redex-priority targets, targeted graphs, local Sigma-closure, universality and equality-completeness. It proves Lemma 62 Sigma-closure for complete targeted graphs and reduces universality to root-step closure. It constructs equality-complete and all-guided targeted graphs by forest spanning, rerooting and retargeting.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Lem.boundary: Deterministic terminating grey subrelations stay inside DownOn and complete graphs close under constructors, while arbitrary or incomplete grey extensions need not. Universality for complete targeted graphs reduces to closure under coalgebra root steps, marking the exact remaining obligation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Lem.conclusion: Deterministic terminating grey subrelations lie inside the invariant, complete graphs are constructor-closed, and complete targeted graphs are Sigma-closed with universality reducing to root-step closure, all realized by equality-complete targeted constructions.
assumptions: Classical.choice and Quotient for target selection and BarClass; noncomputable definitions using Classical.choose and Nat.find; Coalgebra and ConstructorRules hypotheses for main lemmas; classical tactic in proofs

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Lem.summary: This file defines what it means for a relation S to be a consistency invariant on a carrier A for a system R, following Definition 30, and instantiates it for the one-rule system d(x) to x on {d(d(c)), d(c), c}. It proves that the DownOn relation on this carrier is Sigma-closed and satisfies the semantic-fork critical-pair condition, hence is a consistency invariant. It constructs a complete targeted proof graph on the same carrier that is not universal and shows the printed fiber-induction promotion and any edge-preserving repair to a universal graph fail. It then records the two incomparable maximal complete graphs with upper and lower targets and identifies the lower-target choice as the universal one, matching the n equal to 2 instance of the chain classification.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Lem.boundary: The consistency-invariant hypothesis holds for DownOn on this carrier while the universality conclusion fails for a complete targeted graph, so the printed Lemma 64 implication does not cross this carrier. Maximal complete graphs need not be greatest: the upper-target and lower-target graphs are both maximal and incomparable, with universality on the lower side and failure on the upper side.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Lem.conclusion: On the carrier with rule d(x) to x, DownOn is a consistency invariant while a complete targeted proof graph is not universal, so Lemma 64 as printed fails.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Lev.summary: This file defines LevelLabel with condition level and unifier rank and its pair representation. It defines the strict lexicographic LevelLabelLt order with an explicit disjunctive characterization and proves it well-founded. It defines BelowEither labels below a peak and notes no peak-decrease claim is made.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Lev.boundary: Well-founded lexicographic labels are available below peak labels. Their existence alone does not join any peak, so decreasingness remains unproved in this file.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Lev.conclusion: Lexicographic condition-level and unifier-rank labels form a well-founded strict order with an explicit two-case characterization.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Lin.summary: This file defines variable occurrence and the hub LinearizesRule specification with verbatim right-hand side and collapse map, plus bidirectional IsLinearization. It adds the method-faithful layer requiring left-linearity and occurrence-list linearity. It proves self-linearization and binary-diagonal linearization with a concrete f(x,x) to a example, distinguishing transfer existence from left-linearity.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Lin.boundary: Splitting f(x,x) into f(x,y) with condition x to y is left-linear exactly when x and y are distinct; without x not equal y the transfer witness still exists but method-faithful left-linearity fails. The trivial self-linearization always satisfies the transfer specification but defeats the transform purpose on non-linear rules.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Lin.conclusion: Hub linearization with verbatim right-hand side and collapse map gives a transfer specification whose method-faithful left-linear layer includes the binary diagonal and its concrete example.
assumptions: DecidableEq nu for binary-diagonal constructions; kernel-only per header, no sorry, admit, axiom or native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Mod.summary: The file defines signature interpretations and the condition that a model refutes all non-trivial overlaps of a conditional linearization. It proves that such a model yields absence of feasible overlaps and unique normal forms with respect to conversion, and that the quotient by conversion is complete for this certificate format. It instantiates the method on the F45 system F(x,x,x) to x beside F(G(y,A),G(B,A),y) to y with a two-element Boolean model, and shows no model certificate exists for Huet's system or the KO7 kernel.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Mod.boundary: A linearization admits a model certificate exactly when it has no overlap whose conditions are convertible; Huet's system and the KO7 kernel lie on the failing side because their linearizations have feasible overlaps. The certificate implies unique normal forms, but construction of a certificate for every non-omega-overlapping system is left open and would solve RTA problem 79.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Mod.conclusion: The F45 system has unique normal forms with respect to conversion via a two-element model, and model certificates are complete for the no-feasible-overlap hypothesis.
assumptions: conditional linearization IsLinearization R C
left-linearity CLeftLinear C
variable condition on right-hand side variables of R
noncomputable quotient model using Quotients and choice
no sorry axiom native_decide partial unsafe per audit

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.summary: The file defines conversion saturation that adds every conversion edge from a non-normal source and shows it preserves normal forms and conversion. It proves saturation is confluent exactly under unique convertible normal forms and gives a confluent extension characterization. It further characterizes when saturation shares normal-form reductions and describes saturation as a signature adjunction.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.boundary: Saturation is confluent exactly when the original relation has unique convertible normal forms, and it is strongly normalizing only when the original relation is empty. Normal-form reductions of the saturation agree with the original exactly under a non-normal normal-form property.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.conclusion: Unique convertible normal forms hold exactly when the conversion saturation is confluent and provides a confluent extension preserving normal forms and conversion.
assumptions: arbitrary binary relation R without decidability or finiteness assumptions
classical case splits on normal forms in some proofs
no sorry axiom native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.summary: The file fixes vocabulary for arbitrary relations with finite reduction and equivalence conversion and defines normal forms, weak and strong normalization, unique normal forms, confluence and the normal-form property. It proves basic transport, invariance and joining lemmas and the implications between confluence and uniqueness. The empty relation supplies a non-vacuous model of weak normalization, confluence and termination.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.boundary: Under weak normalization, confluence coincides with uniqueness of normal forms, while in general confluence strictly implies uniqueness; strong normalization forbids two-cycles and implies weak normalization. The empty relation lies on the always-confluent and terminating side on every carrier.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.conclusion: Confluence, unique normal forms, termination and weak normalization are related by implications that become equivalences under weak normalization, with the empty relation as a universal model.
assumptions: arbitrary type and binary relation with Mathlib ReflTransGen and EqvGen
classical reasoning for accessible normalizing points and choice of normal forms
no sorry axiom native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.summary: The file introduces conversion to normal form, hereditary normalization, the normalizing carrier and its restricted core, and forward-invariant predicates. It proves the core is always weakly normalizing and characterizes uniqueness and reflection through the core. It builds quotient maps between normal forms, the core quotient and the ambient conversion quotient with injectivity and surjectivity criteria.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.boundary: Ambient conversion agrees with internal conversion of the normalizable core exactly under unique convertible normal forms; otherwise reflection can fail. Normalization, hereditary normalization and conversion to normal form coincide exactly under the normal-form property with uniqueness.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.conclusion: Unique convertible normal forms are equivalent to confluence of the normalizable core together with reflection, with bijective quotients between normal forms and conversion classes.
assumptions: arbitrary carrier and relation without finiteness
Classical choice for chosen normal forms and class representatives via Classical.choose
noncomputable class label and quotient equivalences
no sorry axiom native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.summary: The file builds finite three- and five-point relations checked by decide and proves their reduction, conversion and normalization behavior. It separates reduction uniqueness from conversion uniqueness and conversion uniqueness from weak normalization, the normal-form property and confluence. It gives deletion, union, graph-isomorphism and shortest-path controls showing what extensions preserve and what monotonicity fails.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.boundary: Finite relations separate the properties: reduction uniqueness does not imply conversion uniqueness, and conversion uniqueness does not imply weak normalization, the normal-form property or confluence. Adding one edge can restore weak normalization and confluence while preserving normal forms and conversion, and unions of terminating realizations need not terminate.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.conclusion: Small three- and five-point relations separate unique normal forms, weak normalization, confluence and the normal-form property and witness non-monotonicity of shortest paths.
assumptions: Fintype and DecidableRel for finite truth checks via decide
DecidableEq for element types
kernel reduction only, no evaluator axiom
no sorry axiom native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.summary: The file defines finite paths with lengths, root distance as a classical minimum, and the shortest-path subrelation that keeps distance-lowering edges. It proves shortest restrictions are terminating and preserve realization and classifies functional minimal and least realizations. It shows saturation collapses to the maximal relation and computes edge counts and commutation conditions.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.boundary: A least realization exists exactly when the normalizer is idempotent and fibers have at most two points; otherwise rerouting gives incompatible realizations with no common subrealization. Saturation and shortest-path restriction commute exactly when the normalizer is the identity.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.conclusion: Realizations contain functional minimal subrealizations, least realizations are classified by fiber size, and saturation and shortest paths collapse to root stars with exact edge counts.
assumptions: arbitrary carrier with realizing relation and idempotent normalizer
Classical choice for functional subrelations and minima
noncomputable root distance as classical minimum with zero default
Fintype for edge counting
no sorry axiom native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.summary: The file defines relations realizing a prescribed normalizer and the maximal compatible relation. It proves compatibility plus reachability characterizes realization and that realizability is equivalent to idempotence. It connects weak normalization plus confluence to existence of normalizers and reformulates reachability as hitting all root-free cuts.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.boundary: A relation realizes a normalizer exactly when it is compatible with the maximal relation and reaches every root; in particular a map is realizable exactly when idempotent and the empty relation realizes only the identity. Failure of realization is witnessed by a closed root-free cut with no exiting edge.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.conclusion: Realizability is equivalent to compatibility plus reachability, equivalently to cut-hitting, and holds exactly for idempotent maps with weak normalization plus confluence characterizing existence.
assumptions: arbitrary carrier and prescribed normalizer map
Classical choice for normal-form selection and cut complements
no sorry axiom native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.summary: The file works on first-order terms with contexts and substitutions and characterizes closure of the maximal realization. It proves variable preservation is inherited by steps and gives a greatest variable-preserving realization. It reduces rule safety to side conditions, gives an executable admission test, and shows saturation of an erasing rule introduces a fresh variable with no ordinary presentation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.boundary: Saturation of a variable-preserving erasing system adds a fresh-variable edge, so no ordinary variable-preserving term system presents the saturated step relation. Rule admission is safe exactly on the displayed rule sides when the maximal relation is closed under contexts and substitutions.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.conclusion: Contexts and substitutions preserve the maximal realization, rule extensions are characterized by side conditions, and saturation can force fresh variables with no ordinary presentation.
assumptions: first-order Term syntax with existing Step Rewrite and Subst
DecidableEq on variables and symbols for executable admission
classical reasoning for maximal-relation closure characterization
no sorry axiom native_decide

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.summary: The file studies observation relative to attained images with unique decoders and adequacy conditions for recovering targets and normal forms. It proves normalized transport yields uniqueness and confluence under separation. It defines conjugation through carrier equivalences and shows confluence, termination, realization, distances and minimality transfer across conjugates.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.boundary: An observation recovers targets or normal forms exactly when equal observations imply equal targets or convertible points; otherwise decoding fails. Normalized transport yields uniqueness and confluence only under separation of distinct normal forms by the target invariant.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Nor.conclusion: Observation, decoding and conjugation preserve normalization structure exactly under kernel and intertwining hypotheses, classifying least realizations across equivalent carriers.
assumptions: arbitrary source and target relations with carrier equivalence
Classical choice for attained-image decoders and normal forms
noncomputable observation equivalences
order homomorphisms for conjugacy
no sorry axiom native_decide

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Normalization.conjugate_realizes

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Normalization.realizationConjugacy
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Under intertwining, conjugation gives an order isomorphism between realizing families.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Normalization.conjugate_max_rel
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Under intertwining, conjugation sends the maximal relation to the maximal relation.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Normalization.conjugate_shortestRel
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Conjugation sends shortest-path relations to shortest-path relations of conjugates.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Normalization.conjugate_minimalRealizes

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Normalization.conjugate_leastRealizes
