OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Ove.summary: The file defines two-substitution unifiability and its omega consequence, the subterm and proper-subterm relations, and five overlap classes: non-overlapping, non-omega-overlapping, deterministic root steps, almost non-omega-overlapping, and constructor analogues. It proves that non-omega-overlapping implies non-overlapping in general and constructor forms, and that the proper-subterm half of almost non-omega-overlapping follows from non-omega-overlapping with no side condition.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Ove.boundary: Inside a non-omega-overlapping system the only allowed omega-overlap is a rule with itself at the root. The omega condition implies the finite condition, so finite unifiability refutes fewer overlaps than omega-unifiability.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Ove.conclusion: Every non-omega-overlapping TRS is non-overlapping in general and constructor forms and yields the proper-subterm clause of almost non-omega-overlapping.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Unifiable
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Unifiable s t holds exactly when there exist substitutions a b with Subst.apply a s = Subst.apply b t, with the two sides taken over disjoint variable sets.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.OmegaUnifiable.of_unifiable
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If Unifiable s t then OmegaUnifiable s t; every finite unifier gives an infinite-term unifier because finite terms inhabit the infinite universe.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Subterm
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Subterm s t is inductively generated by refl with s = t and arg with s in an argument of t; it carries the position quantifier of CC1 with the root singled out by s = r1.lhs.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.ProperSubterm
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: ProperSubterm s t holds when t = .app f args for some f, args and a with a in args and Subterm s a.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.NonOverlapping
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: NonOverlapping R holds when for all r1 in R, r2 in R and all s with Subterm s r1.lhs and s.isApp = true, if Unifiable s r2.lhs then r1 = r2 and s = r1.lhs.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.NonOmegaOverlapping
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: NonOmegaOverlapping R holds when for all r1 in R, r2 in R and all s with Subterm s r1.lhs and s.isApp = true, if OmegaUnifiable s r2.lhs then r1 = r2 and s = r1.lhs, where OmegaUnifiable is the certificate proved equivalent to infinite-term semantics.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Deterministic
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Deterministic R holds when root steps are functional: for all s t u, rootStep R s t and rootStep R s u imply t = u.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.AlmostNonOmegaOverlapping
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: AlmostNonOmegaOverlapping R is the conjunction of: for all r1 in R, r2 in R and all s with ProperSubterm s r1.lhs and s.isApp = true, not OmegaUnifiable s r2.lhs; and Deterministic R.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.ConstructorNonOverlapping
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: ConstructorNonOverlapping R holds when for all r1 in R and r2 in R with r1 != r2, not Unifiable r1.lhs r2.lhs.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.ConstructorNonOmegaOverlapping
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: ConstructorNonOmegaOverlapping R holds when for all r1 in R and r2 in R with r1 != r2, not OmegaUnifiable r1.lhs r2.lhs.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.NonOverlapping.of_nonOmegaOverlapping
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If h : NonOmegaOverlapping R then NonOverlapping R, because every finite unifier is an omega-unifier.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.ConstructorNonOverlapping.of_nonOmegaOverlapping
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If h : ConstructorNonOmegaOverlapping R then ConstructorNonOverlapping R, by the same unifiability-to-omega implication.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.properSubterm_clause_of_nonOmegaOverlapping
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If h : NonOmegaOverlapping R then for all r1 in R, r2 in R and s with ProperSubterm s r1.lhs and s.isApp = true, not OmegaUnifiable s r2.lhs, since a proper subterm is strictly smaller and cannot equal r1.lhs.

relations.explanation: The omega condition is stronger, so refuting omega-unifiability implies refuting finite unifiability.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.NonOverlapping.of_nonOmegaOverlapping

relations.explanation: Same strengthening in constructor-signature form.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.ConstructorNonOverlapping.of_nonOmegaOverlapping

relations.explanation: Derives the proper-subterm half of the almost class from the CC1 exception being inapplicable to proper subterms.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.properSubterm_clause_of_nonOmegaOverlapping

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Pro.summary: The file defines grey edges and proof graphs as deterministic partial parent functions with membership, termination, subsumption and grey-edge conditions. It proves the valley-form equivalence coincides with the equivalence closure of parent edges, and that constructor-topped chains carry only constructor-tilde edges, yielding constructor compatibility as Lemma 47. It defines extensions, complete graphs and the finite root set, proving every graph over a strongly finite coalgebra has a complete extension by induction on root count as Proposition 55.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Pro.boundary: A deterministic terminating grey subrelation has its equivalence closure inside down_A. Completeness is obtained only over strongly finite coalgebras via the finite root-count measure.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Pro.conclusion: The equivalence represented by a proof graph is constructor-compatible, and every proof graph over a strongly finite coalgebra has a complete extension.
assumptions: classical choice for Finset filtering of normal forms
strongly finite coalgebra as list A with Coalgebra
Terminating parent function for proof graphs
ConstructorRules hypothesis for Lemma 47

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Grey
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Grey A R E a b holds when rootStep R a b or barRel (DownOn A R) a b or hatEq E a b, where E is the graph's own equivalence.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: PGraph A R has a parent function par, mem_edge keeping edges inside A, Terminating par, sub stating EqvOn implies DownOn, and grey stating every parent edge is Grey for EqvOn; determinism is built in as a partial function.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.eqvOn_iff_eqvGen_up
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For a proof graph rho, EqvOn A rho.par a b holds iff a in A and b in A and Relation.EqvGen (Up rho.par) a b, with no termination hypothesis.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.NF
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: PGraph.NF rho a holds when rho.par a = none.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.hatEq_of_grey_of_conTopped
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Assuming ConstructorRules R, if ConTopped a and Grey A R E a b then hatEq E a b, since root and destructor-tilde sources cannot be constructor-topped.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.conTopped_of_reach
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Assuming ConstructorRules R and that every g-edge is Grey, if Reach g a s and ConTopped a then ConTopped s.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.hatEq_of_reach
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Assuming Coalgebra A and ConstructorRules R, for a proof graph rho with Reach rho.par a s, if a in A and ConTopped a then hatEq (EqvOn A rho.par) a s.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.constructorCompatible
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Assuming Coalgebra A and ConstructorRules R, for a proof graph rho with ConTopped a and ConTopped b, if EqvOn A rho.par a b then hatEq (EqvOn A rho.par) a b.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.Extends
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Extends alpha beta holds when every parent edge alpha.par a = some b remains beta.par a = some b.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.Extends.refl
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Every proof graph rho satisfies rho.Extends rho.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.Extends.trans
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If alpha.Extends beta and beta.Extends gamma then alpha.Extends gamma.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.Complete
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Complete rho holds when for every beta with rho.Extends beta, also beta.Extends rho; equality is extensional at the edge relation.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.nf_iff
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For a proof graph rho, rho.NF a holds iff rho.par a = none.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.roots
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: roots rho is the Finset of a in A with rho.par a = none, by classical filtering of A.toFinset.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.roots_ssubset_of_proper
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If alpha.Extends beta but not beta.Extends alpha then beta.roots is a strict subset of alpha.roots.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.exists_complete_extension
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every proof graph rho over A there exists beta with rho.Extends beta and beta.Complete, by strong induction on the finite root count.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.ReachN
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: ReachN g n a b is the parent chain from a to b with explicit length n, with refl and head cases, so Lemma 52 can induct on n.

relations.explanation: Valley-form equivalence is exactly the equivalence closure of parent edges on members of A.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.eqvOn_iff_eqvGen_up

relations.explanation: Constructor compatibility is proved via constructor-tilde edges along chains.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.constructorCompatible

relations.explanation: A proper extension consumes at least one graph normal form, giving the finite measure for completeness.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.exists_complete_extension

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Pro.summary: The file develops variable-occurrence lemmas, the growth substitution forcing occurrence inclusion from the variable condition, and transport of omega-unifiability across label erasure. It proves the root-overlap clause and the three clause-(ii) cases to obtain Proposition 22 that the constructor translation of a non-omega-overlapping RhsDetermined system over infinite variables is strongly almost non-omega-overlapping, hence a consistency invariant by Corollary 45. It then shows the Huet translation is a counterexample to the same implication from the finite-root almost hypothesis.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Pro.boundary: With NonOmegaOverlapping plus RhsDetermined and an infinite variable supply the constructor translation is strongly almost non-omega-overlapping, while with only the finite-root AlmostNonOmegaOverlapping hypothesis the implication fails as the Huet translation shows.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Pro.conclusion: The constructor translation of a non-omega-overlapping RhsDetermined system over infinite variables is strongly almost non-omega-overlapping and hence carries a consistency invariant, while the finite-root almost hypothesis alone does not imply it.
assumptions: [Infinite nu] for fresh variables in clause (ii)
[Nonempty nu] for listSubst
classical choice for growAt and listSubst
NonOmegaOverlapping R and TRS.RhsDetermined R hypotheses for prop22

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.growAt
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: growAt x f is the substitution sending x to Term.app f [Term.var x] and fixing every y != x.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.determinedBy_of_occurs_subset
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If every variable occurring in r occurs in l then Term.DeterminedBy r l.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.occurs_of_determinedBy
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Given a symbol f and h : Term.DeterminedBy r l, if VarOccurs x r then VarOccurs x l, by growing x and comparing sizes.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.transRule_rhsDetermined
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If Rule.RhsDetermined rule then Rule.RhsDetermined (transRule rule).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.omegaUnifiable_of_destructorPattern
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If OmegaUnifiable (destructorPattern l) (destructorPattern l') then OmegaUnifiable l l', by erasing labels.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.prop22_root_overlaps
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all r1 and r2 in constructorTranslation R and all s with ProperSubterm s r1.lhs and s.isApp = true, not OmegaUnifiable s r2.lhs.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.prop22_rule_rule
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Assuming NonOmegaOverlapping R and TRS.RhsDetermined R, if r in R and r' in R with OmegaUnifiable (transRule r).lhs (transRule r').lhs then the two translated rules have a common generalisation whose right variables occur on the left.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.prop22_rule_pattern
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Assuming NonOmegaOverlapping R, if r in R and n in patternNodes R then not OmegaUnifiable (transRule r).lhs (patternRuleOf n).lhs.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.prop22_pattern_pattern
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Assuming [Infinite nu], if OmegaUnifiable (patternRuleOf n).lhs (patternRuleOf m).lhs then the two pattern rules have a common generalisation over fresh variables whose right variables occur on the left.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.prop22
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Assuming [Infinite nu], NonOmegaOverlapping R and TRS.RhsDetermined R, StronglyAlmostNonOmegaOverlapping (constructorTranslation R).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.consistencyInvariant_constructorTranslation
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Assuming [Infinite nu], NonOmegaOverlapping R and TRS.RhsDetermined R, ConsistencyInvariant (constructorTranslation R) (Down (constructorTranslation R)).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.listSubst
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: listSubst emb L is the substitution reading off list L through Function.invFun emb, requiring [Nonempty nu].

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.freshVars
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: freshVars emb k is the list of k distinct fresh variables ((range k).map emb).map Term.var.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.HuetTranslation.rootRoleLabel
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: rootRoleLabel n is .inr n when n = 1 and .inl n otherwise.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.HuetTranslation.translated_lhs_omegaUnifiable
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: OmegaUnifiable (transRule HuetSystem.ruleAA).lhs (transRule HuetSystem.ruleAB).lhs, by mapping Huet.lhs_omegaUnifiable across rootRoleLabel.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.HuetTranslation.translated_rules_no_common_generalisation
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: There is no Nonempty CommonGeneralisation between transRule HuetSystem.ruleAA and transRule HuetSystem.ruleAB, because their nullary right-hand sides differ.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.HuetTranslation.not_stronglyAlmostNonOmegaOverlapping
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Not StronglyAlmostNonOmegaOverlapping (constructorTranslation HuetSystem.trs).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.HuetTranslation.finite_root_almost_counterexample
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: AlmostNonOmegaOverlapping HuetSystem.trs and TRS.RhsDetermined HuetSystem.trs hold while not StronglyAlmostNonOmegaOverlapping (constructorTranslation HuetSystem.trs).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.HuetTranslation.current_almost_translation_implication_false
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: It is false that for all R : TRS Nat Nat, AlmostNonOmegaOverlapping R and TRS.RhsDetermined R imply StronglyAlmostNonOmegaOverlapping (constructorTranslation R).

relations.explanation: Moves the non-omega-overlapping plus variable condition to the strongly almost property of the translated system.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.prop22

relations.explanation: The Huet translation has omega-unifiable left-hand sides with no common generalisation, blocking the finite-root implication.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.HuetTranslation.not_stronglyAlmostNonOmegaOverlapping

relations.explanation: Provides a system that is almost non-omega-overlapping and RhsDetermined but whose translation is not strongly almost.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.HuetTranslation.finite_root_almost_counterexample

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Rat.summary: The file defines unification closures without an occurs check, rename-apart copies, and certificate-level omega-unifiability, alongside explicit infinite M-type terms, substitutions and their application. It proves the finite certificate coincides with infinite-term unifiability in shared and rename-apart forms, gives clash instruments for symbol equality and argumentwise decomposition, and builds certificates from class lists and finite substitutions. The occurs-check pair and Huet's left-hand sides are proved omega-unifiable with explicit infinite witnesses yet not finitely unifiable.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Rat.boundary: Finite unification requires the occurs check while omega-unification drops it. Hence x with f(x) and Huet's pair are omega-unifiable but not unifiable, and only a symbol clash inside a closure refutes omega-unifiability.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Rat.conclusion: Finite union-find certificates coincide extensionally with explicit infinite-term unifiers, while the occurs-check and Huet pairs separate omega-unifiability from finite unifiability.
assumptions: Classical.choice for chooseQAppRep, closureViewQ and unfoldQ
Quotient and Setoid for certificate classes
Mathlib PFunctor.M final coalgebra for InfTerm
Unit target alphabet suffices for infinite witnesses

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.UnifClosure
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: UnifClosure E holds when E is reflexive, symmetric and transitive and related applications share their symbol with pointwise related arguments; no occurs check is required.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.OmegaUnifiableShared
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: OmegaUnifiableShared s t holds when some E with UnifClosure E relates s and t, treating variables as shared.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.leftCopy
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: leftCopy t is Term.mapVar Sum.inl t, the left side of rename-apart.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.rightCopy
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: rightCopy t is Term.mapVar Sum.inr t, the right side of rename-apart.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.OmegaUnifiable
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: OmegaUnifiable s t is OmegaUnifiableShared (leftCopy s) (rightCopy t), the certificate-level omega-unifiability with disjoint variable sets.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.infTermP
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: infTermP sigma nu is the polynomial functor with variable leaves and finite-arity application nodes whose M-type is the infinite term universe.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.InfTerm
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: InfTerm sigma nu is PFunctor.M (infTermP sigma nu), the potentially infinite first-order terms.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.InfApply
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: InfApply r maps a finite term homomorphically into InfTerm by sending .var x to r x and .app f xs to InfTerm.app f with mapped children.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.InfiniteOmegaUnifiableShared
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: InfiniteOmegaUnifiableShared s t holds when some r : InfSubst sigma nu Unit has InfApply r s = InfApply r t.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.InfiniteOmegaUnifiable
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: InfiniteOmegaUnifiable s t is InfiniteOmegaUnifiableShared (leftCopy s) (rightCopy t), the rename-apart infinite-term semantics.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.omegaUnifiableShared_iff_infinite
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all s t, OmegaUnifiableShared s t holds iff InfiniteOmegaUnifiableShared s t.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.omegaUnifiable_iff_infinite
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For all s t, OmegaUnifiable s t holds iff InfiniteOmegaUnifiable s t.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.UnifClosure.symbol_eq
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If hE : UnifClosure E and E (.app f xs) (.app g ys) then f = g.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.UnifClosure.args_forall₂
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If hE : UnifClosure E and E (.app f xs) (.app g ys) then List.Forall₂ E xs ys; variable-to-application pairs remain permitted.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.omegaUnifiable_of_unifier
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If Subst.apply a s = Subst.apply b t for substitutions a b then OmegaUnifiable s t, via a combined rename-apart substitution.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.classesRel
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: classesRel Cs a b holds when a = b or a and b lie jointly in some C in Cs.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.unifClosure_classesRel
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: classesRel Cs is a UnifClosure when classes sharing a member have the same members and applications in one class agree on symbol with argumentwise related arguments.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.OccursCheck.xTm
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: xTm is Term.var 0 over Nat.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.OccursCheck.fxTm
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: fxTm is Term.app 0 [.var 0] over Nat.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.OccursCheck.omegaUnifiableShared
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: OmegaUnifiableShared xTm fxTm via the single-class certificate.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.OccursCheck.infiniteOmegaUnifiableShared
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: InfiniteOmegaUnifiableShared xTm fxTm, from the certificate via omegaUnifiableShared_iff_infinite.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.OccursCheck.not_unifiable
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: There is no r : Subst Nat Nat with Subst.apply r xTm = Subst.apply r fxTm, since the size would exceed itself.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Huet.lhs₁
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: lhs1 is .app 1 [.var 0, .var 0], that is F(x,x).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Huet.lhs₂
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: lhs2 is .app 1 [.var 0, .app 2 [.var 0]], that is F(x,G(x)).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Huet.lhs_omegaUnifiable
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: OmegaUnifiable lhs1 lhs2 via the two-class certificate with the lower class containing the renamed variables and G(x2).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Huet.lhs_infiniteOmegaUnifiable
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: InfiniteOmegaUnifiable lhs1 lhs2, from lhs_omegaUnifiable via omegaUnifiable_iff_infinite.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Huet.lhs_not_unifiable
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: There are no a b : Subst Nat Nat with Subst.apply a lhs1 = Subst.apply b lhs2, since a unifier would force a term strictly larger than itself.

relations.explanation: Finite certificate and explicit infinite-term substitution semantics coincide.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.omegaUnifiable_iff_infinite

relations.explanation: The occurs equation is omega-unifiable yet admits no finite unifier, separating the two notions.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.OccursCheck.not_unifiable

relations.explanation: Huet's left-hand sides are omega-unifiable but not finitely unifiable, so the system is non-overlapping yet omega-overlapping.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Huet.lhs_not_unifiable

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Rew.summary: The file proves substitutivity of single steps and sequences under substitution and multi-argument congruence for rewriting all arguments of an application. The suffix lemma with an untouched prefix and a pointwise map lemma support the induction. These are the facts Lemma 14 uses as substitutivity and compatibility of rewriting.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Rew.conclusion: Rewrite steps and sequences are preserved under substitution and under pointwise rewriting of application arguments.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.Rewriting.Step.subst
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every substitution t and Step R s u, Step R (Subst.apply t s) (Subst.apply t u).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.Rewriting.StepStar.subst
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every substitution t and StepStar R s u, StepStar R (Subst.apply t s) (Subst.apply t u).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.Rewriting.StepStar.args_append
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For fixed f and prefix pre, if List.Forall2 (StepStar R) xs ys then StepStar R (.app f (pre ++ xs)) (.app f (pre ++ ys)).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.Rewriting.StepStar.args
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If List.Forall2 (StepStar R) xs ys then StepStar R (.app f xs) (.app f ys).

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.Rewriting.forall₂_map_map

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Rul.summary: The file defines arbitrary rule families with root steps, steps, conversions, normal forms and unique normal forms, plus finite parts and membership from lists. It proves transfer lemmas between finite TRSs and families, that every family conversion has a finite support certifying the same conversion, and characterizations of normality and UN failure by finite witnesses. The strongest link is the equivalence between the UN theorem for all finite systems and for all rule families under non-omega-overlapping and RhsDetermined hypotheses.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Rul.boundary: Every conversion, normal form and UN failure for an arbitrary rule family is already witnessed by a finite sub-system, so infinite presentations add no new counterexamples beyond finite ones.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Rul.conclusion: The unique-normal-form theorem for all finite systems is equivalent to its statement for all arbitrary rule families, with every conversion and every UN failure finitely witnessed.
assumptions: classical choice in not_un_iff_finite_witness
finite TRS as List of rules with membership

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.summary: The file defines wrapped tower terms tower c d i, their finite carrier list, and a singleton erase system deleting one destructor layer. It proves the carrier is a coalgebra, the system is constructor and strongly almost non-overlapping, and characterizes root, bar and grey steps and reachability on towers. It builds executable parent, pick, graph, target and targeted structures with completeness and universality characterizations, culminating in a complete universal repair and a depth classification of bad graphs.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.boundary: Depths 0 and 1 force every complete targeted chain graph to be universal, while depth at least 2 admits complete nonuniversal chain graphs. Repairing a complete nonuniversal graph to a universal one must change a parent edge, and completeness cannot be omitted.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.conclusion: At depth at least two there are complete nonuniversal chain graphs, yet every chain admits a complete universal repair that must change an edge, and such bad graphs exist exactly when 2 is less than or equal to n.
assumptions: DecidableEq sigma for executable towerTest, parent, pick, graph and target
ValidTarget n k required for graph, target and targeted constructions
0 less than n and 2 less than or equal n hypotheses for depth results
Classical.decEq sigma used in existence and repair theorems
No sorry, axiom or native_decide visible

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.summary: The file defines the ambient ArgumentChainComposition input and VariableWitness positions for collapsing steps. It proves argument pairs inherit relations from destructor tildes and that every right-hand-side variable has a witness via Lemma 33. It proves the trichotomy for two seed-related root steps of the constructor translation into collapsing, DCT destructor-tilde, or pattern hat-tilde cases.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.boundary: Under non-omega-overlapping, rhs-determinedness, and an ambient constructor-compatible equivalence containing the seed, overlapping translated redexes fall into the three stated cases; without those overlap and variable hypotheses the identification can fail.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.conclusion: Any two seed-related root redexes of the constructor translation contract to collapsing variable instances, a DCT destructor tilde, or a pattern constructor tilde.
assumptions: NonOmegaOverlapping R
TRS.RhsDetermined R
ArgumentChainComposition S E
ConstructorCompatible S
No sorry, axiom or native_decide visible

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.summary: The file defines fiber-argument representation for proof graphs, requiring every destructor-fiber step to carry a destructor tilde of the graph equality, and proves that for complete targeted graphs on finite coalgebras of strongly almost non-omega-overlapping constructor systems, universality is equivalent to this fiber condition. It proves the residual direction that fiber representation implies representation of all root rewrites via Theorem 37, and gives common-reduct criteria for completeness and universality. It constructs a three-term example for the rule d(x) to x with a complete universal targeted graph containing both a root rewrite and a nonidentity fiber step, and a trap graph on the same terms that is complete and targeted but not universal. It then proves repair and reconstruction results distinguishing edge-completeness from equality-completeness and locating an unrepresented argument whenever a root step is missed.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.boundary: A complete targeted proof graph is universal exactly when its destructor-fiber steps are argument-represented. Completeness alone does not imply universality, and equality-preserving reconstruction alone does not repair the trap counterexample.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.conclusion: For complete targeted graphs on finite coalgebras of strongly almost non-omega-overlapping constructor systems, universality coincides with fiber-argument representation, and completeness alone does not guarantee it.
assumptions: Coalgebra A
ConstructorRules R
StronglyAlmostNonOmegaOverlapping R for the residual and equivalence
Complete graph for the residual direction
EqualityComplete graph for the obstruction theorems
classical reasoning in forall₂_exists_aligned_failure and repair constructions
Lean kernel with axiom checks recorded in Section7FiberReductionReach per header

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.TermTargetedPGraph.missing_root_has_unrepresented_argument

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.summary: The file defines the unproved finite-carrier transitivity of DownOn for constructor translations, its class-level form, and the finite targeted-model supply that would imply it. It proves that the model supply yields finite-carrier transitivity via context absorption, that finite-carrier transitivity yields global Down transitivity, and that this yields unique normal forms for conversion and reduction through the Summit and signature-extension theorems. It also proves that three-fold DownOn composition is equivalent to transitivity on a carrier.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.boundary: Unique normal forms follow from finite-carrier Down transitivity, but that transitivity and the finite targeted-model supply implying it are explicitly unproved for non-omega-overlapping right-variable-safe systems.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.conclusion: Assuming the unproved finite-carrier Down transitivity or the finite targeted-model supply implying it, every non-omega-overlapping right-variable-safe system over infinite variables has unique normal forms for conversion and reduction.
assumptions: NonOmegaOverlapping S and TRS.RhsDetermined S for class systems
Coalgebra A for finite carriers
Infinite nu for the final unique-normal-form theorems
FiniteCarrierDownTransitive and Section7FiniteTargetedModels are explicitly unproved assumptions, not results
kernel-only with no sorry, admit, axiom, native_decide, partial, unsafe or opaque per header

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.FiniteCarrierDownTransitive
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For a system S, the relativized invariant DownOn for the constructor translation is transitive on every finite subterm-closed carrier A.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Section7TranslationDownOnTrans
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every system S over the extended signature with NonOmegaOverlapping and RhsDetermined hypotheses, FiniteCarrierDownTransitive holds.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Section7FiniteTargetedModels
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For every class system S with NonOmegaOverlapping and RhsDetermined hypotheses and every coalgebra A, there exists a complete targeted proof graph whose root steps are all represented.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.down_transitive_of_finiteCarrierDownTransitive
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If FiniteCarrierDownTransitive holds for S, then Down for the constructor translation of S is globally transitive.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.finiteCarrierDownTransitive_of_finiteTargetedModels
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If every coalgebra A has a complete targeted graph with all root steps represented, then FiniteCarrierDownTransitive holds for S, via context absorption.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Section7TranslationDownOnTrans.of_finiteTargetedModels
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The class-level finite-model supply implies the class-level missing transitivity theorem.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.htrans_of_section7TranslationDownOnTrans
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The class-level missing theorem supplies the global Down-transitivity input required by UNconv_of_section7.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.UNconv_of_section7TranslationDownOnTrans
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If Section7TranslationDownOnTrans holds and nu is infinite, then every system R with NonOmegaOverlapping and RhsDetermined hypotheses has unique normal forms for conversion.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.UNred_of_section7TranslationDownOnTrans
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Under the same missing-theorem, infinite-variable, NonOmegaOverlapping and RhsDetermined hypotheses, R has unique normal forms for reduction.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.UNconv_of_section7FiniteTargetedModels
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If the finite targeted-model supply holds and nu is infinite, then every R with NonOmegaOverlapping and RhsDetermined hypotheses has unique normal forms for conversion.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.downOn_threeFold_iff_transitive
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: On a carrier, three-fold DownOn composition for all quadruples holds if and only if binary DownOn transitivity holds.

relations.explanation: The theorem derives per-system finite-carrier transitivity from the per-carrier complete root-representing graph supply.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.finiteCarrierDownTransitive_of_finiteTargetedModels

relations.explanation: The final conversion-uniqueness result is moved from the finite-carrier transitivity setting through the Summit and signature-extension chain.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.UNconv_of_section7TranslationDownOnTrans

relations.explanation: The lemma identifies the three-fold class-merge composition required by every sound repair with DownOn transitivity on that carrier.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.summary: The file introduces the guarded relation that is semantically intended only on a finite carrier and proves an argumentwise elimination for it. It proves that sigma-closure on a subterm-closed coalgebra lifts to global sigma-closure of the guard. It deduces that congruence closure cannot create a new pair between carrier members, and specializes this bridge to the equality of a complete targeted proof graph.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.boundary: Congruence closure adds no new pairs between members of a subterm-closed carrier when the base is signature-closed there; the guarantee does not extend off the carrier.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.conclusion: On a finite coalgebra, congruence closure creates no new equalities between carrier members once the base is locally closed, letting finite arguments consume global Theorem-37 conclusions.
assumptions: Coalgebra A with subterm closure
SigmaClosedOn A E for the bridge
ConstructorRules R and Complete graph for the targeted specialization
kernel checked with no new axiom

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.OnGuard
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: OnGuard A E of a and b means membership of a and b in A implies E of a and b.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.forall₂_onGuard_elim
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If all members of as and bs lie in A, then List.Forall₂ of OnGuard A E over as and bs implies List.Forall₂ of E.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.SigmaClosedOn.onGuard_sigmaClosed
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a subterm-closed coalgebra and E is sigma-closed on A, then the guarded extension OnGuard A E is globally sigma-closed.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.SigmaClosedOn.eq_of_CT
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, E is sigma-closed on A, a and b are in A, and CT E holds of a and b, then E holds of a and b.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.TermTargetedPGraph.eqvOn_of_CT_of_complete
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, R has constructor rules, rho is targeted with complete graph, a and b are in A, and CT of the graph equality holds, then the graph equality holds of a and b.

relations.explanation: Local signature closure on a subterm-closed carrier is lifted to a globally sigma-closed guarded relation.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.SigmaClosedOn.onGuard_sigmaClosed

relations.explanation: The targeted graph equality instantiates the general finite-carrier elimination of congruence closure.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.TermTargetedPGraph.eqvOn_of_CT_of_complete

relations.explanation: The collapse uses the guarded sigma-closed extension to run the global closure least principle.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.SigmaClosedOn.eq_of_CT

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.summary: The file defines a join step as a root contraction or replacement of destructor arguments by invariant-related arguments, globally and on a finite carrier with explicit membership. It proves the terminal equality-or-constructor-tilde relation is symmetric and contained in the invariant, that the invariant absorbs join paths on the left, and the two-sided joinability characterizations for Down and DownOn. Both directions use only the six generating clauses, with no overlap, determinism or transitivity hypotheses.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.boundary: Down equals joinability to equal-or-constructor-tilde endpoints with no overlap, determinism or transitivity hypotheses; the terminal equality-or-hat relation itself is only reflexive and symmetric, not transitive.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.conclusion: Down and DownOn hold exactly when both sides join by root and destructor-argument steps to equal or constructor-tilde-related witnesses.
assumptions: no overlap hypothesis, no root-step determinism and no transitivity per header
carrier version uses only explicit memberships with no subterm closure of A
kernel checked with no new axiom

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.JoinStep
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: JoinStep R relates a to b when rootStep holds or barRel of Down R holds, namely a destructor-topped term whose arguments are replaced by Down-related arguments.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.eq_or_hatRel_down_symm
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The terminal relation of equality or hatRel of Down is symmetric.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Down.of_eq_or_hatRel
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If a equals b or hatRel of Down holds, then Down R holds of a and b.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Down.of_joinStep_reach
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If a reaches a prime by JoinStep and Down holds from the prime to b, then Down holds from a to b.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.down_iff_join
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Down R of t and u holds if and only if t and u reach by JoinStep terms that are equal or related by hatRel of Down.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.JoinStepOn
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: JoinStepOn A R relates a to b when both are in A and either rootStep holds or barRel of DownOn A R holds.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.eq_or_hatRel_downOn_symm
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: The carrier terminal relation of equality or hatRel of DownOn is symmetric.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.DownOn.of_eq_or_hatRel
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If a and b are in A and are equal or hatRel-related for DownOn, then DownOn A R holds.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.DownOn.of_joinStepOn_reach
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If a reaches a prime by JoinStepOn and DownOn holds from the prime to b, then DownOn holds from a to b.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.downOn_iff_join
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: DownOn A R of t and u holds if and only if both are in A and reach members t prime and u prime by JoinStepOn that are equal or hatRel-related for DownOn.

relations.explanation: The global theorem identifies Down with joinability to a symmetric terminal relation using only its six generating clauses.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.down_iff_join

relations.explanation: The carrier theorem is the relativized form requiring every node, endpoint and witness to lie in A.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.downOn_iff_join

relations.explanation: The carrier join step restricts the global step by explicit carrier membership and the relativized invariant.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.JoinStepOn

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.summary: The module restricts non-root parent edges to root contractions or congruences over the graph equality and proves they reverse without changing represented equality. It proves tight one-edge extension, existence of tight equality-maximal graphs by an equality-gap induction, and path-rerooting and repair constructions along root-free reaches. Local signature closure then forces root-step representation and universality on the same maximal tight graph of a strongly almost non-omega-overlapping constructor system.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.boundary: Non-root tight edges reverse without changing represented equality while root edges do not; tight equality-maximality plus local signature closure forces root representation, whereas edge-completeness alone does not.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.conclusion: Every finite coalgebra has a tight equality-maximal graph, and under strong overlap plus local signature closure such a graph represents all root steps and is universal.
assumptions: Coalgebra A for routing and closure results
ConstructorRules R
StronglyAlmostNonOmegaOverlapping R for the strong existence and final root representation
finite coalgebra with eqvGap measure for maximal tight completion
root-free repair needs no tightness premise

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.TightEdge
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: A parent edge is tight when it is a root contraction, a one-layer destructor congruence over the represented equality, or a constructor equality over it.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.TightEdge.mono
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Tightness is monotone in the represented relation: tightness for E implies tightness for any larger E prime.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.TightEdge.toGrey
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Every tight edge for the graph equality is a grey edge of that proof graph.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.TightEdge.symm_of_not_root
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If E is symmetric and a tight edge from a to b is not a root step, then the reverse edge from b to a is tight.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Grey.symm_of_not_root
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If E is symmetric and a grey edge from a to b is not a root step, then the reverse grey edge holds, without any tightness hypothesis.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.Tight
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: A proof graph is tight when every parent edge is a tight edge for its own represented equality.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.constructorCompatible_eqvOn
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra and R has constructor rules, then the graph equality EqvOn A rho.par is constructor-compatible.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.Tight.extend_one
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, R has constructor rules, rho is tight, a and b are in A with a a graph root not already equal to b, and a to b is tight, then there is a tight beta extending all equalities with parent a equals b.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.TightEqualityComplete
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: A graph is tight equality-complete when no tight graph represents a strict superset of its equalities.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.Tight.exists_tightEqualityComplete
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Every tight graph has a tight equality-maximal replacement on the same finite coalgebra, by strong induction on the equality gap.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.exists_tightEqualityComplete
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Every finite coalgebra has a tight equality-maximal proof graph, starting from the empty graph.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.exists_tightEqualityComplete_rootStepsRepresented_of_strong
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra and R is a constructor strongly almost non-omega-overlapping system, then there is a tight equality-maximal graph that already represents every root contraction.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.TightEqualityComplete.eqvOn_of_nf_tightEdge
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, R has constructor rules, rho is tight equality-maximal and tight, a and b are in A with a a graph root, and a to b is tight, then a and b are graph-equal.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.TightNonRootReach
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: A parent path with no root-contraction edge, with refl and head constructors recording the non-root property at each step.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.TightNonRootReach.toReach
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Every tight non-root path is a parent reachability path.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.TightNonRootReach.reversible_without_tightness
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Every root-free parent path is reversibly reachable in every proof graph, with no tightness premise.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.TightNonRootReach.reversible
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: A tight root-free path is reversibly reachable.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.Reach.tightNonRoot_or_firstRoot
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Every finite parent path is either root-free or has a first root-contraction edge after a root-free prefix.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.TightNonRootReach.barReachOn
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: A root-free path from a destructor-headed node stays inside its destructor fiber as a BarReachOn path.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.TightNonRootReach.barRel_eqvOn
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra and rho is tight, then a root-free path from a destructor-headed member carries one destructor congruence over the represented equality.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.Tight.rootRoute
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, R has constructor rules, rho is tight and a has a root step, then either a reaches a graph root by reversible destructor edges with a destructor congruence, or it reaches a first represented root contraction with such a congruence to the blocker.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.Tight.reroot_one
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Reversing one non-root tight parent edge into a graph root preserves tightness and the represented equality, making the source a root.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.Tight.reroot_nonRootReach
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Rerooting an entire tight root-free path to its root preserves tightness and represented equality while leaving edges off the path unchanged.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.Tight.repair_rootStep_along_nonRootReach
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, R has constructor rules, rho is tight, a and b are in A with a missing root step and a root-free route to a graph root, then there is a tight beta preserving old equalities that represents a to b.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.repair_rootStep_along_rootFreeReach
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, R has constructor rules, a and b are in A with a missing root step and a root-free path to a root, then some beta with parent a equals b preserves all old equalities, with no tightness premise.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.EqualityComplete.missing_rootStep_has_first_root_blocker
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, R has constructor rules, rho is equality-maximal, and a to b in A is an unrepresented root step, then a has a root-free prefix to an actual earlier root edge.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.EqualityComplete.missing_rootStep_has_fiber_blocker
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Under the same hypotheses, the blocker of a missing root rewrite lies in the same destructor fiber as the missing source.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.TightEqualityComplete.rootStepsRepresented_of_sigmaClosedOn
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, R is a constructor strongly almost non-omega-overlapping system, rho is tight equality-maximal and tight, and its equality is sigma-closed on A, then every root contraction in A is represented.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.TightEqualityComplete.universal_of_sigmaClosedOn
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Under the same coalgebra, constructor, strong overlap, maximality, tightness and local-closure hypotheses, rho is universal on its carrier.

relations.explanation: Maximal tight local closure is promoted to representation of every root contraction via routing and repair.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.TightEqualityComplete.rootStepsRepresented_of_sigmaClosedOn

relations.explanation: The tight maximal graph instantiates the general root-representation implies universality principle on the same carrier.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.TightEqualityComplete.universal_of_sigmaClosedOn

relations.explanation: Root-free paths are reversible without tightness and therefore support repair in arbitrary graphs.
relations.subject: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.TightNonRootReach.reversible_without_tightness

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.summary: The file defines root-step representation and proves universality is equivalent to root representation plus local signature closure, with variants for bar-closed and complete or equality-complete graphs. It shows a signature-closed nonuniversal graph has an actual unrepresented root step and builds root-only and equality-complete graphs representing all contractions under determinism or strong overlap. It proves root representation plus context absorption identifies the completed relation with DownOn and yields global Down transitivity, conversion characterization and constructor compatibility of conversion.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.boundary: A signature-closed graph is universal exactly when it represents every root step; failure of universality therefore yields a concrete unrepresented root rewrite.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.conclusion: Universality is equivalent to root-step representation plus local signature closure, and finite root-representing context-absorbing models yield global Down transitivity and conversion characterization.
assumptions: Coalgebra A where stated
ConstructorRules R for bar-closed, complete and root-only constructions
Complete, BarClosed and EqualityComplete hypotheses where stated
root determinism or StronglyAlmostNonOmegaOverlapping for the existence constructions
no targeting or completeness for the pure universality equivalence

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.RootStepsRepresented
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: RootStepsRepresented means every root step between members of A is represented by the graph equality EqvOn A rho.par.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.universal_of_rootStepsRepresented
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For any graph, root-step representation together with local signature closure implies universality, by induction on DownOn.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.Universal.rootStepsRepresented
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If rho is universal then every root step in A is represented, via the root clause of DownOn.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.Universal.sigmaClosedOn
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If rho is universal then its graph equality is sigma-closed on A.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.universal_iff_rootStepsRepresented_and_sigmaClosedOn
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: For any graph with no coalgebra, constructor, overlap, targeting or completeness premise, universality holds if and only if root representation and local signature closure both hold.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.Universal.barClosed
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If rho is universal then it is bar-closed for destructor edges.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.Universal.equalityComplete
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If rho is universal then it is equality-complete: every represented pair of an extension is already represented.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.sigmaClosedOn_of_barClosed_complete
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, R has constructor rules, rho is bar-closed and complete, then its equality is sigma-closed on A, with constructor closure from completeness.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.universal_iff_rootStepsRepresented_and_barClosed
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, R has constructor rules and rho is complete, then universality holds if and only if root representation and bar-closure hold.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.universal_iff_rootStepsRepresented_of_barClosed_complete
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, R has constructor rules, and rho is bar-closed and complete, then universality holds if and only if root representation holds.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.EqualityComplete.universal_iff_rootStepsRepresented
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, R has constructor rules, and rho is equality-complete and bar-closed, then universality is equivalent to root representation.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.exists_unrepresented_rootStep_of_not_universal
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If rho is sigma-closed on A but not universal, then there are actual a and b in A with a root step missed by the graph equality.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.RootOnly
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: A graph is root-only when every parent edge is an actual root contraction.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.RootOnly.extend_root
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, R has constructor rules, rho is root-only, a and b are in A with a a graph root not already equal to b and a root step from a to b, then there is a root-only beta preserving old equalities and representing a to b.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.exists_rootOnly_rootStepsRepresented
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, R has constructor rules and root steps are deterministic, then there is a root-only graph representing every contraction, via gap-minimal completion.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.exists_equalityComplete_rootStepsRepresented
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Under the same coalgebra, constructor and determinism hypotheses, there is an equality-complete graph representing every root step.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.exists_rootOnly_rootStepsRepresented_of_strong
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, R has constructor rules and is strongly almost non-omega-overlapping, then the root-only root-representing graph exists.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.exists_equalityComplete_rootStepsRepresented_of_strong
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Under the same coalgebra, constructor and strong overlap hypotheses, an equality-complete root-representing graph exists.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.TermTargetedPGraph.universal_of_rootStepsRepresented
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra, R has constructor rules, rho is targeted with complete graph and its graph represents all root steps, then rho is universal.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.ContextTransitive
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Context transitivity means CT of the graph equality composes for triples inside A.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.ContextAbsorbs
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: Context absorption means one represented equality composes with one application pair of CT equalities inside A.

keyDeclarations.name: OperatorKO7.Meta.UniqueNormalization.PGraph.contextTransitive_iff_contextAbsorbs
keyDeclarations.plain_statement: If A is a coalgebra then context transitivity holds if and only if context absorption holds.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.summary: The file proves that an existing proof-graph parent of a selected target redex must be a root rewrite, since the target-exits-fiber condition excludes destructor-tilde edges and destructor-headedness of a Constructor root redex excludes constructor-tilde edges. It then proves that under root determinism and graph completeness the selected target is graph-equivalent to every root contractum, either by reusing the existing parent or by adding the root edge through completeness. This closes the target-redex sentence used in the source proof of Lemma 64 on the live finite carrier.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.boundary: The target-contractum equality needs root determinism and graph completeness; without them the parent need not be a root rewrite nor equivalent to the chosen contractum.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.conclusion: A selected target redex is graph-equivalent to all its root contracta under determinism and completeness.
assumptions: ConstructorRules R
Coalgebra A for the completeness direction
Deterministic R
Complete graph
carrier memberships
kernel checked with no new axiom

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.summary: This file closes Section 7 on the same proof graph. It defines guided targets, missing root equations, and root-argument witnesses, proves that completeness yields signature closure and hence context absorption, and characterizes universality by root-step representation. Its classification theorem builds one equality-complete guided absorbing targeted graph whose positive case is universal and whose negative case carries an explicit unrepresented root and aligned argument.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.boundary: Universality holds on the same graph exactly when root steps are represented, with context absorption following from completeness; failure of representation yields an explicit unrepresented root rewrite together with an unrepresented aligned argument.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.conclusion: Every finite strong constructor coalgebra has a same-graph equality-complete guided absorbing construction that is either universal with root steps represented or carries a complete root-and-argument obstruction.
assumptions: Coalgebra A
ConstructorRules R
StronglyAlmostNonOmegaOverlapping R
graph Completeness
graph EqualityCompleteness

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.summary: This file builds a six-term counterexample to raw self-grey soundness from the single rule d(x) to c(d(x)). It defines a terminating parent with edges dp to cdp to cdq and dq to cdq, proves constructor shape, strong overlap, root preservation, and that every parent edge is Grey for the parent's own equality. It then shows EqvOn equates cdp and cdq while DownOn separates them because DownOn preserves variable sets, so no proof graph realizes this parent and no sound well-founded support certificate exists.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.boundary: All raw self-grey hypotheses hold, including termination and root preservation, yet the graph equality holds where DownOn fails: EqvOn identifies the constructor pair while preservation of variable sets separates them, so raw self-grey reasoning is unsound.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.conclusion: Raw self-grey soundness fails for a terminating root-preserving strong constructor instance whose parent equates cdp and cdq while DownOn separates them, and no sound well-founded constructor-support certificate exists for that parent.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.summary: This file develops simultaneous closure for proof graphs over the constructor translation. It defines root-occurrence certificates inside Down derivations, missing-root pairs with aligned-argument dependencies, parent-replacement and residual-batch seeds, finite residual saturation, root-peeled seeds, initial attachments, and constructor-decomposition closure. It proves that a missed Down pair contains a missed root step, that missed roots form a total dependency with a representation-or-cycle dichotomy, that residuals saturate finitely and support simultaneous repair, that fresh terms insert with terminating tight graphs, and that replacement forks are sound exactly when no finite constructor clash blocks a compatible ambient.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.boundary: Root rewrites are either all represented or the missing roots contain a dependency cycle. Replacement forks are either sound through a constructor-compatible ambient or blocked by a finite constructor-shape clash.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.conclusion: Every concrete parent replacement in the constructor translation either makes all its semantic forks sound or is blocked by a finite constructor-shape clash in its seed equations.
assumptions: Coalgebra A for finite subterm-closed carriers
ConstructorRules R and constructorRules_constructorTranslation
StronglyAlmostNonOmegaOverlapping R for missing-root totality
NonOmegaOverlapping R and TRS.RhsDetermined R for translated forks
EqualityComplete, TightEqualityComplete and Tight for maximal graphs
SigmaClosedOn for old equalities
Classical choice: open scoped Classical, noncomputable defs, Classical.choose and Classical.choice; no sorry, axiom or native_decide shown

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.summary: The file proves root determinism from finite common generalisations of unifiable rule pairs, and derives it from the strong almost non-omega-overlapping hypothesis without constructor, graph or finite-coalgebra premises. It shows root determinism implies right-hand-side determinism and that the strong condition implies the almost condition. It checks that syntactic equality is constructor-compatible, sigma-closed, and fixed under context closure. It concludes with a targeted-graph rule: under a coalgebra, constructor rules, the strong condition and graph completeness, a selected target root redex is graph-equivalent to each of its root contracta.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.boundary: Root steps are deterministic on the side with finite common generalisations, in particular under the strong overlap condition; without such generalisations root rewriting may diverge. The strong condition removes the usual constructor-shape, finite-carrier and graph premises, marking the limit of what determinism needs.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.conclusion: The strong almost non-omega-overlapping condition yields root determinism over every signature, and a complete targeted graph then equates a selected target root redex with each of its root contracta without a separate determinism premise.
assumptions: finite common generalisations for every unifiable rule pair (for the general theorem)
StronglyAlmostNonOmegaOverlapping R (for the strong corollaries)
Coalgebra A, ConstructorRules R and graph Completeness plus carrier membership and rootStep (for the target-redex theorem)
no sorry, axiom or native_decide visible; kernel checked with no new axiom

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.summary: The file formalizes Section 7 targeting: destructor-fiber steps and their reflexive-transitive reachability, the fiber-representative target with redex priority, and the targeted proof graph with its two source conditions and universality. It proves fiber closure lemmas and the constructor sanity facts that constructor-topped terms have singleton fibers, forcing the target to be the term itself and, under constructor rules, excluding root redexes from the fiber. It bridges the quotient-typed Definitions 58-59 from Lemma52 to term-indexed counterparts via pickAt, ofTarget and toTermTargeted and shows every finite coalgebra carries such a target via the canonical target.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.boundary: Constructor-topped members lie on the singleton-fiber side with forced target and, under constructor rules, no root redex in the fiber; general destructor-topped terms may have larger fibers where target choice and redex priority are nontrivial. Targeting alone does not supply transitivity of DownOn, universality or Lemma 64.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.conclusion: Every finite coalgebra carries a term-indexed Section 7 target obtained from the canonical quotient target, with singleton constructor fibers and redex-priority targeting.
assumptions: carrier membership t in A and u in A and ConTopped t where stated
ConstructorRules R for absence of root redexes in constructor fibers
Classical.choice through canonicalTarget and noncomputable pickAt, ofTarget and toTermTargeted with open scoped Classical
no transitivity of DownOn, universality or Lemma 64 assumed; no sorry, axiom or native_decide visible

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.summary: The file studies tight equality-maximal proof graphs over finite coalgebras. It shows maximal tight graphs are constructor-closed, characterizes signature-closure failure as a missing destructor congruence, and proves that well-founded descent of right-hand-side destructor symbols yields signature closure and universality. From this it derives transitivity of Down, identification of conversion with Down, constructor compatibility, consistency, and certified constructions by constructor slices, one-term context insertion, parent splicing and simultaneous root grafting.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.boundary: With well-founded right-hand-side destructor descent every equality-maximal tight graph is signature-closed, universal and consistent, whereas without that closure signature failure is exactly a missing destructor congruence between members of the coalgebra.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sec.conclusion: Well-founded syntactic right-hand-side destructor descent yields a tight universal proof graph on every finite coalgebra, so conversion equals the Down invariant and is transitive, constructor-compatible and consistent.
assumptions: Coalgebra A for finite carriers and Coalgebra (a :: B) for extensions
ConstructorRules R
StronglyAlmostNonOmegaOverlapping R
WellFounded lt and RhsSymbolsDescend R lt for destructor descent
Tight, TightEqualityComplete and EqualityComplete graphs
Terminating parent functions and Grey edge evidence
classical tactic used in several proofs; no sorry, axiom or native_decide visible in the code

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sem.summary: The file defines parallel reduction with a conversion oracle for semi-equational conditional systems and the hypotheses of left-linearity, variable condition, oracle stability and no feasible overlap. It proves that level-stratified steps coincide with oracle steps and that parallel moves yield confluence without termination. Through transfer it deduces unique normal forms for systems whose hub linearization has no feasible overlap, including syntactic non-overlap and flat-root cases. It instantiates Klop's non-confluent system and an infeasible-overlap system with unique normal forms, and shows Huet and KO7 linearizations retain feasible overlaps.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sem.boundary: Left-linear variable-condition systems are confluent when no overlap has both condition sets convertible, while a feasible overlap can destroy confluence. Unique normal forms lie strictly beyond confluence, since Klop's system has unique normal forms but is not confluent.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sem.conclusion: Left-linear semi-equational systems with the variable condition and no feasible overlap are confluent, giving unique normal forms to original systems with such linearizations even when the original is not confluent.
assumptions: CLeftLinear left-linearity
CVarCondition variable condition
NoFeasibleOverlap for cconv oracle
OracleStable for semi-equational oracle
Nat variables and finite rule list for hub results
Classical.choose for image targets in parallel moves
no sorry axiom native_decide partial unsafe opaque per header

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sig.summary: The file builds the extended signature with a constant for each variable and a fresh symbol F, with freezing and unfreezing maps and the two F-rules forming system U. It proves frozen normal forms stay normal, frozen conversion lifts, distinct-variable identification, preservation of non-omega-overlap and the variable condition. From Theorem 68 quantified over the extended signature it proves Theorem 69, and with Down-transitivity as the only hypothesis it proves the Section 7 summit for conversion and reduction.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sig.boundary: A non-omega-overlapping system meeting the variable condition has consistent equational theory and unique normal forms, while two distinct convertible normal forms make the F-extension identify distinct variables and hence inconsistent.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sig.conclusion: RTA open problem 79 follows from Section 7 Down-transitivity alone, with all extension and Theorem 69 steps machine-checked.
assumptions: Nontrivial or Infinite variable supply
NonOmegaOverlapping hypothesis on R
TRS.RhsDetermined variable condition
Down-transitivity on constructor translations as Section 7 hypothesis

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sum.summary: The file shows the constructor translation is a Constructor TRS and that Down is contained in conversion, with the reverse inclusion exactly under transitivity. OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sum.boundary: When Down on the constructor translation is transitive then conversion coincides with Down and is constructor-compatible, while without transitivity the coincidence and the reduction to unique normal forms fail.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Sum.conclusion: Pre-extension RTA open problem 79 follows from Section 7 Down-transitivity together with same-signature class membership for the auxiliary extensions.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Ter.summary: The file defines symbol relabelling and variable renaming with list companions, functoriality, commutation with substitution and injectivity of injective renamings. It defines recursive arity correctness and ranked terms with lifted maps commuting with substitution. It characterizes arity preservation by probes and all terms, and gives a counterexample that list-length preservation does not imply arity preservation.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Ter.boundary: Arity-preserving symbol maps preserve and reflect well-formedness, while mere argument-list length preservation does not imply the arity law.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/Ter.conclusion: Symbol and variable maps behave functorially with substitution and arity, except that list-length preservation alone does not force arity preservation.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/The.summary: The file defines strongly almost non-omega-overlapping systems and consistency invariants with the destructor-tilde amendment. It proves that a term with constructor-only instance is constructor-only. It proves Theorem 37 that semantical critical pairs land in CT via Corollary 35, Lemma 36 and common generalisation, and Corollary 45 that Down is a consistency invariant.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/The.boundary: Semantical critical pairs stay inside CT of the equivalence under strongly almost non-omega-overlap, while without root-only overlaps and a common generalisation the containment can fail.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/The.conclusion: In a strongly almost non-omega-overlapping Constructor TRS, Down is a consistency invariant.

OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/The.summary: The file defines the two F-extension rules and the extended system U with same-signature freshness as SymbolAbsent. It proves U-steps on fresh-free terms are old steps, normal forms survive, and the extension identifies the chosen variables hence is inconsistent for distinct convertible normal forms. It reduces UN to consistency plus class membership, and gives a one-rule counterexample where an open normal form omega-unifies so the unfrozen extension leaves the class, showing freezing is required.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/The.boundary: With freezing into constants the extension can stay non-omega-overlapping, while the fresh symbol alone does not preserve the class for open normal forms. Distinct convertible normal forms make the extension identify distinct variables and hence inconsistent.
OperatorKO7/Meta/UniqueNormalization/The.conclusion: Unique normal forms follow from consistency of the class plus class membership of the extensions, and freezing is necessary as shown by the counterexample.
assumptions: two distinct variables x y with x not equal y
conversion between the two normal forms
Theorem 68 consistency for systems in the class
class membership of each extension with variable condition
SymbolAbsent freshness for normal-form preservation
no sorry axiom native_decide partial unsafe opaque per header
